Business Requirement 
Cross Border Limit Management <B2-001-1>, <B2-003-1>
In CTBC, an external system called “Global Instance” (also known as “Global Limit” or “GI”) is used to manage customer cross-country risks. The limit Id in GBP must be linked to the limit ID in GI and any transaction related to the limit ID must be approved in GI before processing in GBP. So, it is a 2-stage process. 
Additionally, collateral records in GBP must also support linkage to GI. 
Setup: Mapping between GI and GBP Limits and Collaterals:
The total limit for risk management between countries will be set up in GI. So, this action will be triggered by GI. 
A new API will be required to create the linkage between the limit in GI and the limit id of GBP (CBS Transaction # 61000). Linkage is also required with Collateral records. The collateral-related steps will be discussed in B2-013-17. 
This linkage record must be maintained in a local table in GBP. (In CBS, the table used is FCLM). 
Below information must be captured in the table:

Audit log must be maintained for the linkage table. 
Note that exposure limits and secondary limits / shared limits will not be linked to GI. 
Based on the agreed approach between TCS and CTBC, the messaging with GI will be managed by an external system. To meet the messaging requirements of GI, additional information below must also be stored, along with the linkage information.

Utilization Update Process in Limits for GBP 
When any transaction is performed in GBP that involves utilization update of a limit ID that is linked to GI, approval must be first obtained from GI before processing the transaction in GBP. This includes transactions like loan disbursement as well as trade module transactions. 
Below is how a loan disbursement transaction is currently performed in the legacy CBS system. 
Step 1: (CBS)
While performing the transaction, the system will do the funds availability check on the linked limit id and validates whether the limit or one of its parent nodes is “GI related”. 
If not, the process will continue within the system using existing process.
If yes, the below process will be followed. 
Step 2: (CBS)
When teller performs a loan disbursement transaction, the limit id that is linked to GI will return a specific error code with text like “GI Related – please wait and try later”. 
Step 3: (UI / CBS)
Based on this response from host, the front end / UI fires a transaction (CBS transaction # 61028) that will send a message via MQ to ESB. 
Currently CTBC will send a message via MQ to ESB (then forward to GI) in this transaction, the message includes real-time utilized amount between level-1 to level-4. 
Step 4: (ESB)
When ESB gets the message from CBS, it will get forwarded to GI for approval. 
ESB will also fire a transaction (CBS transaction # 61027) to CBS.

Step 8: (CBS)
Teller re-attempts the disbursement transaction. 
If step-5 response is not yet received, users will get the same response as that of step-2 as FCLU record is not found. 
The result code from GI is still “pending” (and “manual operation” is blank), they will get an error. 
When “Result code from GI” is “Error” (and “manual operation” is blank), return error to user. 
When “Result code from GI” is “Excess Occupation” (and “manual operation” is blank), return error to user. 
When “Result code from GI” is “Successful” (and “manual operation” is blank), no error returned, and the transaction must be processed.

The list of records will be returned (CBS transaction # 61022). 
Users can select one record to update the “manual operation” attribute of the record (CBS transaction # 61023). 
If the result code from GI is “Pending” but the disbursement must be done immediately, teller will update the “manual operation” to “GI Skipped” and perform the disbursement transaction again, bypassing the GI validation. 
If the result code from GI is “Error” but disbursement must be done, teller will update the “manual operation” to “GI Skipped” and perform the disbursement transaction again, bypassing the GI validation.
If the result code is “Excess Occupation”, it means this disbursement is required to be approved manually. Tellers will update the “manual operation” to “Approval” and perform the disbursement transaction again, bypassing the GI validation. 
If the result code is “Excess Occupation” or “Successful”, but for some reason the teller decides not to do the disbursement, “manual operation” must be set as “Canceled”, and this record will also be updated as “Closed”. It means this disbursement is no longer allowed.
Inquiry for listing out “Closed” status records must also be available (CBS transaction # 61024).

Step-5: (GI)

The result code could be one of the below.

If the result of GBP is successful but the result of GI is failed, tellers will manually perform a transaction to send the ‘02-Reversal of Limit Occupation’ to reduce utilization in GBP.

Utilization Update Process
#1.4 Enhancement to Limit Utilization Update API
When the limit utilization update API is invoked during transactions like loan disbursement or trade transactions or from KF, after performing the existing standard validations, the system must also check whether the limit to be updated has an active linkage to GI limit or not, in the linkage table. 
If there is no linkage, then there is no change in the existing GBP process. 
If there is a linkage, it means that an interaction process with GI must be triggered. Here again, there can be two cases. 
Case 1: The interaction with GI has not been initiated for the day.
In this case, there is no record in the GI Transaction Table for the account reference with “transaction date” = current system date. Note that records with transaction date <> current system date are not to be considered. 
A new interaction record must be created in a GI transaction table created for this purpose using the “Create GI Transaction Record” API described in later sections. 
After creating the GI transaction record,
If invoked from GBP, and the limit utilization is to be increased, an error must be returned stating that it’s a GI related limit and the user must wait and try again later. Limit utilization update must not happen in this case. 
If invoked from other systems like KF, when limit utilization is to be increased, no error must be returned. Limit utilization must happen. The API output must also publish an additional attribute to indicate to KF/external system that it’s a GI linked limit id. 
For limit utilization = decrease cases, limit utilization update must happen in all cases. 
Case 2: Interaction with GI has already been initiated for the day. 
In this case, there is already a record in the GI transaction table for the account reference for the day. 
When invoked from KF/system other than GBP, a new record must be written in the GI transaction table using the ‘Create GI Transaction Record’ API, as the previous record will be in ‘closed’ status. Utilization update must happen, same as in case 1. 
When invoked from GBP and the limit utilization is to be decreased, a new record must be written in the GI transaction table as the previous record will be in ‘closed’ status. Utilization update must happen, same as in case 1.
When invoked from GBP and the limit utilization is to be increased, there can be multiple responses as below. 
When the existing record status is ‘closed’, a new record must be written. Like in Case 1, utilization update must not happen, and the error must be returned. 
When the record status is ‘open’ and the ‘result code’ is ‘successful’, utilization update must happen. The status of the record must be changed to ‘closed’ using the ‘Close GI Transaction Record’ API. 
When the record status is ‘open’ and the ‘result code’ is ‘pending’, and ‘manual operation’ is ‘GI Skipped’, the utilization update must happen. The status of the record must be changed to ‘closed’ using the ‘Close GI Transaction Record’ API. 
When the record status is ‘open’ and the ‘result code’ is ‘error’, and ‘manual operation’ is ‘GI Skipped’, utilization update must happen. The status of the record must be changed to ‘closed’ using the ‘Close GI Transaction Record’ API. 
When the record status is ‘open’ and the ‘result code’ is ‘excess occupation’, and ‘manual operation’ is ‘Approval’, utilization update must happen. The status of the record must be changed to ‘closed’ using the ‘Close GI Transaction Record’ API. 
When the record status is ‘open’ and the ‘result code’ is ‘pending’, error must be returned. Utilization update must not happen in this case. Users can wait for the GI ‘result code’ to be updated via the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record’ API and then try again. Else, users must invoke the ‘Enquire GI Transaction Records’ API to search for the record and then trigger the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record manual operation’ to update the ‘manual operation’ attribute value to ‘GI Skipped’ and then reattempt the limit utilization update transaction. 
When the record status is ‘open’ and the ‘result code’ is ‘error’ and the ‘manual operation’ is spaces, error must be returned. Utilization update must not happen in this case. Users must invoke the ‘Enquire GI Transaction Records’ API to search for the record and then trigger the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record manual operation’ to update the ‘manual operation’ attribute value to ‘GI Skipped’ and then reattempt the limit utilization update transaction. 
When the record status is ‘open’ and the ‘result code’ is ‘excess occupation’ and the ‘manual operation’ is spaces, error must be returned. Utilization update must not happen in this case. Users must invoke the ‘Enquire GI Transaction Records’ API to search for the record and then trigger the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record manual operation’ to update the ‘manual operation’ attribute value to ‘Approval’ and then reattempt the limit utilization update transaction.

#2 Return Limit ID for fund check failures <B2-001-3> and <B2-006-3>
During the limit utilization update process, if there is insufficient available limit to accommodate the transaction amount, along with the error message, the system must also return the limit ID and limit type. 
The limit utilization update API (LMM-25: Limit utilization Update) must be enhanced to meet this requirement. 
If the “Limit Type” = “Credit Limit”, the response message must include the limit id. For example, “Insufficient Limit Availability at Limit ID <123>”. 
If the “Limit Type” = “Exposure Limit”, there must be an additional indicator for the type of limit as well. For example, “Insufficient Limit Availability at Exposure Limit ID <123>”.
If the “Limit Type” = “Shared Limit”, there must be an additional indicator for the type of limit as well. For example, “Insufficient Limit Availability at Shared Limit ID <123>”.
Note that in a transaction like say loan disbursement, there could be multiple credit limits involved plus shared limits and exposure limits. When an error is encountered in a limit id, the system will stop and return the error and not validate the remaining limit ids involved. 
For example, assume that loan account 10001 is linked to limit id 1234 and it has a parent limit id 1230. If during loan account disbursement, there is insufficient limit availability at 1234, the processing will stop, and the error will be returned to the user. Availability at limit id 1230 will not be validated.

Processing Logic:
The status of the limit must be “Active” or “Utilized”. Else, an error must be returned to the user. The other output fields must not be populated. 
If the annual review date is invalid (B2-002), the system must return an error to the user. The other output fields must not be populated.
Next is the amount-based validation using the input disbursement amount converted into the currency of the limit. 
For limit ids where ‘limit valuation’ is set as ‘limit amount’. 
Validate whether there is sufficient limit availability to accommodate the disbursement amount. 
If yes, return a success. 
If no, return an error stating “Insufficient Limit”. 
Calculate the ‘utilized amount’ and ‘available amount’ in both cases after adding the disbursement amount in limit currency. 
For limit ids where the ‘limit valuation’ is set as ‘lower of two’. 
First validate whether there is sufficient availability based on the limit amount and current utilization. This is done first as if this fails, no amount of collateral addition is going to help. 
If no, return an error stating “Insufficient Limit”. Calculate the ‘utilized amount’ and ‘available amount’ using the limit amount and not the effective limit amount.
If yes, validate for availability using the effective limit amount and current utilization. In this case, a revised effective limit will have to be calculated if there is a non-zero input in the ‘increased collateral value’ field. Calculation details are in the next section. 
If there is sufficient availability, return a success. Calculate the ‘utilized amount’ and ‘available amount’ using the revised effective limit amount. 
If there is insufficient availability, return an error stating “Insufficient Collateral”. Calculate the ‘utilized amount’ and ‘available amount’ using the revised effective limit amount. Also calculate the ‘collateral value needed’ as it must be returned in the response. Calculation logic is detailed in the next section.  
For limit ids where the ‘limit valuation’ set as ‘collateral amount’. 
Validate for availability using the effective limit amount and current utilization. In this case, a revised effective limit will have to be calculated if there is a non-zero input in the ‘increased collateral value’ field. Calculation details are in the next section. 
If there is sufficient availability, return a success. Calculate the ‘utilized amount’ and ‘available amount’ using the revised effective limit amount. 
If there is insufficient availability, return an error stating “Insufficient Collateral”. Calculate the ‘utilized amount’ and ‘available amount’ using the revised effective limit amount. Also calculate the ‘collateral value needed’ as it must be returned in the response. Calculation logic is detailed in the next section.  
In the API response, the ‘utilized amount’ and ‘available amount’ calculated at each level must be returned for both success and failure responses. 
If the failure is only due to ‘Insufficient Limit’ reason, that is the response that must be returned in the API. 
Additionally, the system must also validate linkages to shared limits for each node. 
If there is linkage to one/multiple shared limits, the “shared limit connected” field must return a “Yes” response for that node. 
The available amount for each linked shared limit must be calculated after reducing the input amount. If there are multiple shared limits linked, the lowest value of available limit must be returned in the “minimum availability at shared limit” field. 
If there is insufficient availability at shared limit, then an error “Insufficient Shared Limit” must be returned along with the shared limit ID. Note that if there are multiple shared limits with insufficient limit, then the first limit id linked to the lowest level node must be picked up. For example, assume that shared limit id 125 and 120 are linked to limit level 4 and limit level 3 respectively and both have insufficient limit availability. So the error message must return limit id 125 as its linked to the lowest level (level 4) in the example.
If the failure is due to “insufficient limit” in some nodes but there is also an “insufficient collateral” in other nodes and “insufficient shared limit”, the overall API response error message must be “insufficient collateral” with the calculated ‘collateral value needed’ also returned in the response. 
Calculation of Effective Limit with collateral linkage
Step 1: Divide the “increased collateral value” that has come in the input with the Requisition Ratio or LTV ratio percentage that is applicable for the limit. 
Step 2: Convert the value of Step 1 in to limit currency. 
Step 3: Add the value of step 2 to the current effective limit amount to arrive at the new effective limit. 
Calculation of Collateral Value Needed
Step 1: Take the shortage amount (negative available amount) and multiply it with the Requisition ratio or LTV ratio percentage. 
Step 2: Convert the value of Step 1 into the collateral currency (part of API input). 
Step 3: Roundup to zero decimals and add the value to the input “increased collateral value” that came as input, if any.

GI Linkage Processing:
If the internal GBP validations are okay and the limit tree/chain has sufficient available limit to process the transaction, the system must additionally check if any of the impacted limit ids is actively linked to GI in the GI linkage table. If not, there is no additional processing, and the response can be given back. 
If yes, a process similar to what was covered in B2-001-1 must be followed. 
If simulation is attempted for the first time for the day for the limit id, an error must be returned to the user stating “GI Related Limit. Please wait and try later”. Note that the utilized amount and available amount calculated for the limit ids must also be returned in the response. 
Using the ‘Create GI Transaction Record’ API, a new record must be written in to the GI transaction table (equivalent to FCLU in CBS) with “Account Reference” = Limit ID on which GI is linked and “Transaction Code” as an internal business event number indicating ‘simulation’, something like ‘0000’. The status of the record must be ‘Open’. “Result Code” will be “Pending” and “Request Type” will be “Increase”. 
The communication with GI will be handled by the external system / ESB. 
If user tries simulation on the limit id again with the result code in pending status, error will be returned to users. To perform simulation without waiting for response from GI, users must invoke the ‘Modify GI transaction record manual operation’ API to set the attribute as “GI Skipped” and then do the simulation again.
The result code from GI will be updated by the external system using the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record’ API.
If the result code is “successful”, users can do the simulation again for the limit id and give the output from GBP. 
If the result code is “excess occupation”, users need to invoke the Modify GI transaction record manual operation’ API to set the attribute as “Approval” and then do the simulation again to get a successful response. If the manual operation attribute is not updated, error will be returned in the response.  
If the result code is “error”, users need to invoke the Modify GI transaction record manual operation’ API to set the attribute as “GI Skipped” and then do the simulation again to get a successful response. If the manual operation attribute is not updated, error will be returned in the response.
After simulation, the status of the record must be updated to ‘closed’ by triggering the API to close the record. If the status is not closed, a second simulation cannot be done for the same limit id again that day. 
Simulation for Limit Release Cases
If the disbursement amount is given as a negative value, it must be treated as a simulation for reducing utilization from the entire limit chain, starting from the lowest level.  
The utilization amounts must be increased by the negative amount input, which will result in the reduction of utilization, across the board. 
If there is a GI linkage for any limit id, it must be treated like limit utilization = decrease cases, covered in B2-001-1 of this FSD.

CTBC will define 5 levels in a limit tree structure from top to bottom, as given below. 
1st level (1G): Group
2nd level (2S): Child Group (Subgroup)

4th level (4F): like table FACM in CBS

Auto Limit Amounts <B2-002-1><B2-004-1>
When creating a limit / facility, users have a choice of not inputting the required limit amount. The limit must be derived by the system based on the limit amounts on linked child limits. 
In legacy CBS, the functionality is available at levels 1G, 2S and 3C. 
A new field – “Input Type of Limit Amount” – must be added at the limit level with options as below. 
Manual: User must input a limit amount > 0. 
Auto: User will leave the limit amount blank. In such cases:
Limit amount should increase when child (or grandchild) node is created. 
Limit amount should decrease when child (or grandchild) node is closed. 
Limit amount must be recalculated when child (or grandchild) node’s limit amount or exchange rate is modified. 
The limit amount must be recalculated if users change the field value from “Manual” to “Auto”. 
A new field (Exchange rate on approved date) will be added at limit level for cross currency conversion between child and parent node – please refer B2-002-3.  This will be used to calculate the limit amount in case the currencies are different between parent and child limits.

Note on ‘first drawdown expiry date’:
In CBS, CTBC uses a field ‘Advance counter’ to identify whether this is a first drawdown transaction or not.
Any occupation from loan/trade/external system, below validation is applicable.
1.  If ‘Advance counter’ is equal to 0, then validation of ‘first drawdown expiry date’ is required.
2.  If ‘Advance counter’ is more than 0, then no more validation of ‘first drawdown expiry date’ is required.  Add 1 to ‘Advance counter’
Once the ‘approved date’ is modified manually as part of the limit renewal process, then ‘advance counter’ will be reset as 0. The drawdown after this process will again be treated as the first drawdown transaction and will be subject to the validation of ‘first drawdown expiry date’.

Promissory Notes <B2-002-14>
CTBC maintains promissory notes as inventory in legacy CBS and the same must be supported in GBP. Each promissory note is assigned a user input “Inventory Reference” number. 
Each such inventoried promissory note is assigned an amount, start + end dates and linked to the loans / limits of a customer. 
A unique reference number, “Promissory Note Reference”, must be system generated for each record created. 
Multiple entities can be linked to each promissory note. 
Each entity can be linked to multiple promissory notes. 
CTBC also takes stock of inventory once a month for all the promissory notes. It will be performed by each branch.

When ‘input type of limit amount’ is set as ‘Manual’, the existing process of user input of the limit amounts – intraday, overnight, effective intraday, effective overnight – will continue. 
Input type of limit amount can be set to ‘Auto’ irrespective of the currency of the limit ID. 
When ‘input type of limit amount’ is set to ‘Auto’, then the limit amounts must not be taken as input in the API. It must be calculated by adding up the limit amounts of the linked child limits. 
Note that ‘Auto’ can be setup only when limit level is “1”, “2” or “3”. For other levels, if setup, an error must be returned. 
If the child and parent are in different currencies, the ‘exchange rate as on approved date’ must be used to convert the child limit amount in to the parent limit’s currency. If both are in the same currency, the exchange rate will be set as “1”. 
When the limit is created, there will be no child limit linked to the limit and so, the limit amount will be zero to begin with, when the ‘input type of limit amount’ is ‘Auto’. 
As and when child limits are created under a parent, the system must check if any of the parent limit id in the chain is set up with ‘input type of limit amount’ = ‘Auto’. If yes, the limit amount of the child must be added to the parent limit id. Note that if the parent’s parent is also setup to have auto limit, then its limit must also be recalculated and updated. Same process for the parent’s grandparent. 
Note that an ‘auto’ limit’s limit amount must never exceed its parent limit amount if the parent is set to ‘manual’. The standard limit tree validation will be applicable in this scenario and an error will be returned.

Business Requirement 
Parent Limit Reference Change <B2-005-2>
For an existing limit id in GBP, the system must support changing the parent limit id. A new API must be developed to support this functionality. 
Change can involve the following.
Remove the parent limit id.
Replace the parent limit id with another limit id. 
Add a parent limit id to a standalone limit id. 
For the limit id being removed as the parent, a reduction in utilization must happen – not just for the limit id but for its parent chain as well. 
For the limit id being added as parent, an increase in utilization must happen – not just for the limit id but for its parent chain as well. 
Note that there must be sufficient availability on the parent and its parent chain to accommodate the newly added child limit id. Else, a supervisory override error must be returned if the transaction is from the branch channel. If it is from SI/batch, the utilization update must be force posted. 
The above processing is to be done on any linked shared limits as well. 
The parent and child limit ids may be of different currencies. 
The change in parent limit id must be allowed for limit ids in any status, including cancelled and closed. 
Also note that the customization covered in B2-002-1 must be handled, where the limit amount is automatically recalculated based on the limit of the child limit ids. 
For example, let us consider a limit tree structure as below.

Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-005 
Existing Functionality 
GBP Supports modifying various attributes of a Limit Id using the below APIs. Change in parent is not supported and must be customized to meet CTBC requirements. 
#
Object Reference
API Name
API URI
1
Limit Management
LMM 11: Modify Limit details
PUT /limit
The above list is as per the current API catalogue which will get further enhanced basis the updated catalogues.
Proposed Solution
A new API – Change Parent Limit - is required to be developed in GBP to support the below functions:
Add a parent limit id on a standalone limit id.
Remove the linked parent limit id.
Replace the parent limit id on a child limit with another limit id. 
The inputs required are as below. 
Sl.No.
Attribute Name
Description
O/M
Data Type
1
Limit ID
Limit ID on whom the parent limit is being added /removed / replaced. 
M
Varchar2 (20)
2
Parent Limit ID
The limit id to be added or removed or replaced with
M
Varchar2 (20)
3
Service Flag
Indicates the action to be performed: 
Add
Delete
Replace
A new domain “d_LmtParentSerFlg” must be defined.
O
Varchar2(1)
When a limit id must be added to a stand-alone limit id as a parent, the parent limit id must be input and the service flag must be kept as ‘Add’. 
When the parent limit id must be removed from a child to make it a stand-alone limit, the existing parent limit id must be input and the service flag must be kept as ‘Delete’, to remove the linkage. 
When the current parent limit id must be replaced with a new parent limit id, the new parent limit id must be taken as input and the service flag must be kept as ‘Replace’ to delete the old parent and add the new parent. 
Validations
When adding a child limit ID, 
The parent limit id’s expiry date must be equal to or later than that of the child. 
If the API is fired from SI/Batch, this validation must be bypassed, and it must be allowed.  
From the branch channel, a supervisor over-ride error must be returned to users. 
The parent limit id’s limit amount must be equal to or higher than that of the child. 
If the child is getting added at level 5 and the parent at level 4 has a ‘facility code’ or ‘CPS’s facility code’ input, the ‘keyword’ of the child limit must be one of the parameterized keywords linked to the facility code. Please refer to NVBK_B2-002 FSD section 3.1.2, topics #2 and #3. 
When adding to a new parent, the parent limit id and its parent chain must have sufficient available limit to accommodate the child limit’s utilization. (Note that child limit amount becomes the utilization amount to be updated in case the child is a ‘static’ limit). 
If the API is fired from SI/Batch, this validation must be bypassed, and excess utilization must be allowed.  
From the branch channel, a supervisor over-ride error must be returned to users. 
Note that the child limit may be of a different currency with respect to that of the parent limit or its parent chain. In such cases, the validation must happen after converting the child limit amount and utilization to the required parent currencies using the applicable exchange rate configured.  
The new parent limit id being added must be at a level that is one step above. For example, if the child limit is at level 4, the parent must be at level 3. 
If the parent or its parent chain is linked to a shared limit, the shared limit is expected to have sufficient availability to accommodate the new child utilization. (Note that child limit amount becomes the utilization amount to be updated in case the child is a ‘static’ limit). But this validation is channel specific, as below.  
If the API is fired from SI/Batch, the validation must be bypassed, and excess utilization if any, must be allowed.  
If the API is fired from the branch channel, a supervisor override error must be returned to users. 
There are no validations based on limit status of the child – it must support change even in closed or cancelled statuses. But the parent limit must be in ‘Active’ status. 
Processing logic
Adding a Parent limit ID
The child limit must be added to the limit hierarchy of the parent. 
When the nature of child limit is ‘dynamic’, the child limit utilization must be added to the parent limit utilization and to all other nodes in the parent chain. 
When the nature of child limit is ‘static’, the child limit amount must be added to the parent limit utilization and to all other nodes in the parent chain. 
If any node in the parent chain is linked to a shared limit, the child limit utilization/amount must be added to the shared limit utilization as well. 
When the limits are of different currencies, the conversion must happen based on the applicable exchange rate.
Removing a Parent Limit ID
When removing a parent limit id from a child, the utilized amount on the child limit must be reduced from the parent limit utilization and all nodes in its parent chain. This is when the nature of the child limit is ‘dynamic’. For static child limits, the child limit amount must be reduced from the utilization amount of the parent and all nodes in the parent chain. 
If the parent or any limit id in the parent chain is linked to a shared limit, the utilization of the shared limit must also be reduced by the utilization/limit amount of the child limit being removed from the chain. 
When the limits are of different currencies, the conversion must happen based on the applicable exchange rate.
Replacement of Parent Limit ID 
Replacement is a removal and add. Removal must be processed first so that the utilizations are reduced and then the addition must happen. 
Example 1: Assume a 5-level limit structure as below (all linkages are not shown). 
A standalone limit ID 5008 is being added as a child of Limit ID 4001. 
Since limit ID 4001 and its parent limit IDs 3001, 2001 and 1001 and the shared limit ID 8001 have limit amounts and availability higher than that of limit ID 5008, the linkage will happen successfully, and utilization update will happen throughout the chain and in the shared limit. 
After Linkage:
Example 2: Assume a 5-level limit structure as below (all linkages are not shown). 
A standalone limit ID 5008 of USD 15,000 is being added as a child of Limit ID 4001. 
Assuming mid-rate as 32. 
TWD equivalent of limit ID 5008
Limit Amount = 15,000 x 32 = 480,000
Utilization = 15,000 x 32 = 480,000
Even though the parent limit ID has 500,000 TWD limit amount which can fit in the 480,000 child limit, it does not have sufficient available amount to accommodate the child utilization. The linkage thus will be allowed from branch channel only with supervisor override.  
After linkage: There is excess utilization at the parent limit ID and at the shared limit. 
Example 3: Assume a 5-level limit structure as below (all linkages are not shown). 
Limit ID 4001 is being removed as the parent of limit ID 5002. The utilization of the child ID being removed must be reduced from the parent limit chain as well as the shared limit involved. 
After Delink: 5002 becomes a standalone limit id and its utilization is reduced from the tree. 
Example 4: Assume a 5-level limit structure as below (all linkages are not shown). 
The parent limit ID of 5003 is being changed from 4002 to 4001. 
After the parent ID replacement, the utilizations of linked limit IDs are updated. 
Example 5: Assume a 5-level limit structure as below (all linkages are not shown). 
Limit IDs 3001 and 4001 are ‘Auto’ limits, where the limit amounts are the sum of the linked child limits. 
A standalone limit ID 5008 is being added as a child of Limit ID 4001. 
Since limit ID 4001 and its parent limit IDs 3001, 2001 and 1001 and the shared limit ID 8001 have limit amounts and availability higher than that of limit ID 5008, the linkage will happen successfully, and utilization update will happen throughout the chain and in the shared limit. 
The limit amounts of the two auto limits – 4001 and 3001 – will also be recalculated. 
After linkage: utilization update throughout the parent chain and limit change for 4001 and 3001. 
Key Changes
New API to add / remove / replace the parent limit ID on a limit ID. A new method / task to be developed to check the parent limit utilization while adding a new child to the limit tree.

Business Requirement 
Internal Limit Validation Skip <B2-007-1>
Sensitive Customers are also known as ‘Interested Party’. The Internal Limit Management for Sensitive Customers is already covered under Taiwan localization requirements in GBP. 
Below additional changes are expected by CTBC. 
At the limit level, a new field – “No Internal Limit Check till Date” – has been introduced as part of B2-002-3 at level 4 in FSD NVBK_B2-002. 
When a transaction is being performed that occupies/utilizes the limit
If the system date = < ‘No internal limit check till date’ field and the customer is a ‘Sensitive Customer’, the Customer must be treated as a ‘non sensitive customer’ and validated against the non-sensitive limits. 
If the date is not captured or system date > ‘no internal limit check till date’ field, the sensitive customer limits must be validated, as per the localization requirements. 
The rest of the process remains unchanged. 
    For example:
    When performing loan disbursement and customer is a Sensitive Customer: 
    Case 1: This account is not linked to any limit ID.
Validate as sensitive customer.
Case 2: Account is linked to a limit ID where “No internal limit check till date” = Sep-20-2024
Case 2-1: System date = Aug-01-2024 
Validate as non-sensitive customer.
Case 2-2: System date = Sep-20-2024
Validate as non-sensitive customer.
Case 2-3: System date = Oct-01-2024 
Perform validation as sensitive customer.

Proposed Solution
The field – “No internal limit check till date” has been added to limits as part of B2-002-3 in FSD NVBK_B2-002.
When the customer is a ‘Sensitive’ Customer and when a transaction (from loans, trade, external systems etc.) involves increasing the limit’s utilization and system date is equal to or less than the value set in “no internal limit check till date” field on the limit id, the customer must be treated as a ‘Non-Sensitive’ Customer and validated against non-sensitive customer limits in the Internal Limit Control setup. 
The rest of the process remains the same. Validations and error handling for any failures are already covered in localization.   
Note that this is applicable for Credit Limits as well as Exposure limits. 
For example, assume that disbursement transaction is being performed on a loan account where the customer is a sensitive customer.  
‘No internal limit check till date’ is set as ’30 Apr 2024.’ 
Case 1: System date = 23 Apr 2024
In this case, when the loan disbursement is performed, all internal limit control validations must be done assuming that the customer is a non-sensitive customer.  
Case 2: System date = 30 Apr 2024
Same as case 1. System date = No internal limit check till date. 
Case 3: System date = 1 May 2024
In this case, the customer will be validated and processed as a Sensitive Customer. 
Key Changes
Sensitive Customers must be treated as a Non-Sensitive Customer when the value in the ‘no internal limit check till date’ field at limit id level is greater than or equal to system date.

#1: Additional Information in Limit Prebooking <B2-008-2> and <B2-008-3>.

#2: Internal Limit Control for Exposure Limits <B2-008-6>. 
Sensitive customers are also known as ‘Interested Party’. 
When limit utilization is to be updated for Exposure Limits as part of any transaction, Internal Limit Control validation must be performed for the exposure limit owner/customer as well. 
The “Secured Flag” on the exposure limit ID level (added as part of B2-002-3 in FSD NVBK_B2-002) must be used to determine whether it’s an unsecured or secured limit. 
For example, if the customer is a sensitive customer + corporate and the exposure limit id has the ‘secured flag’ set as ‘secured’, then the maximum exposure must be limited to ‘10%’ (localization parameter) of the Bank’s net worth. 
If the customer is a sensitive customer + corporate and the exposure limit id has the ‘secured flag’ set as ‘unsecured’, the update must fail as unsecured limits are not allowed for sensitive corporates (localization parameter). 
If the customer is flagged as ‘Public Services’, the maximum exposure must be limited to 100% (localization parameter) of the Bank’s net worth. 
If the customer is a sensitive customer, then the ‘All Sensitive Customers’ utilized amount must also be validated to be within 150% (localization parameter) of the Bank’s net worth. 
Any validation failure must return the standard error as response (localization). 
As covered in localization, if the ‘Legal Utilization Exemption’ is set as ‘Y’, then the validation can be bypassed. 
As covered in B2-007-1 of NVBK_B2-007 FSD, if the ‘No Internal Limit Check till Date’ on the exposure limit is > system date, the customer, even if flagged as a sensitive customer, must be treated as a non-sensitive customer. 
#3: GI Related Limit Prebooking <B2-008-7> and <B2-008-8>
Linkage of GI to limit nodes in GBP and handling of limit utilization update when GI is linked is covered in detail in B2-001-1 in NVBK_B2-001 FSD. 
A similar process needs to be done when prebooking / fund hold is created, modified, or deleted on limits which are linked to GI or any node in its parent chain is linked. After all internal validations are successful, GI related handling must be done. 
Note that all details and validations are not being repeated here as the full process is already detailed in the NVBK_B2-001 FSD. 
#3.1: Creation of Prebooking: from GBP
When prebooking/fund hold is being created on the lowest node in the limit tree, after internal validations are successful, the system must check if the limit id or any limit id in its parent chain has an active linkage to GI or not. This will be an enhancement on the ‘Create Fund Hold’ API. 
If yes, additional processing as below must be performed. 
If not, there is no GI related processing and the prebooking can be committed. 
Assuming it’s the first prebooking on the limit for the day, a new record must be written in the GI transaction table (FCLU equivalent of CBS) with the ‘account reference’ as the level 5 limit id on which prebooking is being performed. The record status will be ‘open’ and the ‘result code’ will be ‘pending’. The ‘business event’ used must indicate that it’s a fund hold transaction. The ‘Create GI Transaction Record’ API discussed in B2-001 -1 must be enhanced to support this. 
For example, assume that prebooking is being performed on 3 May on a limit id 1001 for TWD 5000.

The Create fund hold API must return an error to users – ‘GI related limit. Please try later’.  The fund hold update must also not happen. This is the same process discussed in B2-001 FSD during the limit utilization update process. 
The interaction with GI will be handled by the interface layer and based on response from GI, the ‘result code’ on the above record will be updated as ‘Successful’, ‘Excess Occupation’ or ‘Error’ using the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record’ API. 
When user attempts prebooking/fund hold on the limit id again, the system must check if it’s a re-attempt or a new attempt using the ‘account reference’ (limit id), transaction date, business event and the transaction amount. 
If everything matches, it will be treated as a ‘re-attempt’ and the system must check the status of the current request. 
If the ‘result code’ is ‘pending’, an error will be returned stating – GI related limit. Please check the status of the request. 
If the ‘result code’ is ‘successful’, the prebooking must happen and the status of the record must be changed to ‘closed’ using the ‘Close GI Transaction Record’ API.
If the ‘result code’ is ‘error’ or ‘excess occupation’, with ‘manual operation’ as spaces, an error must be returned stating – GI related limit. Please check the status of the request. 
If it doesn’t match, it will be treated as a new request. New requests will be allowed only if the previous request is in ‘closed’ status, and a new record will be written for the limit id for the day, with a new sequence number. Else, an error must be returned to users, stating that there is an incomplete/open request. 
Users can override the ‘pending’, ‘error’, ‘excess occupation’ result codes by updating the ‘manual operation as ‘GI Skipped’ or ‘Approval’ using the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record Manual Operation’ API and re-attempt the transaction. The transaction will be allowed to go through for the below combinations. 
Result Code = ‘Pending’ + Manual Operation = ‘GI Skipped’
Result Code = ‘Error’ + Manual Operation = ‘GI Skipped’
Result Code = ‘Excess Occupation’ + Manual Operation = ‘Approval’. 
Users can also cancel a record using the functionality discussed in B2-001 FSD. 
#3.2: Creation of Prebooking: from External Systems
Prebooking / fund hold can also happen on a limit id from external systems like KF. 
If there is a GI linkage in the limit chain, a new record must be written in the GI transaction table, like in #3.1.

In the create fund hold API response, an additional attribute must be returned to indicate to external system / KF that the transaction is successful in GBP but there is a GI related limit involved.
Note that in step 2 above, if there was an ‘open’ status record for the limit Id in the GI transaction table, an error must be returned, and the transaction must fail.
The communication with GI and update to the GI transaction table record will be handled by the interface layer.

A modification of prebooking amount, where GI is involved, must be written as a new record in the GI transaction table for the delta amount and with a new business event to indicate that it’s a modification of the hold. 
For example, when the fund hold for TWD 5000 is being amended and increased to 7000, a record as below must be written for the delta amount = 2000.

The ‘modify fund hold’ API must return an error stating that it’s a GI related limit and please try after some time. Hold update must not happen. 
The interaction with GI is the same as what happens during creation. 
When user does hold modification again, the system must ascertain whether it’s a re-attempt or a new attempt by checking for records in the GI transaction table in open status using the limit id, date, business event and the delta transaction amount (2000 TWD in our example). 
If it finds a record in open status, it means that it’s a re-attempt and the result code + manual operation will determine whether the modification will go through. Same process as what was explained in the creation part. 
If there is no matching record, it will be treated as a new request and will be subject to the validations and processing explained earlier.

#3.6: Expiry / Deletion of Prebooking: from GBP
The expiry / deletion of fund hold / prebooking will also be a single step process, for limit ids with linkage to GI. 
A new record must be written in to the GI transaction table for the limit ID with business event as ‘Fund hold expiry’, the fund hold amount, request type as ‘decrease’. The status of the record must be ‘Closed’.

#4: Internal Limit Control during Limit Prebooking <B2-008-9>
Sensitive customers are also known as ‘Interested Party’. 
Internal Limit Control / Sensitive customer limit validations are being developed in GBP as part of Taiwan localization. 
During fund hold / prebooking creation on a Credit/Exposure limit ID, the limit ID customer must be subject to Internal Limit Control validations. If breached, appropriate error messages must be returned. 
Creation of fund hold must be treated like a loan disbursement transaction, where the utilization is increasing by the amount of the transaction. 
Expiry / deletion / utilization of fund hold must be treated like a loan repayment transaction, where the utilization is decreasing by the amount of the transaction. 
Modification of fund hold where the fund hold amount is increasing must be treated as a utilization increase for the delta / increased hold amount.
Modification of fund hold where the fund hold amount is decreasing must be treated as a utilization decrease for the delta / decreased hold amount. 
The ‘Secured flag’ added as part of B2-002-4 in NVBK_B2-002 FSD (tagged to level 4’s facility code) must be used to determine whether the limit chain is secured / unsecured for internal limit control validations. 
Example:
Assume Bank net value = TWD 100,000,000
Customer 90001 is flagged as a Sensitive Corporate customer and so as per the internal limit control parameter, the total secured lending cannot exceed 10% of the Bank’s net value. 
So, 10% of TWD 1,000,000,000 = TWD 10,000,000
Assume that the customer has already utilized 8,000,000. So, the maximum that the customer can draw again is 2,000,000. If a prebooking / fund hold is attempted for more than this value, an error must be returned, and the transaction must fail because of internal limit control. 
Let’s assume that fund hold was done for 1,000,000. So now, the total internal limit control utilization for the customer becomes 9,000,000.
The fund hold was modified to 1,500,000. The total internal limit control utilization must now increase to 9,500,000. 
The fund hold was modified again, taking it to 1,200,000. The internal limit control utilization must now decrease to 9,200,000. 
When the fund hold is utilized/deleted and actual disbursement is done for 1,200,000, there will be no change in the net internal limit control utilization as the decrease and increase happened for the same amount. 
#5: Internal Limit Control for Borrower when Sensitive Guarantors are linked <B2-019-3>, <B2-020-11>
Sensitive customers are also known as ‘Interested Party’. 
In Taiwan, guarantee collaterals will be created for General Guarantors, Co-Borrowers , Joint Borrowers, Joint Debtors etc. and then linked to the loan account or limit Id (level 4). The attribute ‘Guarantor Identification type’ will indicate the relationship type - whether it’s a general guarantor, co-borrower, joint borrower etc. This is covered as part of localization. 
When a loan disbursement transaction is being performed and the customer is not a sensitive customer, the system must validate whether any of the guarantee collateral customers linked with ‘Guarantor Identification Type’ as ‘co-borrower’ or ‘joint borrower’ are sensitive. The system must first check linkages to the loan account and then at the linked limit tree (till level 4). 
If yes, internal limit control must be performed treating the loan owner/customer CIF as a sensitive customer. 
If not, then the customer remains a non-sensitive customer.

Annual Review Date
Annual Review Date is a new field added at limit levels 1,2,3 in B2-002-3. 
When the Annual Review Date expires, the limit ID and all its child limit IDs must be frozen with a parameterized reason code for each level. A new BOD batch must be developed for this purpose. 
For example:
Annual review date = 2024/09/28
At 2024/09/29 BOD batch, this limit must be performed “Limit freeze”.
When users change the ‘Annual Review Date’ to a future date (> system date), the freeze on the limit ID and its child limits with the same reason code must be automatically removed. 
Examples about predefined reason code:
Level 1: Reason code 90
Level 2: Reason code 91
Level 3: Reason code 92
Promissory Note End Date
Promissory note functionality is covered in B2-002-14. 
When the end date of a linked promissory note is expired, all linked limit IDs and their child limit IDs must be automatically frozen by a new BOD batch. The reason code must be parameterized. 
For example:
End date of promissory note = 2024/09/28
At 2024/09/29 BOD batch, all linked limits must be performed “Limit freeze”.
When users change the ‘End date of promissory note’ to a future date (> system date), the freeze on the limit ID and its child limits with the same reason code must be automatically removed. 
Limit Freeze on Limit Creation <B2-011-4>
CTBC may create a limit ID in the system before all documentations are complete, but this limit must not be used. 
In such cases, the limit must be frozen along with creation. The freeze reason code is to be taken as input in the limit creation API. 
Once the documentation is complete, the users will unfreeze the same manually. 
Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-011

Proposed Solution
#1: Limit Freeze Enhancements <B2-011-2>
#1.1: Auto Limit Freeze of Child Limits
Setting up freeze on limits and its unfreezing is covered as part of localization requirements. 
If there are linked child limits, the limit freeze API must be enhanced to write the details in to a new database table for batch job processing. The details expected are:
Limit Id – limit on which the freeze / unfreeze is happening. 
Freeze Type – debit freeze / complete freeze (localization)
Reason Code 
Valid Till Date (localization)
Remarks
Action – to indicate whether the record is for ‘freeze’ processing or ‘unfreeze’ processing. 
Status – an internal batch processing status. Note that these details will only be finalized during technical design. 
A new batch job must be written to read the above-mentioned data and apply the same freeze attributes - ‘Freeze Type’, ‘Reason Code’, ‘Valid Till Date’, ‘Remarks’ - on all linked child limit IDs. This batch job must be configured to work as a near real time job. 
Note that since the parent node is frozen online, there is no risk to the bank on not freezing the child nodes online as the utilization update will fail at the parent node and return an error. 
Likewise, the ‘Remove Limit Freeze’ API must be enhanced to write details into the same database table when freeze is removed from a limit Id which has child limit Ids linked. Another batch job must be written to read the table and pick up linked child limit ids and remove freeze records with the same ‘Reason Code’ that was removed from the parent limit ID. Note that unfreeze on the parent is online but, on the children, will be handled by the batch job. This batch must also be configured as a near real time job. 
In the below example, when freeze is setup on Limit ID 4001 online, freeze must be applied on its child limits 5001 and 5002 by the batch. Shared limit is not impacted. 
When freeze is removed from 4001 online, freeze with the same reason code must be unfrozen on limit ids 5001 and 5002 by the unfreeze batch. 
If freeze is setup on Limit ID 3001, freeze must be applied on its child limits 4001, 5001, 5002, 4002 and 5003 by the batch. During batch processing, if say child 5002 has an existing freeze with the same reason code, freeze must not be applied on any of the child limits. Note that freeze on the parent will remain. 
#1.2: Annual Review Date
Annual Review Date is a new field added at limit levels 1, 2 and 3 in B2-002-3 in FSD NVBK_B2-002. 
When system date crosses the annual review date for a limit Id at these levels, the system must freeze the limit Id and all linked child limit IDs at one / multiple lower levels. 
Freeze Type = Debit Freeze. Repayments will be permitted. 
Reason Code = configured in the batch job for limit levels 1,2,3. 
As discussed in #1.1, if the limit ID or any of its child IDs is already frozen with the same reason code, the entire freeze process must fail. In the batch exception table, a record must be written for the parent limit id with reason as - freeze already exists on one or more child limits with the same reason code. 
A new beginning of day batch job must be developed for this purpose. 
When the ‘Annual Review Date’ is modified using the ‘Modify Limit Details’ API, and the date is later than system date, the system must unfreeze the limit ID for the freeze reason code that matches the freeze reason code configured in the batch job.  
If the freeze does not exist on the limit id being modified, a supervisor override error must be returned that says ‘freeze record not found’. The error is being kept as an override error so that the limit amendment can go through even if there is no freeze record on the limit id for some reason.
If there are linked child limits for the limit IDs being unfrozen, the details must be written to the same database table mentioned in section 3.1.2 in #1.1. Unfreezing the child limits must be handled by the ‘unfreeze child limits’ batch job, which will be configured as a near real time job.  
#1.3: Promissory Note End Date
Promissory note functionality is covered in B2-002-14 in FSD NVBK_B2-002. 
Promissory notes can be linked to loan accounts or limits and there is an end date captured on the linkage record. 
When system date crosses the ‘End Date’, the system must freeze the linked limit Ids and all their linked child limit IDs at one / multiple lower levels. 
Freeze Type = Debit Freeze. Repayments will be permitted. 
Reason Code = configured in the batch job. 
As discussed in #1.1, if the limit ID or any of its child IDs is already frozen with the same reason code, the entire freeze process must fail. In the batch exception table, a record must be written for the parent limit id with reason as - freeze already exists on one or more child limits with the same reason code. 
A new beginning of day batch job must be developed for this purpose. 
When the ‘End Date’ is modified using the ‘Modify Promissory Note Reference Details’ API, and the date is later than system date, the system must unfreeze the linked limit IDs for the freeze reason code that matches the freeze reason code configured in the batch job.  
If the freeze does not exist on the limit id being modified, a supervisor override error must be returned that says ‘freeze record not found’. The error is being kept as an override error so that the record amendment can go through even if there is no freeze record on the limit ids for some reason. 
If there are linked child limits for the limit ids being unfrozen, the details must be written in to the database table referred to in #1.1 of section 3.1.2. Unfreezing the child limits must be handled by the ‘unfreeze child limits’ batch job, which will be configured as a near real time job. 
Note on Unfreeze: The limit Id may be frozen with multiple reason codes. So, when we refer to “unfreeze” of one reason code, it only means that the selected freeze record on the limit id is being unfrozen/inactivated. The limit status will remain “frozen” till all freeze reason codes / records are unfrozen. 
#2: Limit Freeze on Limit Creation <B2-011-4>
In the ‘Create Limit’ API and ‘Create Quick Set Limit’ API, additional attributes must be added to freeze the limit ID on creation.

New Batch Job for Freezing Child Limit IDs when Parent is Frozen
Driver Query: Limit IDs which are frozen on system date where there are linked child limits where the freeze is not applied (unprocessed limit ids from the new database table mentioned in #1.1 of section 3.1.2 where action reads as ‘freeze’). 
Processing Logic: Create a new freeze record for all its child limit IDs with the same reason code and other attributes used on the parent limit id. 
Exception Handling: If a freeze record exists for any child ID with the same reason code, rollback freeze processing on all the child limit IDs. Record the failure reason against the parent limit Id in the same database table or in the batch exception table for reporting purposes. 
New Batch Job for Freezing Limit IDs on Expiry of Annual Review Date
Driver Query: Limit IDs where Annual Review Date has expired on the previous day (if 7 day processing) or till and including the previous working day (if 5 day processing). 
Processing Logic: Create a new freeze record for the limit ID with the reason code configured for the limit level. Create freeze records for all linked child limits and their child limits, till and including the last level. 
Exception Handling: If a freeze record exists for the limit Id or its children with the same reason code, rollback freeze processing on the limit id and its children. Record the limit Id in the exception table for reporting purposes. 
New Batch Job for Freezing Limit IDs on Expiry of Promissory Note Reference End Date
Driver Query: From the Promissory note reference records where the End date has expired on the previous day (if 7-day processing) or till and including the previous working day (if 5-day processing) and pick all actively linked Limit Ids. 
Processing Logic: Create a new freeze record for the limit IDs with the reason code configured. Create freeze records for all linked child limits and their child limits, till and including the last level. 
Exception Handling: If a freeze record exists for the limit Id or its children with the same reason code, rollback freeze processing on the limit id and its children. Record the limit Id in the exception table for reporting purposes.

Processing Logic: Unfreeze all linked child limit ids for the same reason code that was unfrozen on the parent limit ID.

Proposed Solution
#1: Collateral Field Enhancements <B2-013-2>, <B2-013-32>, <B2-013-6>, <B2-013-12>, <B2-015-1>, <B2-015-2>
The embedded xls lists the fields that are required for CTBC for the different collateral types. Some of the fields exist in GBP and have been flagged as “GBP support” = Yes.

Note that the existing fields in the standard product APIs will be retained and its handling will be covered as part of localization exercise. 
#2: Collateral Insurance Enhancements <B2-013-3>
The ‘insurance required’ flag at collateral parameter controls whether insurance details must be mandatorily captured on the collateral record or not. This is the current functionality and there is no option to override the flag at individual collateral record level. 
To meet CTBC requirements, the flag must be introduced in the Create Collateral API as below.

If a value is input during collateral record creation, it will be taken as the applicable value, overriding the collateral parameter one. 
If the value input is different from what is there at the parameter level, a supervisory override warning must be returned. 
#3: Land and Immovable Property Enhancements <B2-013-4>
Land and immovable property collateral must support multi record inputs for the below details.

Please refer to the xls embedded in B2-013-2 where the fields required for each section above are listed (Column H). 
The Create Collateral API must be enhanced to support multi row inputs for the above-mentioned sections. 
New APIs must be developed to provide listing inquiry for each of the sections above, with the collateral number as the expected input and all fields on the record as the output. 
New APIs must also be developed to modify existing records and to add additional new records. 
For example, if we take the case of collateral address details, APIs would be required for:

Maintain LIM Collateral Address Detail
#4: GI Linkage Related Enhancements <B2-013-17>
#4.1 Exposure Limit Utilization Update
When exposure limit ids are captured on ‘Guarantee’ type collaterals, the utilization of the exposure limit increases by the collateral lendable value. This is a localization enhancement in GBP. 
As part of NVBK_B2-001 FSD, exposure limits can also have linkage to GI. 
So, when exposure limit with GI linkage is getting captured on the guarantee collateral and utilization is being updated on it using the limit utilization update API, it must follow the same two-step process detailed in the B2-001 FSD under section 3.2.1, #1. The steps in brief, are given below. Please refer to the FSD mentioned above for details. 
The ‘Create GI Transaction Record’ must be internally invoked with ‘Account Reference’ as ‘Exposure Limit ID’, a unique business event / transaction code to identify collateral linkage, collateral lendable value, and the record will be in ‘Open’ status. 
An error must be returned to the user stating ‘GI related limit. Please wait and try later’. The exposure limit tagging to the collateral will not happen at this stage. The utilization update on exposure limit will also not happen. 
The interface layer will communicate with GI and then update the GI transaction record table with ‘result code’ from GI, using the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record’ API. 
Users can inquire / update the result code manually wherever required, using the ‘Modify GI Transaction Record Manual Operation’, ‘Enquire GI Transaction Record’ APIs. 
When user tries to capture the exposure limit ID again on the collateral record, the system will check the status in the GI transaction record table using the date, exposure limit id, currency, amount, and business event/transaction code and if there is a valid result code and manual operation combination, the collateral update transaction and limit utilization update on the exposure limit will go through. The status of the GI transaction record will get updated as ‘Closed’. Else, appropriate error messages will be returned. 
Note: If the tagging of exposure limit ID is happening during collateral creation itself and there is a linkage to GI, the collateral creation must itself fail in the first attempt. Creation must be reattempted after the GI transaction detail is successfully updated. 
A similar process must be triggered when the lendable value increases on the collateral where the exposure limit is linked to GI. 
For the delta increase amount, a record must be written in the GI transaction table and processed in a similar fashion. 
When lendable value decreases on the collateral, the utilization on the exposure limit will be decreased by the delta amount. When there is a linkage to GI, a record must also be written in to the GI transaction table for the delta amount with ‘request type’ as ‘decrease’ and in ‘closed’ status. 
When Collateral is discharged or the exposure limit is removed from the collateral, the utilization on the exposure limit will be reduced by the collateral lendable value. When there is a linkage to GI, a record must also be written in to the GI transaction table in ‘closed’ status for the reduction amount. 
#4.2 Linkage of Collateral to GI
The ‘Create GI Linkage’ API is covered in FSD NVBK_B2-001 and it handles linkage of limit ids or collateral ids to GI. 
When ‘Local Line ID’ = Collateral ID, the below additional fields must also be captured during linkage. Note that the fields are.

These fields must be available in the enquire API as well - Get GI Linkage details.  
Additionally, the fields – Limit Level, Line Currency, Line Amount – are mentioned as mandatory in NVBK_B2-001 FSD in section 3.1.2 #1. These should be made conditionally mandatory, to be captured only when Pool Type = FACILITY. When Pool Type = POOL, the above three fields – Appraisal Value, Bank Valuation, Currency – must be made mandatory, as discussed above. 
#5: Guarantee Collaterals – Exposure Limit Utilization Update <B2-013-18>
When exposure limit ids are captured on ‘Guarantee’ type collaterals, the utilization of the exposure limit increases by the collateral lendable value. This is a localization enhancement in GBP. 
To control how the utilization must be updated on the exposure limit, a new field – Occupation Indicator – must be added to the ‘guarantee’ type collateral, alongside the exposure limit field. Note that the field is also part of the field list in B2-013-2.

Occupation Indicator

Valid values are:

A new domain “d_CollExpLmtOccInd” must be introduced for this purpose.

The field must be added to the Create Collateral, Maintain Guarantee Details, Get Guarantee Details APIs. 
The field becomes mandatory for input when exposure limit id is captured on the collateral. It will be left blank when exposure limit ID is not captured. In cases where the exposure limit id is removed from the collateral, the field must also be updated as blank/spaces by the host. 
Exposure limit ID / Occupation indicator can be captured on the collateral only if. 
Segment code on the collateral is ‘Corporate Banking.’
Customer rating has got captured on the owner CIF (localization B31-016). 
When exposure limit is added during collateral creation or amendment, the value in the ‘occupation indicator’ must be “1” or “2”. 
During amendment of the Guarantee collateral, the value of ‘occupation indicator’ can only be changed if its set to “2” initially. “2” can be changed to “3” or “1”. Note that in this case, no GI related action must get triggered. Also, when changing from “2” to “1”, a supervisory override error must be returned.

#6: Limit Freeze on Collateral Expiry <B2-013-21>
When the linked collateral expires (expiry date < system date) on a limit id with ‘limit valuation’ as ‘Lower of Two’ or ‘Collateral Amount’, the effective limit amount becomes zero. This is an existing functionality. 
When the collateral expires, and its segment code = Corporate Banking, all linked limit ids and their child limit ids must be frozen with a configured reason code. A new BOD batch must be written for this purpose. 
When the ‘expiry date’ is updated and is greater than system date, the system must unfreeze all linked limit IDs with the configured freeze reason code. 
If one / more of the linked limit IDs do not have an active freeze with the required freeze reason code, the system must return a supervisory override error. On authorization, the limit amendment must be processed. 
The unfreeze of child limits will be processed by a near real time batch job. 
Please refer to NVBK_B2_011 where there are similar freeze/unfreeze batch jobs based on triggers like annual review date expiry and promissory note end date.

Validation during Loan Disbursement – Validate Imperfect Reason Code
Validation processing logic – loan disbursement where there is no linked limit. 
Pick up all linked collaterals where the ‘Validate Imperfect reason code’ = ‘At Disbursement’ or ‘Both’ on the collateral record’s parameter. 
If on any collateral, the ‘Imperfect reason code’ is set as ‘Attachment’ or ‘Seizure.’
Return supervisor override error if channel is branch channel. 
For other channels, bypass the validation. 
If on any collateral, the ‘Imperfect reason code’ is set as ‘Freeze’ or ‘Destroy and Lost.’
For all channels, return error. 
Validation processing logic – loan disbursement where there is a linked limit ID. 
Pick up all collaterals which are directly linked to the loan account, linked to its limit ID or the limit ID’s parent limit (Level 4 Limit ID), where the ‘Validate Imperfect reason code’ = ‘At Disbursement’ or ‘Both’. 
[Note: the collateral is expected to be linked to the level 4 limit ID, which will be the parent limit ID of the lowest level (level 5) which is linked to the loan account directly. In such cases, the collateral is not expected to be linked to the loan account directly but from a product perspective, we will validate direct linkages to the account and to its linked limit id and its parent. The other limit levels will not be validated.]
If on any collateral, the ‘Imperfect reason code’ is set as ‘Attachment’ or ‘Seizure.’
Return supervisor override error if channel is branch channel. 
For other channels, bypass the validation. 
If on any collateral, the ‘Imperfect reason code’ is set as ‘Freeze or ‘Destroy and Lost.’
For all channels, return error. 
Validation during Limit Prebooking / Fund Hold – Validate Imperfect Reason Code
Validation processing logic
Pick up all collaterals which are linked to the limit Id and its Level 4 Limit ID (parent limit id) where the ‘Validate Imperfect reason code’ = ‘At Disbursement’ or ‘Both’. 
If on any collateral, the ‘Imperfect reason code’ is set as ‘Attachment’ or ‘Seizure.’
Return supervisor override error if channel is branch channel. 
For other channels, bypass the validation. 
If on any collateral, the ‘Imperfect reason code’ is set as ‘Freeze or ‘Destroy and Lost.’
For all channels, return error. 
Validation during Collateral Discharge - Multiple validations
Validation processing logic – Validate CIF sanction list.
If the ‘Validate CIF Sanction List’ at collateral parameters is set to ‘Yes’, pick up all Owner CIFs of the collateral and Owners of all linked limit IDs and loan accounts. 
If any CIF has ‘sanction list = Y’, a supervisory override error must be returned. 
Validation processing logic – Validate Follow-up Status.
If the ‘Validate Follow-up Status’ at collateral parameters is set to ‘Yes’, pick up all Owner CIFs of all linked limit IDs and loan accounts.  Note that the Owner CIF of the collateral is not required to be validated. 
If any CIF has an active follow-up status record, a supervisory override error must be returned. 
Validation processing logic – Validate Imperfect Reason Code.
If the ‘Validate Imperfect Reason Code’ at collateral parameters is set to “At Collateral Discharge” or “Both”, the same must be validated. 
If the ‘Imperfect reason code’ is set as ‘Attachment’ or ‘Seizure.’
Return supervisor override error if channel is branch channel. 
For other channels, bypass the validation. 
If the ‘Imperfect reason code’ is set as ‘Freeze’ or ‘Destroy and Lost.’
For all channels, return error. 
Validation processing logic – Validate Loan PDCs.
If the ‘validate loan PDCs’ at collateral parameters is set to ‘Yes’, pick up all loan accounts directly linked to the collateral as well as loan accounts linked to limit IDs linked to the collateral.  
If the status of any PDC is “Stocked”, return supervisory override error. 
Validation processing logic – Validate Collateral Description. 
If the ‘validate collateral description’ at collateral parameters is set to ‘Yes’, the system must validate whether the ‘description’ field is filled in on the collateral. 
If it is blank, return a supervisory override error. 
#7.3: Update Collateral Detail after discharge
A new API - Maintain Collateral Detail after Discharge - must be developed to update the below two fields after the collateral is discharged. Note that the fields are already added as part of B2-013-2 of this document. 
Cancellation Option
Received Date of Clearance Certificates
These two fields are applicable only for Collateral types – Land and Immovable Property and Vehicles and Heavy Machinery. 
Note that these two fields will also be available in the standard collateral modify API. But once a collateral is in discharge status, the standard APIs will not allow modifications. 
Validations required while updating the ‘Received date of Clearance Certificates’ 
If ‘Cancellation Option’ is “1”, the date must be system date or less. Else, error to be returned. 
If ‘Cancellation Option’ is “2” or “3” and Segment Code = Corporate Banking and date is entered as future date, a warning must be returned. 
These validations are required irrespective of whether the ‘Received Date of Clearance Certificates’ is updated via standard collateral modification API or the new API for update after discharge.

New Batch Job for Freezing Limit IDs on Expiry of Collateral 
Driver Query: Limit IDs linked to collaterals where the Segment Code = Corporate Banking and whose ‘Expiry Date’ has expired on the previous day (if 7-day processing) or till and including the previous working day (if 5 day processing). 
Processing Logic: Create a new freeze record for the limit ID with the reason code configured in the job. Create freeze records for all linked child limits and their child limits, till and including the last level. 
Exception Handling: If a freeze record exists for the limit Id or its children with the same reason code, rollback freeze processing on the limit id and its children. Record the limit Id in the exception table for reporting purposes. 
New Batch Job for Un Freezing Child Limit IDs 
Driver Query: Limit Ids with linked child limits where the parent limit Id has got unfrozen that day when its linked collateral’s ‘expiry date’ is updated to be greater than system date. 
Note: Please refer to the unfreeze limit batch job in NVBK_B2-011. Maybe reused based on technical feasibility. 
Processing Logic: Unfreeze all linked child limit ids for the same reason code that was unfrozen on the parent limit ID.  
Exception Handling: If freeze record for the reason code does not exist on any child limit ID, rollback unfreeze processing for all the child limits for a given parent limit id. Record the failure reason against the parent limit Id in the same database table or in the batch exception table for reporting purposes.

Business Requirement 
Effective Limit Amount Calculation <B2-014-1>, <B2-014-2>
On a limit ID, GBP supports setting up multiple ‘Limit Valuation’ options as below, to arrive at the effective limit amount. 
Limit Amount – the sanctioned limit amount is also the effective limit amount. 
Collateral Amount – the value of linked collaterals becomes the effective limit amount. 
Lower of the two – the lower of the sanctioned limit amount and the value of linked collaterals becomes the effective limit amount. 
Collaterals are created in the Collateral module / microservice and then linked to entities like loan accounts, limits etc., after assigning an ‘allocation %. Applying the ‘allocation %’ on the collateral value gives the collateral value linked to that entity from the selected collateral.

Case 1: Limit Valuation selected as ‘Limit Amount.’
In this case, the collateral value has no impact on effective limit. 
Effective limit = sanctioned limit = 8,000,000
Case 2: Limit Valuation selected as ‘Collateral Amount.’
Here, the value of linked collaterals = (3,600,000 + 2,400,000) = 6,000,000 becomes the effective limit amount
Case 3: Limit Valuation selected as ‘Lower of the Two’. 
Intraday limit amount = 8,000,000.
Value of linked collateral = (3,600,000 + 2,400,000) = 6,000,000
So, the lower value = value of linked collateral = 6,000,000 becomes the effective limit amount. 
To the above-described existing functionality of GBP, CTBC needs an enhancement. 
During collateral linkage to entity type = facility, additional fields as below needs to be added. 
Linked Value Option
By Appraisal Value (Bank Valuation)
By Facility LTV ratio
By Requisition Ratio
The ‘Facility LTV Ratio’ and ‘Requisition Ratio’ fields have been added at limit level as part of B2-002-3 in FSD NVBK_B2-002. These two fields must also be available during limit Id linkage to collateral, where the values are expected to be defaulted from the limit ID but can be overridden. 
Validations:
If “linked value option” is “By facility LTV ratio”, then a non-zero ‘facility LTV ratio’ must be available as input. 
If “linked value option” is “By requisition ratio”, then a non-zero ‘requisition ratio’ must be available as input. 
For the above mentioned ‘linked value options’, the linked collateral value must be calculated as below:
[Collateral Value x Allocation % / Ratio]
If the ‘linked value option’ is ‘by appraisal value’, the existing GBP logic of using the Bank Valuation amount x Allocation % must be used. The facility LTV ratio or Requisition ratio, even if available at the limit id level, must not be used in calculations.

Proposed Solution
#1: Enhancements in Entity Linkage:
During Collateral to Entity linkage, when the ‘linkage entity type’ is ‘facility’, additional attributes may be captured, as given below.

A new domain d_CollLnkValOpt must be defined. 
Mandatory when ‘linked entity type’ is selected as ‘Facility’. 
Note: ‘By Appraisal Value’ indicates that the existing logic of using the Bank valuation amount x Allocation % will be used.

The applicable facility LTV ratio for the limit ID. 
It is expected to be fetched and populated from the limit details by the UI when the limit id is selected but can be overridden at the linkage level if required.

The applicable requisition ratio for the limit ID. 
It is expected to be fetched and populated from the limit details by the UI when the limit id is selected but can be overridden at the linkage level if required. 
Mandatory for input when ‘linked value option’ is set as ‘By Requisition Ratio’.

Number (5,2)
The attributes must be available in the ‘Create Collateral’, ‘Maintain Entity Linkage’, ‘Get Entity Linkage Details’ APIs. 
Note that these attributes must not be captured for other linkage entity types. It is expected to be controlled by the channel / UI. Even if captured, it will not be processed at host for other entity types. 
#2: Enhancements to Calculation of Linked Collateral Value
As discussed earlier, the ‘Facility LTV Ratio’ and ‘Requisition Ratio’ are added to limits as part of NVBK_B2-002 FSD. These can be fetched and displayed to users on the branch channel from the limit details, based on the limit Id input. These can also be overridden at the collateral linkage level and the input in the linkage API will be used in the processing logic explained below. 
During linkage of limit ID to collateral, when the ‘Linked Value Option’ is selected as ‘By Appraisal Value’, the existing GBP functionality of taking the collateral to value / lendable value of the collateral and calculating the value assigned to the entity based on the % of allocation to the entity must continue.

Enhancement to Shares and Bonds Collateral <B2-015-3>

To be able to input the ‘Market value of total collateral’ and/or the total ‘collateral to value’ amount directly, without capturing the shares/bond details in certain cases. 
A new flag – share bond detail capture - must be available to control whether the shares/bond details are to be captured mandatorily (existing GBP function) or optional capture to support the CTBC requirement above. 
During collateral modification, when the shares / bond details are input or modified, the same flag must control whether the ‘market value of total collateral’ and the ‘collateral to value’ total amount are recalculated or not.
