When the ‘share bond detail capture’ is set to ‘Yes’, it means that the existing GBP functionality will be used. 
The individual share/bond detail must be input – at least one record. The mandatory fields per record will be same as what is there in the create API. 
The ‘total market value of collateral’ must be the sum of the individual market values captured on the share/bond records. 
The ‘total collateral to value’ must be the sum of the individual collateral to values captured on the share/bond records.
This means that any change in the valuation of the individual records must result in recalculation of the total market value and the total collateral to value amounts. 
When the ‘share bond detail capture’ is set to ‘No, it means that: 
The individual share/bond detail becomes optional for input. The existing mandatory fields on the individual share/bond detail must be kept optional. 
The ‘total market value of collateral’ is expected to be manually input. It needn’t be the sum of the individual market values captured on the share/bond records, even if captured. 
The ‘total collateral to value’ is also expected to be manually input. It needn’t be the sum of the individual collateral to values captured on the share/bond records, even if captured. It also needn’t be equal to (total market value of collateral – margin). 
This means that the API will not expect a change in the total market value or total collateral to value when there is any change in the individual share/bond detail captured. 
A supervisor override error must be returned in cases where share bond detail capture is set to ‘No’. 
Note that during shares and bonds collateral creation and amendment, when the ‘share bond detail capture’ is set as ‘Yes’, the UI/Channel is expected to add up the individual record amounts and send the ‘total market value of collateral’ and ‘total collateral to value’ as inputs in the API. When the ‘share bond detail capture’ is set to ‘No’, the UI/Channel is expected to not add up and keep the total amounts as manual inputs for the API.

CTBC Requirement around Periodical Insurance Renewal: 
A file will be provided from an external system, to be processed by SI. 
The system is expected to deduct the premium amount, create a new insurance record, and modify the previous insurance record to stamp it as ‘Closed’ or ‘Cancelled’. 
If the deduction is unsuccessful, insurance premium amount must be charged as an advance fee on the loan account using the localized functionality. 
The file will contain the required fields to invoke APIs performing the below functions. 
Fund transfer from CASA to BGL for the premium amount
Expense advance fee charging
Create insurance record
Modify Insurance record
As part of the insurance file processing, the below steps must be executed one after the other. 
Step 1: Validations: 
Collateral ID must be existing, and the collateral status active. Else, return error. 
CASA must be existing and the account status active. Else, return error.
Internal Account must be existing and account status active. Else, return error.
Loan account must be existing and the account status active. Else, return error.
If the loan account is marked as NPA or has been written off, return error. 
If the collateral is linked to a limit(s) and all loan accounts under this 4F limit are closed, return error. 
The cover end date on the existing insurance record must be less than or equal to (system date + 2 months). 
Date 1 = System date + 2 months
For example, 2024/7/31 + 2 months = 2024/9/30
2024/12/30 + 2 months = 2025/2/28
If cover end date at insurance record > Date 1, then return error. 
The ‘Entrust Flag’ on the existing insurance record must be ‘Yes’. 
If the input loan account’s Segment Code = Consumer Banking, the input CASA account must be either the settlement account of the input loan account or the linked CASA account (when loan account is an overdraft loan account). 
The ‘Insurance Required’ flag must be ‘Yes’ on the collateral. 
Priority on the collateral record must be set as ‘First Priority’. 
If the input loan account’s Segment Code = SBG, collateral is expected to be linked to limit ID. But even in such cases, a loan account number that is linked to the limit ID will be provided as input in the API. The system must validate that the loan account primary owner is one of the collateral owner CIFs. 
Error must be returned If the input loan account’s Segment Code = SBG, 
AND the maturity date of the input loan reference and the cover end date on the existing insurance record are in the same year + month.
 AND the loan account’s product/instrument is not an overdraft product.
Step 2: Premium Deduction
Deduct premium from CASA and transfer to the designated Internal Account. 
If this transaction is successful, go to step 4. Else, step 3. 
Step 3: Charging of advance fee
Perform a localized transaction to charge expense advance fee on the “X” bucket of the loan account. 
Step 4: Create a new Insurance record on the input collateral ID. 
Step 5: Modify old insurance record on the input collateral, updating the status with the input status. Exit.

New business events must be created for this purpose to handle premium collection, either from the CASA account or from the loan account. 
Processing – pre-requisites:
The applicable ‘exchange rate purpose’ to be used must also be preconfigured, in case of any cross-currency transactions. 
The ‘expense advance fee type’ to be used must be pre-configured.  The ‘due raising’ logic (unpaid first term or delay dues bucket) and the bucket impacted (L, X, Y, Z) will be as per what is parameterized for the fee. 
Processing – Step 1 – Validations
The existing insurance details given as input in the API must be on the input collateral id. Else, an error must be returned. 
The collateral ID input must be in ‘Complete’ business status. Else, an error must be returned. 
The CASA account input must be in Active status and without any follow-up status that prevents debit. Else, an error must be returned. This will require co-ex processing in the initial phase as the CASA will reside in the legacy system. 
The loan account input must be in active status and not an NPA account or written off. Else, an error must be returned. 
Note that if the collateral is linked to a limit (level 4) and not to a loan account, the logic must be built in the interface layer to fetch and populate the required loan account number. If there is no active loan account linked to the limit, the API cannot be invoked as it’s a mandatory field. 
The Internal account to be credited must be in active status. Else, an error must be returned. 
A validation is required with the ‘cover end date’ on the existing insurance record. The end date must be earlier than or equal to (system date + 2 months).  It basically means that the current insurance policy can only be renewed in the last two months before expiry or after expiry. 
The ‘Entrust Flag’ on the existing insurance record must be set to ‘Yes’. 
If the input loan account’s ‘Segment Code’ = ‘Consumer Banking’, the input CASA account number must be either the settlement account of the input loan account number or the linked CASA account (when loan account is an overdraft loan account. Overdrafts are covered in B2-035 / B2-036). 
The ‘Insurance Required’ flag must be ‘Yes’ on the collateral. 
Priority on the collateral record must be set as ‘First Priority’. 
If the input loan account’s ‘Segment Code’ = SBG, the system must validate that the input loan account’s primary owner is one of the collateral owner CIFs. 
If the input loan account’s Segment Code = SBG, AND the maturity date of the input loan reference and the cover end date on the existing insurance record are in the same year + month AND the loan account’s product is not an overdraft product, an error must be returned. 
Processing – Step 2
The insurance renewal premium amount must be debited from the input CASA account and credited to the internal account. 
The existing BAL-39: Post Bookings API is expected to be internally invoked in this step, to be finalized during the technical design. 
If this transaction is successful, step 3 below must be skipped. 
Processing – Step 3
If the insurance premium debit from the input CASA account fails due to insufficient funds, the same must be debited from the input loan account as an expense advance fee and credited to the internal account. 
The localized Expense Advance fee charging API is expected be internally invoked in this step, to be finalized during technical design. 
Processing – Step 4
The new insurance renewal details must be updated, creating a new internal sequence on the existing insurance record. The existing record must be moved to history using existing process. 
The Maintain Insurance Details API is expected to be internally invoked in this step, to be finalized during technical design.

New inquiry for listing collateral insurance details
New fields in Collateral Insurance
Composite API to handle file-based insurance renewal process.

Posting Restriction for loan accounts <B2-019-9>
CTBC requires to set posting restrictions for transaction to allow its user to set or remove posting restrictions on a loan account to allow or restrict the posting of certain transactions.
Posting Restrictions are used to stop certain groups of transactions from being performed on an account.  The restriction can be set at product level or account level.  If set at product level, it will be inherited at the account level and can be overridden at account level.  
On setting up the posting restrictions or when its removed, it is recorded in the transaction history of the loan account.  If a posting restriction is removed from an account, a Reason Code should be captured and recorded in transaction history of the loan account. This will be part of the non-financial transaction that needs to be recorded as part of the loan account transaction history and needs to be printed in the loan account statement.
Further to this, CTBC requires the option to have the posting restriction set as error or overridable also defined at the loan account level overriding the product level.

Settlement account validation on loan creation <B2-019-16><B2-025-4>
CTBC wants for its certain loan products to validate the settlement account that is given for the loan in loan creation or amend.
Following validations are required,
For certain loan products the settlement account should be of the primary borrower.
For certain loan products the settlement account should be of either the primary borrower or the guarantor.
For certain loan products the settlement account’s CIF and the primary borrowers CIF should be having the relationship as specified by bank in a parameter like,
Spouse 
Parents
It’s for cases where the loan is in the name of husband, but the settlement account is of spouse as she will be paying back the loan. 
Finally for some other loan products none of the above validations are required.
Apart from the product level validations, if the loan is marked under a debt negotiation plan, then no settlement account should be allowed for the loan.
Customer validations on loan creation <B2-019-2>
CTBC wants the following new validations on the primary customer of the loan during loan creation.
For loan creation with segment code given as ‘consumer banking’ or ‘SBG’ the primary borrowers CIF level uncooperative flag value should be ‘N’. The uncooperative flag at the customer level is a new field being added as part of SSR topic B31-003. This validation is not applicable for certain loan products like the ‘Labor Relief’ product.
For loan creation for a company or business customer, as part of the company details validation it should be checked that a CIF is linked to the company CIF as person in charge. The CIF tagged as person in charge should be valid with the below values present in the system.
National ID number
Name 
Date of Birth
Active address
For certain loan products (loan for public servants) during its loan creation, it should be checked that the primary customer has the below information captured at their CIF level.
Institution Type
Institution
For foreign currency loan products during its loan creation, it should be checked that the primary customer has the below information captured at their CIF level.
Country of risk

Business Requirement 
Credit account validation on disbursement <B2-020-1><B2-041-4>
For certain loan products CTBC performs a validation to check whether the disbursement proceeds are getting credited to its own CASA accounts.
Following validations are required,
For certain loan products the credit account should be of the primary borrower.
For certain loan products the credit account should be of either the primary borrower or the guarantor.
For certain loan products the credit account should be the settlement CASA as defined at the loan account and not to any other account. 
Finally for some other loan products none of the above validations are required.
Apart from the product level validations, 
for unsecured loans, if the credit account is a CASA used for Securities transactions, then it should not be allowed.
For any loan, if the credit account is a CASA used for cash card, then it should not be allowed.
On reversal of disbursement this validation should not be done.
Customer validation on disbursement <B2-020-5>
CTBC wants the following new validation on loan disbursement.
On disbursement it should be checked that the primary borrowers and the guarantors CIF level uncooperative flag value is ‘N’. The uncooperative flag at the customer level is a new field being added as part of SSR topic B31-003. Non overridable error should be return if the flag value is ‘Y’.
This above validation should be done for,
All disbursements for certain loan products
Only first disbursement for certain loan products
Not to be validated for certain loan products
On reversal of disbursement this validation should not be done.
Tenor and Maturity date validation against limit on loan creation and disbursement <B2-020-16>
CTBC for its facility limits requires to have the below mentioned fields, which is covered as part of SSR B2-002.
Annual review date
Grace days for Annual review
Annual review date validation required.
Maximum loan tenure
Last loan disbursement date
If the loan account is linked to a limit, then the following validations are required.
Loan Function
Validation to be performed
Create Loan 
Loan Tenure @Loan account <= Maximum tenure @ limit
If Annual review date validation required = Y then check 
Loan Maturity Date @ Loan Account <= {Annual Review Date @ Limit + Grace     Days @ Limit}
Else skip this validation
Amend Loan
Loan Tenure @Loan account <= Maximum tenure @ limit
If Annual review date validation required = Y then check 
Loan Maturity Date @ Loan Account <= {Annual Review Date @ Limit + Grace     Days @ Limit}
Else skip this validation
Disburse Loan
Loan Tenure @Loan account <= Maximum tenure @ limit
If Annual review date validation required = Y then check 
Loan Maturity Date @ Loan Account <= {Annual Review Date @ Limit + Grace     Days @ Limit}
Else skip this validation
Final Disbursement date @ Loan Account <= Last loan Disbursement @ Limit
On reversal of disbursement these validations should not be done.
Maturity date validation against calendar on loan creation and disbursement <B2-020-17>
CTBC wants for its certain loan products to validate the maturity of its accounts not to fall on a holiday basis the applicable calendar at the loan account. 
For certain products it should validate that the maturity date (last installment payment date) is on a working day and if it is falling on a holiday on disbursement then overridable warning error should be given. 
For certain products this validation should not be applicable.
Further if the calendar is not setup, then the validation should not be done and for the maturity date arrived no error should be returned.
Disbursement date deadline validation <B2-020-22>
CTBC wants to enhance the current localized validation (under SSR 1.2) of validating the first disbursement to be done before a parameterized number of months set at loan product level.
The enhancement required is to perform the validation not just for the first disbursement but for all the disbursements. Again, for certain loan products the validation is required only to be done for the first disbursement and for certain products it’s required to be done for all the disbursements and the last disbursement should be completed before the period set at the product level.
For example:
Consider a loan product/instrument set up as “2 months” as period and “all disbursements need validation”.
Account level: 
Date of sanction : 3-Mar-2023
So, all disbursements to be completed by 3-May-2023.
First disbursement on 25-Mar-2023 -> Allowed.
Second disbursement on 30-Apr-2023 -> Allowed.
Third disbursement on 4-May-2023 -> Disallowed
Setting up account level margin interest rate from limit and account attributes <B2-020-19>
CTBC requires to automate the input of account level interest rates margin. It needs to be derived basis the below loan and its limit attributes. 
Loan Account loan product/Instrument ID
Loan Account tenure
Loan Account approved amount (Sanction amount in GBP)
Loan Account limit’s start date
Loan Account limit’s Customer Rating (Localized under SSR B2-002)
These values need to be compared with a new parameter to be defined having the following attributes.
Effective Date
Loan Instrument ID
Customer Rating
Loan Tenure from
Loan Tenure to
Loan amount from
Loan amount to
Additional Margin Rate
Fee Amount
After comparing the accounts and its limits data with the new parameter the additional margin rate is to be fetched which will be one final additional margin rate basis the tier to which the account falls. 
Sample calculation sheet attached for reference.
The additional margin rate fetched will be one final rate which is added with the standard margin rate (Localized under SSR B2-002) from limit and this should be the net margin to be given at the loan account level. This part of adding the margins to get final margin will be done outside of GBP. 
Composite RestAPI to club and perform multiple loan functions together <B2-020-9><B2-042-3>
CTBC requires to perform multiple loan functions together with a single input, basis certain condition. This is required for the external systems integration and usability.
Four composite RestAPIs are required as below,
1st composite RestAPI: To perform the functions of ‘Loan creation’, ‘Authorization’ (User confirmation) and ‘Loan Disbursement’.
2nd composite RestAPI: To perform the functions of ‘Loan top-up’ and ‘Loan Disbursement’.
3rd composite RestAPI: To perform the functions of ‘Loan Reschedule’ and ‘Loan Disbursement’.
4th composite RestAPI: To perform any of the above 3 composite RestAPIs based on certain conditions as per the input given as detailed below.
Below input fields should be mandatory for the RestAPI,
Loan reference
Instrument ID
Rate type (Part of interest details at account level)
Margin rate (Part of interest details at account level)
Third party limit id (Added as part localization item SSR B2-019)
For each loan instrument it should be defined if its loan accounts details can be copied, and a new account can be created.
Conditions are listed as below, which need to be executed step by step.
Step 1 - GET loan details via (a)loan reference and save this account’s Instrument ID, Rate type, Margin rate, third party limit id as ORIGINAL value, let’s say F1, F2, F3, F4.
Step 2 - GET loan instrument details via (b)
Step 3 - Compare ORIGINAL value with input value, which mean. 
Compare (b) with F1
Compare (c) with F2
Compare (d) with F3
Compare (e) with F4
Step 4 - If there is no difference then GO TO step 5 ELSE step 8.
Step 5 - If this account is undisbursed, for example: business status = Ready for disbursement, then execute third composite API and no next step.
Step 6 – If this account is closed, then execute first composite API and no next step.
Step 7 - If this account is disbursed, for example: business status = Active /Expired /Freeze then further condition are listed as below:
If at loan instrument it allows to copy from old account (this flag comes from step 2), then execute first composite API and no next step.
If at loan instrument it does not allow to copy from old account (this flag comes from step 2), then execute second composite API and no next step.
Step 8 - If this account was disbursed, for example: business status = Active/ Closed/ Expired/ Freeze, then execute first composite API with loan creation basis the input values given in the RestAPI and no next step.
Step 9 - If this account is undisbursed, for example: business status = Ready for disbursement, then throw transaction error and no next step.
Currency Change for Loan Account <B2-020-14>
CTBC requires the option to change the loan currency of a disbursed loan. 
The loan should have no unpaid dues, Interest Accrued, Penal Interest Accrued.
The loan accounting entries should use the Mid-Rate for the balance transfer if no exchange rate is specified in the transaction. When the exchange rate is specified in the transaction then it should be taken as the cross rate and from amounts the rates to base currency should be arrived and accounted.
For example: 
Case 1: For a loan in USD currency changed to EUR currency of DBU, where the DBU’s base currency is TWD and no exchange rate is given.

Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-020 Loan Disbursement
Existing Functionality 
GBP supports loan disbursement with single or multiple tranches in any currency with a linked fee to be charged with disbursement. 
GBP supports top-up loan disbursements.
GBP has the option to disburse and top-up loan with the below RestAPI’s.
#

GET /consumer-loan/{account-number}/disbursement-details
3
disbursement-schedule

The new RestAPI should have in its input, the primary borrower’s CIF, loan product and the credit CASA account. 
The new RestAPI with its input should process as below,
Step-1:
Validate, if the disbursement proceeds is not being credited to a CASA account, then error should be returned as ‘Invalid CASA Account’, that is when this new RestAPI is invoked with an incorrect CASA account in its input.
Step-2:
Validate, if the CASA account is an account created for securities processing and loan is marked as a unsecured loan. The CASA accounts product should be checked if it is defined for stock trading (Deposit product parameter to define a stock trading product is covered as part of the SSR B3-036). If the CASA account is under a stock trading deposit product, then error should be returned as ‘Credit account cannot be a stock trading account for unsecured loan’, else continue with the step-3 as below.
Step-3:
Validate, if the CASA account is an account created for cash card processing. The CASA accounts product should be checked if it is defined for cash card processing (Deposit product parameter to define a cash card product is covered as part of the SSR B3-029). If the CASA account is under a cash card deposit product, then error should be returned as ‘Credit account cannot be a cash card account’, else continue with the step-4 as below.
Step-4: 
Check the validation method set at the loan product and perform the validation as listed below.
For,
1 – The primary borrower’s CIF and the credit CASA accounts CIF should be compared and matched, if they are different then error should be returned as ‘Incorrect CASA account’.
2 – The primary borrower’s CIF to be compared with credit CASA accounts CIF and guarantor’s CIF. If anyone is matching, then success msg to be returned to continue with the disbursement processing, else error to be returned as ‘Incorrect CASA account’.
The guarantor CIF to be fetched using another inter microservices call to ‘Collateral Management’ with the primary borrower’s CIF and credit CASA account’s CIF if they are linked under a guarantee collateral type.
3 – The credit CASA account should be the settlement account of the loan else error to be returned as ‘Incorrect CASA account’.
4 – No validation is required for the loans under these product and credit CASA account can be any CASA account.
Once the above validations are successful the success response should be returned, and the credit CASA account should be allowed to be used for the loan disbursement process.
The loan disbursement should have the orchestration to call this API and continue the processing only if this API is successful. On reversal of loan disbursement this API need not be called.

Composite RestAPI to club and perform multiple loan functions together <B2-020-9><B2-042-3>
Four composite RestAPIs and their reversals are required to be developed as detailed below,
1st composite RestAPI: To perform the functions of ‘Loan creation’, ‘Authorization’ (User confirmation) and ‘Loan Disbursement’.
This RestAPI should have the attributes of 
‘Create Loan Account’
‘Authorize Loan Account Opening Request’ 
‘Create Manual Disbursement Request’ 
‘Authorise Manual Disbursement Request’
It should have the necessary attributes in its payload to perform these transactions one after other and the new loan creation and its disbursement should be completed in one go.
In case of failure in processing of any of these individual RestAPIs the respective error should be returned and the whole request should be failed without any loan getting created. The loan accounts sequence number will be skipped, and the next number will be allocated for the next loan created.
For reversal individual RestAPIs reversals should be used with the original composite API’s transaction reference number. The user can reverse the disbursement first and then separately cancel the loan.
2nd composite RestAPI: To perform the functions of ‘Loan top-up’ and ‘Loan Disbursement’.
This RestAPI should have the attributes of 
‘Create Loan Top-Up  Request’
‘Release Loan Top-Up Request’ 
‘Authorize Loan Top-Up Request’ 
‘Create Manual Disbursement Request’
‘Authorise Manual Disbursement Request’
It should have the necessary attributes in its payload to perform these transactions one after other and the loan top-up and its disbursement should be completed in one go.
In case of failure in processing of any of these individual RestAPIs the respective error should be returned and the whole request should be failed without any loan top-up and disbursement getting recorded.
For reversal individual RestAPIs reversals should be used with the original composite API’s transaction reference number. The user can reverse the disbursement and reduce the loan amount till the disbursed value.
3rd composite RestAPI: To perform the functions of ‘Loan Reschedule’ and ‘Loan Disbursement’.
This RestAPI should have the attributes of 
‘CreateLoanReschedule’
‘Create Manual Disbursement Request’
‘Authorise Manual Disbursement Request’
It should have the necessary attributes in its payload to perform these transactions one after other to increase the loan term and perform its disbursement in one go.
In case of failure in processing of any of these individual RestAPIs the respective error should be returned and the whole request should be failed without any loan reschedule instruction and disbursement getting recorded.
For reversal individual RestAPIs reversals should be used with the original composite API’s transaction reference number. The user can reverse the disbursement and then user can perform another reschedule to bring back the old loan term.
4th composite RestAPI: To perform any of the above 3 composite RestAPIs based on certain conditions as detailed below.

Step-1:
Validate, if the loan account is active and has only principal outstanding and no other dues/arrears, interest accrued, penal Interest accrued pending at the loan account level. If there are any other dues, then error should be returned as ‘Currency Change not allowed with outstanding dues’ else next step to be done.
Step-2:
Validate, the new account currency given is an active currency set in the system with exchange rate set between the loan account currency and the new currency. If successful, the next step to be done else error should be returned as ‘To currency is not active in the system’.
Step-3:
After successful validations, the following processing should be done,
The loan account’s currency should be changed to the new currency as specified.
The account’s GL should be remapped to reflect the new currency.
The principal balance in the loan account should be updated basis the new currency after converting the balance using the prevailing mid-rate using triangulation method.
If the exchange rate is input by the user, then that rate should be used to arrive at the converted amount in the new currency.
Balance transfer GL entries should be generated for the change for the account’s old currency balance to the new currency balance. Sample accounting entries is given in section 2.8 above.
With the new currency balance at the account, it’s linked facilities utilization should be revalued using mid-rate between old currency to new currency using triangulation method.

Business Requirement 
Stamping Multi-Stage Absolute Interest rates for loan <B2-021-10>
CTBC for its corporate loans negotiates with its customers the interest rate of their loans for a fixed period. Maybe every week, every month. This is done in an external system called BRAM and it sends a file which contains the accounts and its effective date, fixed rate and expiry date to be stamped for negotiated interest rates.
The Interest rate type is set as fixed rate. Meanwhile, CTBC will set a higher interest rate which is effective from the end date of negotiated period. If customers fail to negotiate with the bank, the higher interest rate will start to be applicable. The higher interest rate will be additional reference rate from product + 4%.
Thus, one absolute interest rate record should be captured and stamped on the loan, like for a loan with account number – 10001
Effective date = 08-May-2023, Net rate = 2% till Expiry date = 21-May-2023
On 21-May-2023 the new rate of additional reference rate + 4% should be stamped and effective on loan.
CTBC requires to have the option to take a single input of the above data as below,
Effective date= 08-May-2023, 
Fixed rate= 2%  
Expiry date= 21-May-2023
and create interest condition record for 2% till 21st May and then on from 21st May have the interest rate switch to a product specific reference rate plus a 4%.
Additional Interest Details Capture <B2-021-11><B2-021-7>
CTBC wants to capture two additional user input data with the capture of interest records at the loan account level. This is required to input the reason and remark on why the interest record were modified or created.
Whenever for a loan account the interest details are captured or modified, the below two new data is also to be captured as an optional input.
New field
Field type and length
Reason code
Text of length 2 characters
Remark
Text of length 100 characters
Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-021 Loan Interest Details
Existing Functionality 
GBP supports setting interest rate for loan with fixed interest rates. The fixed interest rates can be set with a future dated valid from date and it can be enquired using the Interest rate history option.
The option to capture and modify the interest rates is done using the below RestAPI’s.
#
Object Reference
API Name
API URI
1
loan-account-onboarding
Create Loan Account
POST /consumer-loan/create-loan-account
2
interest-conditions
Get Account Level Interest Conditions
GET /consumer-loan/{account-number}/interest-conditions/account-level/{interest-category}
3
interest-conditions-type
Modify Interest Conditions
PUT /consumer-loan/{account-type}/{account-number}/interest-conditions/{interest-category}
4
interest-conditions-type
Approval workflow of interest-conditions-type
PATCH /consumer-loan/{account-type}/{account-number}/interest-conditions-type
5
loan-rollover
Create Loan Rollover Request
POST /consumer-loan/{account-number}/loan-rollover
6
quick-onboarding
Create Loan Account (Quick onboarding)
POST /consumer-loan/quick-onboarding
The above list is as per the current API catalogue which will get further enhanced basis the updated catalogues.
Proposed Solution
The current loan interest rate setting options in GBP should be enhanced as below for the new requirements as detailed in section 2 above.
Stamping Multi-Stage Absolute Interest rates for loan <B2-021-10>
The current RestAPI’s used to set interest conditions should be enhanced, to set, in a single input the data to create a negotiated absolute interest condition record with below 3 values from the external system (BRAM).
‘valid from date’, ‘next interest rate review date’ and an ‘absolute interest rate’.
The above input should be used in the enhanced RestAPI as detailed below. 
The ‘Modify Interest Conditions ‘ RestAPI should allow to input a new interest condition for negotiated absolute interest rate in the interest condition section.
The RestAPI should be enhanced to have a new Product override type (prodovrrdtyp = Negotiated Absolute) value for the input of negotiated interest rate for a Loan Account number (account-number). The enhanced RestAPI with the below input should stamp the fixed rate.
Interest Rate Type (intrst-rate-type = Fixed)
Application Frequency (application-freq = Monthly)
Rate Category (rate-category = Debit)
Product override type (prodovrrdtyp = ‘Negotiated Absolute’)
Interest Effective From date1 (intrst-effect-from-date = input date) – (This field should be used to specify the interest valid from date)
Interest Rate1 (intrst-rate = input rate) – (This field should be used to specify the absolute interest rate)
Next Review date (nxt-intrst-rt-revw-dt = input date) – (This field should be used to specify the interest rate expiry date for the negotiated fixed rate)
With the above input of the new value prodovrrdtyp = ‘Negotiated Absolute’, the negotiated absolute rate should be stamped in the loan account for the period from ‘intrst-effect-from-date‘ till the next review date ‘nxt-intrst-rt-revw-dt’ thus the next review date should be the expiry date for negotiated absolute rate. 
The current processing for next review date should continue the same when the ‘prodovrrdtyp’ is ‘Incremental’ or ‘Absolute’.
The system codes for the attribute 
‘prodovrrdtyp‘ (d_OverrideType) should have a new value of ‘Negotiated Absolute’
For the interest condition records with prodovrrdtyp = ‘Negotiated Absolute’ on the next review date the product level additional reference rate should be stamped with the fixed margin for the remaining period of the loan.
The additional reference rate and the fixed margin for the loan should be picked up as specified for the loan product. For this a new loan product level special interest rate container should be defined.
The current special interest rate container for deposits and the localized special interest container for loan subsidy interest should be further developed. The new special interest rate container should be named as ‘Negotiated Absolute Interest Containers’. 
At the special interest rate container, the reference rate and its fixed margin should be set for the loan product which can be floating or fixed as per the current special interest container structure.
The below EOD batch should be enhanced to read the loan interest condition for prodovrrdtyp = ‘Negotiated Absolute’ to check if it’s on the next review date as per the current processing. Then a new interest condition row should be inserted with the reference rate and type along with its margin as set in the special interest rate containers.
Job ID 
Job Name 
10635
Interest reset processing for loans.
With the new interest condition added, the existing absolute rate should be moved as a past record.
Say on or before the expiry date of the negotiated rate record if the customer again negotiates, then a similar record with new valid from date should be created along with a future next review date. In such cases the special interest container rates need not be picked up, as the new absolute rate record is effective now and the old record is moved as past records. Further only on the EOD of next review date of the new negotiated absolute rate record the special rate container should be further used if there was no new negotiated absolute rate stamped.
The below additional validations should be present in addition to the RestAPI’s current validation to see that,
‘next review date’ is greater than ‘Interest Effective From date1’.
‘next review date’ is not backdated.
Both the dates are not after the loan maturity date.
In case of failure, error should be returned as ‘Incorrect effective dates entered for rates’.
The negotiation of the loans interest rate is done via the external system BRAM. BRAM then sends a file to process the negotiated interest requests in bulk. The file should be read by SI and then for each record the enhanced RestAPI should be fired to stamp the fixed rate. In SI there should be validation to check that the ‘valid from date’, ‘next interest rate review date’ given in the input file from BRAM are not backdated. In such cases the record should be rejected, and not processed and remaining records should be taken up for processing. The detailed SI processing will be covered as part of Interface.
With the old rate being moved as past record and a new rate record being inserted the loan account rate history should show the past, current and future interest rates in a listing. The current ‘Get Account Level Interest Conditions´ gives only one interest details as per the effective date given. A new ‘Loan Search’ should be developed to return the past, current and future interest rates. It should list all the interest rate records grouped as past records, current applicable records and future records.
Additional Interest Details Capture <B2-021-11><B2-021-7>
The current options to set or modify interest rate conditions for debit or penalty interest, should be enhanced to capture additional input data of reason code and remarks on performing the operation. The new fields should be returned as part of the enquiry also.
The current RestAPI’s to capture, modify and enquire the loan interest conditions should be enhanced to have two new input fields as defined below.

Business Requirement 
Flexible Installments for loan <B2-022-1>
CTBC requires for its loan accounts, the option to set flexible installments within the loan term. 
The flexible installments are to be computed based on a flexible installment period within the loan term. 
Within the “flexible installment period,” the installment amount is calculated based on “flexible installment term”.
After the “flexible installment period,” the installment amount is calculated based on remaining loan tenure.
For example, a loan account has a loan tenure of 240 installments. For the first 36 installments, each installment amount is to be calculated based on 360 installments, and starting from the 37th installment, each installment amount is calculated based on the remaining 204 terms.
In the above scenario, the setup at the account level would be “flexible installment period = 36” and “flexible installment term = 360”.
The flexible installment period and term can be set in different scenarios,
Flexible installment period can start from the start of the loan.
It can be set during the tenure of the loan.
Flexible installment period or the term or both can be amended during the flexible installment period.
Flexible installment period and term can be set multiple times during a loan tenure.
During flexible installment period, repayment holidays like principal holidays can be set.
Each of the flexible installment period given to the loan should be listed as like the installment holidays records in the current reschedule listing transaction.
A sample working sheet for the above cases is embedded below for reference,
The flexible installment period and term should not be allowed if,
Amortization period is given for loan period.
Balloon/bullet payment is given for loan.
Installment frequency is not monthly.
Loan created is with fixed maturity date given by user at time of loan creation.
Loan is in NPA status.
Flexible installment period given is greater than the remaining tenure of the loan from the Flexible Installment Start date. 
Flexible installment start date is given as a backdated date. 
Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-022 Loan Installment Type
Existing Functionality 
GBP supports flexible repayments with the options of initial repayment holidays for principal only or for Installments (principal plus interest).
GBP also supports giving repayment holidays during the life of the loan.
GBP has the option to give repay holidays with the below RestAPI’s.

Proposed Solution
The current option for giving repayment holidays should be enhanced as below for the new requirement as detailed in section 2.1 above.
Flexible Installments for loan <B2-022-1>
The current option to set repayment holidays and rescheduling of loan should be enhanced to setup flexible installment period with a flexible installment term as its amortization term to arrive at the installment for the flexible installment period.
The following needs to be done,
Capture of additional data attributes of flexible of installment start date, period and term as part of the option for setting repayment holiday and rescheduling and loan creation.
Perform the cross-field validation at the time of set up and throw relevant errors as covered in paragraphs below.
Basis the input the repayment schedule should be generated considering the flexible installment term and period as specified. 
First the schedule to be generated where the flexible installment term is not applicable as per the current process then from the flexible installment start date the next installment should be identified from when the flexible installment should start. 
From this installment, the installment period should be computed including this as the first one.  On the scheduled balance as of the BOD of first flexible installment date, the schedule should be generated as per the installment arrived using the flexible installment term for the flexible installment period. 
After the flexible installment period ends again for the remaining term of loan the repay schedule basis scheduled balance as of the flexible installment end date should be generated as per current processing.
That is, if a loan account has a loan tenure of 240 installments and flexible installment set to start from the start of the loan with ‘flexible installment period’ as 36 and ‘flexible installment term’ as 360. For the first 36 installments, each installment amount is to be calculated based on 360 installments, and starting from the 37th installment, each installment amount is calculated based on the remaining 204 terms.
Similarly let's take a case with,
Loan amount : 100000
Interest Rate: 6.5%
Loan Term: 6 months
Disbursement dt: 1-Jan-2023
Interest Practice: Actual by 365
Without any flexible installment the repayment schedule should be as below,
Now after setting the below flexible installment terms the repayment schedule should be as given below with the flexible term values,
Flexible Installment Start Date: 10-Mar-2023
Flexible Installment Period: 2
Flexible Installment Term: 36
Flexible Installment Start Date: 28-Feb-2023
Flexible Installment Period: 2
Flexible Installment Term: 36
Here the flexible installment period starts from immediate next installment from the ‘Flexible Installment Start Date’ and if its same as well its from the next installment as given in the cases below,
Repay day=10
System Date=2023/10/04
Case1:
if flexible installment start date=2023/10/4 then first flexible term will be applicable to the installment of 2023/10/10.
Case2:
if flexible installment start date=2023/11/9 then first flexible term will be applicable to the installment date of 2023/11/10
Case3:
if flexible installment start date=2023/12/10 then first flexible term will be applicable to the installment date of 2024/01/10
Case4: Repay day=10 and System Date=2023/10/10
if flexible installment start date=2023/10/10 then first flexible term will be applicable to the installment of 2023/11/10.
In the above process c) multiple schedule computation should be performed and merged to form the single repay schedule for the loans having flexible installments during the flexible installment period and other installments during the remaining period.
Working samples are attached in the section 2.1 above for reference.
During the flexible installment period, the user can setup principal holidays and also change the repay day of the loan.
In current principal holiday processing where once, the principal holidays are marked basis the holiday start date, then those interest only installments do not reduce even if the repay day is changed or repayment schedule is rebuilt. Similarly, the flexible installments once marked should not change even if the repay day is changed or repayment schedule is rebuilt.

Business Requirement 
New Discounted Interest Computation <B2-023-3>
CTBC requires for its Discounted interest loan accounts, the discounted interest to be computed basis a new formula. 
This new method is called the True Discount Interest computation with the below formula to compute the upfront discounted interest,
Upfront interest amount = Loan amount – Loan amount / ( 1 + (account rate * loan tenor in days / BASIS DAYS))
So, for the case,
Loan amount 
600000
Account rate 
5%
Loan tenor in days 
730
BASIS DAYS (Days in a Yr)
365
The upfront interest will be computed as below,
Upfront interest amount = Loan amount – Loan amount / ( 1 + (account rate * loan tenor in days / BASIS DAYS))
= 600000 – (600000/ (1+((0.05*730)/365)))
= 600000- 545454.54
= 54545.46
The disbursement amount will be 600000 and the upfront interest of 54545.46 will be reversed back from the credit account.
This new discounted interest method should be in addition to the existing formula of, 
‘Upfront interest amount = Loan amount * account rate * loan tenor in days / BASIS DAYS’ 
and both these methods should be available at the loan product level for the user to configure the product basis one of the methods.
Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-023 Loan Interest Calculation Accrual and Computation

So, for the case,

Account rate 
5%
Loan tenor in days 
730
BASIS DAYS (Days in a Yr)
365
The upfront interest will be computed as below,
Upfront interest amount = Loan amount * account rate * loan tenor in days / BASIS DAYS
= (600000 * 0.05*730)/365
= 60000
The interest is amortized during the life of the loan.

FSD-B2-024.name: NVBK_B2-024_遲延利息及違約金_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99.docx
FSD-B2-024.text:
Business Requirement 
Capitalize Penalty accrual on Repayment <B2-024-1>
CTBC requires to capitalize and collect the penalty accrual on principal or interest arrears on repayment. So, while appropriating the repayment amount with the penalty interest, first the penalty interest capitalized if any should be knocked off and then the penalty interest accrued should be capitalized to the tune of the amount being repaid and then it should be knocked off.
CTBC wants the penal interest accrued also to be shown as part of the due amount in repayment and arrears enquiry.
e.g.
If there are unpaid dues, let’s say installment date is 10-Aug-2023.
Today is 24-Aug-2023, account is in arrears, let’s say.
Principal due= 10,000
Interest due= 2,000
Penal accrual= 50
So, the due amount will be 12050 (10,000+2,000+50) on 24-Aug-2023.
If payment with 12050 has been made by customer on 24-Aug-2023.
Penal accrual of 50 should be first capitalized to loan and income recognized and then with the repaid amount the penal interest bucket should be knocked off.
Penal Interest for Principal Moratorium Period and Negotiated Repayments<B2-024-4>
As per the Taiwan’s country regulations, if installment type is “EI – Equated principal plus interest installments” or “Equal-Equal principal installments”, for the consumer loan, the penal interest should be calculated based on unpaid principal dues only.  
So, at the loan instrument level, for penal interest (Interest Category=Penal) the calculation basis should be defined as “Unpaid principal dues”.
Penal Interest on Normal Interest arrears during Principal Moratorium Period:
Further at the loan account, there might be a case with principal moratorium (or principal holiday) and only interest installments during the moratorium period. So penal interest is required to be charged if accounts are in interest arrears during that period, which should be calculated based on “unpaid interest dues” instead “unpaid principal dues”. After the moratorium period the penal interest should be computed on “unpaid principal dues”. The penalty rate and grace period to be applied for moratorium period arrears and installment period arrears is same.
For example:
     First disbursement date: 01-Jan-2023
     Principal moratorium : 6 months 
     During first 6 months, penal interest will be calculated based on “unpaid interest dues”.
     Afterwards, penal will be calculated based on loan instrument’s setup.
Penal Interest on EMI components for Negotiated Repayment Schedules:
For the cases where there is “EI – Equated principal plus interest installments” and negotiated principal repayments and if both falls on the same day. Then the penal interest on unpaid principal due or unpaid principal plus interest dues should not include the negotiated principal due. The penal interest on negotiated principal should be computed separately at a different rate and method as localized.
For example: 
   10-Jul-2023: Installment=10,000 (Principal=8,000 and Interest=2,000)
   10-Jul-2023: Negotiated principal=5000
In this gap, if the penal interest calculation basis is “unpaid principal dues”, the unpaid negotiated principal is required to be excluded from unpaid principal dues.
So, the penal principal interest should be first calculated based on 8,000 if calculation basis is selected as “unpaid principal dues”, then penal for negotiated principal should be computed separately.
Additional arrear details and enhanced consecutive arrear term processing <B2-024-5>
On top of the localization done under this SSR B2-024, to have flat amount-based penalty with a ‘Max Continuous Penalty Terms’.  
CTBC requires to have below 2 additional requirements,
Configure the term between two consecutive arrear terms:
The current localized processing for continuous arrear installments for the ‘Max Continuous Penalty Terms’ and then stopping the arrear processing for one installment and then again to start the arrear processing after one break installment, needs to be enhanced to have the stop period of arrear processing to be made configurable.
New arrear details in loan enquiry:
3 new arrear fields to be computed and stored at loan account level and to be displayed in loan enquiry.
Arrears collected terms: The field should have the unpaid arrear term subject to the max of the term set in the instrument as per the below logic.
Should be the count of unpaid dues increasing with every defaulted installment, up to a “Max Continuous Penalty Terms” defined at loan instrument. 
IF the value of “Max Continuous Penalty Terms”  reaches its max value then no more incrementing of this field is done and its value is capped till the dues are fully paid.
Should be blank if unpaid dues are zero.
Arrears collected start date: The field should have the last arrear date till it’s fully paid as per the below logic.
Should be the last arrear date (date from when the arrear is overdue) if there are unpaid dues else this field is empty.
On partial payment and if the oldest due is appropriated then last arrear date should be the next oldest outstanding arrear.
Should be blank if unpaid dues are zero. 
Arrears collected end date: The field should have the date of dues firing when the arrears overdue term equals the maximum continuous penalty term set at loan instrument level.
Should be the date of dues firing when the arrears overdue term is equal to “Max Continuous Penalty Terms” as set at the loan instrument.
Should be blank if unpaid dues are zero.
Threshold amount for rate-based penalty <B2-024-6>
Like the threshold check for flat fee-based penalty done as part of the localizations of the SSR B2-024. CTBC wants to add a threshold at loan instrument, which should decide whether to accrue penal rate-based accrual for its loan accounts. 
The threshold should also have the option to be set based on any of the below mentioned arrear balances,
Unpaid Principal
Unpaid Interest
Unpaid Principal plus Unpaid Interest
For example: 
Say the,
Threshold amount:5000
Threshold based on: Unpaid Principal + Unpaid Interest
First disbursement date : 05-Jan-2023
First installment date : 05-Feb-2023, 
Installment:2000 
Unpaid Dues:2000
From 05-Feb-2023 to 04-Mar-2023, no penal accrual as its under threshold.
Second installment date: 05-Mar-2023
Installment:2000
Unpaid dues:4000
From 05-Mar-2023 to 04-Apr-2023, no penal accrual as its under threshold.
Third installment date: 05-Apr-2023
Installment:2000
Unpaid dues:6000
From 05-Apr-2023, penal accrual will be start as the unpaid dues has crossed the threshold.
Enhanced grace period computation <B2-024-7>
The current localized grace period function for arrear accrual, needs to be enhanced to define the grace period against the following,
Grace period Calculation basis (“Unpaid Principal” or “Unpaid Principal + Unpaid Interest”)
Grace period including holidays (‘Yes’ or ‘No’)
Negotiated Principal Payments with Interest only Installments:
This is for corporate loans, where if installment type is selected as ‘Interest only’, then principal repayments will be negotiated with specific principal repayment schedule.
For example:
First disbursement date: 10-Jan-2023
Principal payment frequency: Quarterly
Principal repay day: 25
Principal payment start date: 25-Apr-2023
Interest payment frequency: Monthly 
Interest repay day: 10
Interest payment start date: 10-Feb-2023
The new grace period parameter at loan instrument should be allowed to set grace period basis,
Calendar working days or including holidays.
Also, the calculation basis based on “unpaid principal” or “unpaid principal + unpaid interest”.
If loan instrument is set with,
Grace period: 5 days 
Grace period including holidays: Yes
Grace period Calculation basis: Unpaid Principal 
Then,

Proposed Solution
The current penal interest processing GBP should be enhanced as below for the new changes as detailed in section 2 above.
Capitalize Penalty accrual on Repayment <B2-024-1>
The penal interest is always accrued, it’s not capitalized, on repayment it is required to be capitalized and collected. This should be done basis the localized parameter value of Interest Application Frequency = With Collection.
All the repayment RestAPI’s (refer to impacted RestAPI list) should be enhanced so that, while appropriating the repayment amount with the penalty interest, first the penalty interest due if any should be knocked off and then subsequently the penalty interest accrued should be capitalized to the tune of the amount being repaid and then it should be knocked off.
As part of repayment transaction, BaNCS must do the following.
If accrued penal interest is available
   Capitalize the same. 
       {Debit Loan Account
      Credit Interest Income}
 Then
   Proceed with repayment collection and appropriation.
Else
Proceed with repayment collection and appropriation. 
End if
The current repayment enquiry and the account financial enquiry should be enhanced to show the penal interest accrued as part of the due amount.
Penal Interest for Principal Moratorium Period and Negotiated Repayments <B2-024-4>
The penal interest processing should be enhanced for the interest only payment arrears and negotiated principal payment arrears.
Penal Interest on Normal Interest arrears during Principal Moratorium Period:
For loan accounts in principal moratorium (or principal holiday) and interest only installments the penal interest should be charged on “unpaid interest dues” if accounts are in interest arrears during that period. After the moratorium period the penal interest should be charged on “unpaid principal dues”.
Sample computation is given in the embedded worksheet below.
For this on top of the localized penalty interest processing, enhancement should be done to add additional penalty processing calculation basis for Interest only installments. A new penal calculation basis (Mora Int and OD Prin) in interest parameters should be added at the loan product/Instrument level for principal moratorium-based accounts. This should compute penal on interest arrears during moratorium period and unpaid principal arrear during installment period as given below.

Business Requirement 
ACH repayment with Valid from and to dates < B2-025-5>
CTBC requires to have a valid from and to date for its ACH records of loans. The ACH job which picks the records for the current dates processing for file generation should only pick those records for which the current date is in between the records valid from and to dates.
For example: 
 Loan creation & disbursement done on 10-Mar-2023 with repay day as 10.
   ACH record to be set with valid from date as 10-Jun-2023 and valid to date as 10-Dec-2023.
ACH files (for external banks’ auto debit) will be generated with the account from 10-Jun-2023 to 10-Dec-2023 on every 10th of the month.
New ACH Settlement Instruction status and processing < B2-025-7>
CTBC requires to have a new ACH instruction status which is to be updated as part of confirmation done by the centralized operation centre of the bank. This step is done after the ACH settlement instruction is recorded at the loan account.
Only after this confirmation these instructions are to be sent for the external bank’s approval.
This is applicable only for ACH with direct debit (created via Application document through branch OTC) and not for the ACH with electronic direct debit (created via alternate channel like Web/Net banking).
With the new status the new enhanced processing is required to be as below,
Steps
CTBC’s ACH processing flow
Online Step 1
Capture of ACH request with DDA and eDDA identifier.
Online Step 2
On ACH repayment details creation, the ACH record status should be ‘Apply’ for DDA and eDDA requests.
Online Step 3
CTBC’s additional step to confirm the borrower’s ACH records documents received which are in ‘Apply’ status. This is done by the CTBC user from the centralized operation center of the bank for the DDA records and for eDDA records, it’s done by the external system.
Step-1:
For the DDA and eDDA records once confirmed should move to the ‘Document Confirmed’ status. 
Step-2: 
For the DDA records which are in ‘Document Confirmed’ status the user does the additional bulk confirmation to stamp the current application date as a ‘Settlement date’. The settlement date being a new field for the ACH records of CTBC.
This is not required for the eDDA records.
Batch 1: 
The request file (ACHP02) generation for external bank’s approval of the ACH records should follow the below new process.
Select criteria: For the ACH records of,
DDA: (ACH status = ‘Document confirmed’ and settlement date > 0)
eDDA: ACH status = ‘Document confirmed’
After the file is generated then ACH status should be set as ‘Waiting for approval’.
Batch 2: 
The processing of the response file should read external files (ACHR02, result of ACHP02) received from external banks, each record in the file will be with the ACH status of ‘Waiting for approval’.
Basis the ACHR-CR-RCODE value (one of the column record of ACHR02) the ACH status should be updated as below, 
If value is ‘0’ then update ACH status as ‘Active’ else update the ACH status as ‘Inactive’.
Batch 3: 
The request file (ACHP01) generation for external banks auto debit with the records having their ACH record active and loan repay due date on 2 working days after current application date.
Select criteria: For the ACH records of, 
DDA and eDDA: (ACH status= ‘Active’ and (loans repay date – 2 working days )= current application date)
Batch 4: 
The processing of the response file should read external files (ACHR01, result of ACHP01) received from external banks, for each record in response file having its ACH status “Active”. The repayment to the loan account should be done with the amount as received in the response file.
Changes on top of the localization are in the steps ‘Online Step 3’, ‘Batch 1’ and ‘Batch 3’. The embedded excel below depicts the customization changes in ACH processing along with the localized ACH processing steps.
Failure counter with retry and termination for ACH processing  < B2-025-15>
CTBC requires to have a failure count to be recorded with the ACH record for the loan when the external file comes in with unsuccessful return code like “Unavailable balance”. This should be incremented for each return code when there is an unsuccessful return. 
Also, a retry option is required where the failed record should be retried the next day for that installment period. If it again returns with an unsuccessful return code, then retry should be stopped. For one installment period only once the retry should be performed. 
For certain return code if the failure count exceeds a threshold value, then the ACH processing should be stopped, and the status of ACH instruction should be stamped with a new Termination status.
The count should keep on incrementing for each failure and when its successful it should be reset.
Changes on top of the localization are in the ‘Batch 4’ and ‘Batch 1’ as covered in section 2.2 above.
Enhancement on credit arrears processing < B2-025-11>
CTBC wants to provide interest benefit for the excess payments done on its certain loans. The credit arrears in loan should be netted with the loan outstanding to compute loan debit interest.
With the credit arrears getting netted for the loan interest computation the breakdown also needs to be shown basis the netted balance.
Similar breakdown is covered for interest rate change and prepayment (Principal credit) as part of localization.

Proposed Solution
The current localized ACH repayment processing and repayment enquiry in GBP should be enhanced as below for the new changes as listed in section 2 above.
ACH repayment with Valid from and to dates < B2-025-5>
CTBC requires to have effective date and expiry date on its ACH repayment records. 
The current RestAPI’s capturing the settlement instructions for loan ACH payment-method should be enhanced to have additional processing for valid-from-date and valid-to-date.
The localized batch job to generate the ACHP01 file for external banks auto debit should be enhanced to pick, only those ACH records having their valid-from-date less than or equal to current application date (QZ date) and valid-to-date greater than or equal to current application date (QZ date). On loan’s repay date (Repay date = QZ date) in the ACH job, the ACH settlement instruction should also validate that its Valid-from-date <= QZ date <= valid-to-date, then only the record should be included in the auto debit request file ACHP01.
That is, for a loan created and disbursed on 10-Mar-2023 with repay day on 10th and having its ACH settlement instruction set with valid-from-date as 1-Jun-2023 and expiry date as 15-Dec-2023. Then the ACH file ACHP01 (for external banks’ auto debit) should be generated with the loans record from 10-Jun-2023 to 10-Dec-2023 every month 10th. For the 10-Jun-2023 installment the repayment file ACHP01 should be generated on 2 working days before the 10-Jun-2023. This change is covered in the below paragraph.

With the current processing of ACH, after the settlement instruction for ACH is recorded the record is in ‘Apply’ status and then the batch picks these records for external banks confirmation. This needs to be enhanced in the CCP microservices by having two additional steps to be performed with the ACH records moving to a new status of ‘Document Confirmed’ with its stamping date as recorded in a new field ‘Settlement date’.

Enhancement in Batch-3 processing in generating the ACHP01 file
The current localized batch-3 job generating the ACHP01 file on the due date of the loan should be enhanced to have one more option to generate the ACHP01 file 2 working days in advance for CTBC in EOD. 
CTBC uses the file to load into its internal system and perform its internal processing and sends this file to the clearing systems one day before the due date and on the due date the external bank processes the request and sends the response file by 4 pm. The response file received by CTBC on the loan due date is processed and the loans are repaid.
Consider the case: 
   Loan creation & disbursement: 10-Mar-2023 and repay day: 10th. 
   ACH repayment details set with effective date = 10-Jun-2023, expiry date = 10-Dec-2023
   ACH files (for external banks’ auto debit) will be generated from 10-Jun-2023 to 10-Dec-2023
Say the calendar to be followed is as follows,
Working
Working
Holiday
Holiday
Working
08-Jun
09-Jun
10-Jun
11-Jun
12-Jun
With generation of ACHP01, 2 working days before the due date.
On running batch 3 on 8-Jun, the account should be picked up and added to the file. The accounts having their installment date between 10-Jun and 12-Jun with ACH active collection should be added to the ACHP01 file.
In the same case if the ACH record was not active or say its effective valid from date was given to be a future date then it should not be added to the ACHP01 file.
At CTBC the effective valid from date is input as the applicable installment date.
Let’s say current date = 2-Apr-2023, repay day = 10 and auto debit is to be effective from 10-Jun-2023. So, the valid from date for the instruction is given as 10-Jun-2023.
While running batch 3 on following date:
on 8-Apr-2023: ACHP01 will NOT include the account in the file generated.
On 8-May-2023: ACHP01 will NOT include the account in the file generated.
On 8-Jun-2023: ACHP01 will include the account in the file generated.
So, with valid from date for the settlement instruction in future the batch-3 should fetch the ACH instructions basis the below date condition.
ACH valid from effective date <= Next installment date <= Expiry date
Failure counter with retry and termination for ACH processing < B2-025-15>
CTBC requires to have a failure count to be recorded with the ACH record for specific failure return codes.
A new field should be added to the localized ACH master table to record the failure count. 
Sl.
No.
Attribute Name
Description
O/M
Data Type
1
Failure Count
It’s to record the count of times the ACH recovery request to external bank has failed with specific return code consecutively
O
Numeric (2)
To configure the return codes for which the failure count should be incremented, a new lookup table should be developed with below attributes,
Label
Data Attribute
Remarks
ACH Return Code
Varchar2 (2)
The field will have the ACH return code for which the failure count should be incremented
Threshold Count
Numeric (2)
The field will have maximum count for a return code after which the ACH record will be terminated.
This field when defined with the return code of 00 should indicate that it’s for the aggregate failure count across all return codes for the ACH record to be terminated.
In the lookup table the ACH return code and their threshold count should be stored. This table should be referred by the ACH batch to perform the failure count update and processing.
Basis the failure count for the return code as incremented for an ACH record, the configured the threshold count should be compared and then the ACH record stopped, and its status should be updated as ‘Termination by CTBC’. The current Termination status will continue to be stamped when the ACH instruction is terminated by customer or when its expiry date is crossed as per current processing.
Also, on failure for a particular return code in an installment period, the record should be retried only once irrespective of the return code in that installment period. Thereafter for the ACH record the collection will be tried only in the next installment period.
The detailed processing is illustrated in the examples below.
For example, with the below thresholds
ACH Return CodeThreshold Count
01-Unavailable balance3
22-Account Closed1
00-Aggregate Counter3
Changes on top of the localization are in the ‘Batch 4’(to update failure counter) and ‘Batch 1’(to terminate).
Changes in Batch 4 and Batch 1 are illustrated with used cases as given below: 
<Case-1> Set 0 to “Failure count” if RCODE of ACHR01 is “00” 
“00” means “auto debit is successful”
<Case-2> Plus 1 to “Failure count” if RCODE of ACHR01 is “01”
“01” means “Unavailable balance”
<Case-3> If one of the following happened, then CTBC wanted to terminate the external banks’ auto debit, system needs to update ACH status as “Termination by CTBC” & update End Date of ACH records as next working date.
# If RCODE of ACHR01 is specific code, e.g. 22,23,24 … (codes as defined in the above lookup table)
# If “Failure counter” = 3 (this max counter as defined in the above lookup table) 
Batch 4: This batch should be enhanced to mark the ACH record with ‘Termination by CTBC’ status and set the end date.
Batch 1:  This batch will handle ACH record with ‘Termination by CTBC’ status, once ACH status = (‘Termination by CTBC’ or ‘Termination) & End Date=system date, this batch will generate a new record (ACHP02) to intimate the external bank to stop the ACH, this is covered in localization. Including the new status of ‘Termination by CTBC’ is the additional enhancement.
<Case-4> if RCODE of ACHR01 is “01” and the failure count has not reached the threshold, then CTBC wants to retry and request another “Auto debit”, but just try only one more time in the installment period.
That is if first request and its retry both failed then for the installment period the request should not be sent and only for the next due date the request for collection should be sent. 
For example: 
Say, Repay day=10
10-May => send file ACHP01 for external banks’ auto debit  <-First time during this installment period
11-May => receive file ACHR01, RCODE=”01”   <--- update failure count as 01
12-May => try again, send file ACHP01 for external banks’ auto debit <-Second time during this installment period
13-May => receive file ACHR01, RCODE=”01”. <= Stop here till next due date <--- update failure counter as 02
10-Jun => send file ACHP01 for external banks’ auto debit 
11-Jun => receive file ACHR01, RCODE=”01”    <--- update failure count as 03
If “Max Threshold failure count=03” then stop here, no more trying.
12-Jun => ACHP01 file for external banks’ auto debit will not contain this record anymore.
<Case-5> if RCODE of ACHR01 is “00” while it’s the second time on retry the success response was received, the value date of repayment must be the sending date of ACHP01. Hence the loan should be credited with back value dated repayment.
For example: 
Sub-Case 1: 
Repay day=10
10-May => send file ACHP01 for external banks’ auto debit  <-First time during this installment period
11-May => receive file ACHR01, RCODE=”00”
<--- value date of repayment will always be the date when the request was sent to external bank (10-May) even if the file generated by the system is 2 working days before 
Sub-Case 2: 
Repay day=10
10-May => send file ACHP01 for external banks’ auto debit  <-First time during this interest/installment period
11-May => receive file ACHR01, RCODE=”01”
12-May => try again, send file ACHP01 for external banks’ auto debit <-Second time during this interest period
13-May => receive file ACHR01, RCODE=”00”. 
<--- value date of repayment will be the date when the request was sent, the sending date of ACHP01 (12-May)
