Business Requirement 
Threshold Validations for Loan Prepayment < B2-026-1>
CTBC requires new validations to be done on performing loan prepayment, basis new threshold values. CTBC needs two sets for threshold value parameters to be set at the loan instrument level.
Set–1 – Basis the prepayment penalty period final end date.
With localization the new method to compute prepayment penalty in amount or percentage rate, basis period based slab was developed as per below sample. 
Period From
Period To
%
Amount
0 months
3 Months
5
3 months
6 Months
3
6 months
9 Months
2
CTBC requires to have new threshold amounts to be set basis prepayment transaction being performed before or after the prepayment penalty period final end date (9months post first disbursement date for the above sample case).
Prepayment Transaction Threshold Amount (Before Penalty Period Final End Date):
This new prepayment threshold amount is required to be checked when the prepayment transaction is done before the Penalty Period Final End Date, the transaction is validated against this threshold amount. If the transaction amount is under the threshold, the transaction continues, otherwise, its further checked against a prepayment retention period being covered in section 2.2 below.
For example, if this Prepayment Threshold amount is set as $5000, then, if prepayment amount is over $5000, then the transaction should further check the retention flag and period as per section 2.2 else the prepayment transaction should continue.
Prepayment Accumulated Threshold Amount (After Penalty Period Final End Date):
This new prepayment threshold amount is required to be checked when the prepayment transaction is done after the Penalty Period Final End Date or if the period based penalty rate slabs are not set, the transaction is to be validated against accumulated threshold values as listed below.  
Accumulated Period (in Months)
Accumulated Threshold Amount
Installment Threshold (no. of instalments)
These new thresholds of accumulation period - ‘Accumulated Period (in Months)’ and maximum accumulated repayment – ‘Accumulated Threshold Amount’ and  defined number of installments – ‘Installment Threshold’ should validate with the prepayment amount, the accumulated repayment amount for the defined accumulation period is not breaching the threshold of maximum accumulated repayment amount and the amount of next installment amount times the number of installments defined. 
That is, that within the accumulation period, the total amount of all repayment and prepayment including the current prepayment amount should not be larger than the maximum accumulated repayment amount set at the product level. 
For example, the setup could be “Accumulation Period” is 2 Month, and “Max Accumulated Repayment Amount” is $50000 and no Installment threshold count set. Then, say for an account the accumulated repayments including repayment and prepayment is $46000 and then if the user does a prepayment of $4001 then the prepayment transaction should further check the retention flag and period as per the processing given in section 2.2 below. If user does a prepayment of $4000 then the prepayment transaction should be successful.
If number of installments – ‘Installment Threshold (no. of instalments)’ is also set then accumulated repayment should be validated with the next installment amount times instalment threshold count
That is, for the threshold parameter setup. 
Accumulated Period = 2M, 
Accumulated Threshold Amount = NT$50000, and 
Threshold Installment = 5 Installments. 
If the user wishes to do a prepayment say on Oct.19th 2023, then with this parameter setting, the following will happen:
The Accumulated Period is 2 Months, so system needs to trace accumulated payment amount back 2 Months from the transaction date. And this traced accumulated payment amount is to be validated against both the Accumulated Threshold Amount of NT$50000 and the Installment Threshold Amount, which in this setup is 5 times of the Next Installment. If the traced accumulated payment amount is under both thresholds, the transaction continues, otherwise, the retention processing is done as given in section 2.2 below.
Set–2 – Basis the threshold amount and count of installments.
If the loan instrument is set with below thresholds, then these thresholds are required to be checked when the prepayment transaction is done.  
Threshold Amount
Installment Threshold (No. of Instalments)
The threshold parameter setting for this one can be Threshold Amount = NT$500000, and Installment Threshold = 15. Assume the loan account’s Next Installment NT$20000. So, the Installment Threshold Amount would be 15 * 20000 = 300000.
The prepayment transaction amount is validated against the Threshold Amount of NT$500000 and Installment Threshold Amount of NT$300000. If the transaction amount is under both thresholds, the transaction continues, otherwise, the retention processing is done as given in section 2.2 below.
Of the above 2 sets of threshold validations, for a loan product only one should be allowed to be set and made effective. The above threshold validations should be skipped if the loan is under debt negotiation plan even if the threshold flags are set for the loan product and account.
Prepayment Retention Applicable Period < B2-026-2>
CTBC requires to set a prepayment allowed period whenever customer requests for a prepayment in a consumer loan. After the request is taken, the customer is allowed to do the prepayment within the period and thereafter it should be disallowed, and a new request should be raised.
The prepayment allowed period in working days needs to be defined at loan product. When the customer requests for a prepayment via call centre or branch the request is to be taken and basis the period defined at the product the prepayment allowed end date should be set at the loan account and validated.
The above threshold validations should be skipped if the loan is under debt negotiation plan even if the threshold flags are set for the loan product and account.
New Prepayment Penalty Computation method with Threshold< B2-026-4>
CTBC uses 2 prepayment penalty computation methods with collection options of Inclusive(Prepay amount including penalty) and Exclusive(Prepay amount excluding penalty). 
Prepayment Penalty Method:
The two methods should use the below formulas,
Method 1:
Exclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = prepayment amount * rate% * (prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment date)/Interest Practice
Inclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = [prepayment amount / (1 + {rate% * ((prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment date)/Interest Practice)})] * rate% * ((prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment date) / Interest Practice )
Method 2:
Exclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = prepayment amount * rate% 
Inclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = prepayment amount – (prepayment amount / (1 + rate%))
Note that the method 2 is covered as part of localization.
The rate here is the localized prepayment penalty rate set basis period tier. 
Interest Practice refers to the number of days in a year set for the product for normal interest accruals which could be 360 or 365 or actual.
For example,
Say the prepayment amount is 50000 NTD,
Loan disbursement date is 1Jan2023,
Prepayment date is 10Jan2023,
Loan maturity date is 1Jan2024,
Prepayment rate tier is set as below for both the new methods.
Penalty period from
Penalty period from
Prepayment penalty rate
0 months
3 months
5
3 months
9 months 
2
Prepayment penalty period final end date is 9 months after 1Jan2023 which is 1Oct2023.
Then the prepayment penalty for the Method 1 with interest practice days as 365 will be,
Exclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = prepayment amount * rate% * (prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment date)/Interest Practice
= 50000*0.05*(01Oct2023 – 10Jan2023)/365
= 50000*0.05*264/365
= 50000*0.05*0.7232876
= 1808 (Rounded)
Inclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = [prepayment txn amount / (1 + {rate% * ((prepayment penalty period final end date  – prepayment txn date)/365)})] * rate% * ((prepayment penalty period final end date  – prepayment txn date) / 365)
= [50000/ (1+{0.05*(01Oct2023 – 10Jan2023)/365})] * 0.05 *((01Oct2023 – 10Jan2023) / 365)
= [50000/(1+{0.05*264/365})] * 0.05 *(264 / 365)
= [50000/(1+{0.05*0.7232876})] * 0.05 *0.7232876
= [50000/(1+0.036164)] * 0.036164
= [50000/1.036164] * 0.036164
= 48254.91 * 0.036164
= 1745 (Rounded)
The prepayment penalty for the Method 1 with interest practice days as 360 will be,
Exclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = prepayment amount * rate% * (prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment date)/Interest Practice
= 50000*0.05*(01Oct2023 – 10Jan2023)/360
= 50000*0.05*264/360
= 50000*0.05*0.7333333
= 1833 (Rounded)
Inclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = [prepayment txn amount / (1 + {rate% * ((prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment txn date)/360)})] * rate% * ((prepayment penalty period final end date  – prepayment txn date) / 360)
= [50000/ (1+{0.05*(01Oct2023 – 10Jan2023)/360})] * 0.05 *((01Oct2023 – 10Jan2023) / 360)
= [50000/(1+{0.05*264/360})] * 0.05 *(264 / 360)
= [50000/(1+{0.05*0.7333333})] * 0.05 *0.7333333
= [50000/(1+0.036666)] * 0.036666
= [50000/1.036666] * 0.036666
= 48231.54227 * 0.036666
= 1769 (Rounded)
The prepayment penalty for the method using Method 2 will be,
Exclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = prepayment amount * rate%
= 50000 * 0.05
= 2500 (Rounded)
Inclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = Prepayment amount – (Prepayment amount / (1 + Rate%))
= 50000 – (50000 / (1 + 0.05))
= 2381 (Rounded)
Prepayment Penalty Charging Threshold:
CTBC also requires a new threshold parameter to skip the computed prepayment penalty collection from the loan account.
The new threshold parameter “Prepayment Penalty Threshold” (in installments) should be defined at the product/instrument level, which will be number of installments. The prepayment amount if its less than the parameterized count of threshold installments times the next installment amount then no penalty should be charged else the penalty should be collected.
For example, setup can be “Prepayment Penalty Threshold” = 2. This means if the prepayment transaction amount is less than the amount of 2 installments, then no prepayment penalty is to be collected from customer.
Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-026 Loan Principal Credit
Existing Functionality 
GBP supports the prepayment function and has loan product parameter to enable prepayment at loan account level.
GBP also supports the function to apply penalty on prepayment.
The current loan prepayment RestAPI’s are as given below,

Proposed Solution
The localized prepayment/principal credit penalty computation and collection function should be enhanced as below for the new requirements as detailed in section 2 above.

A new loan product/Instrument parameter should be introduced to define the thresholds for loan prepayment transaction to be performed over and above the current prepayment allowed parameter flag. These thresholds are not applicable if the loan account is under a debt negotiation plan, so if the loan account has the ‘Debt Negotiation Flag’ set then this threshold validation should be skipped. (‘Debt Negotiation Flag’ will be covered as part of the SSR B2-032).
After the current prepayment validations like prepayment allowed flag and prepayment period checks and the check for debt negotiation flag this new threshold validation should be performed in prepayment transaction and prepayment enquiry.

1 – Threshold basis the prepayment penalty period final end date.
With the new parameter prepayment threshold type set as 1, the prepayment transaction date should be validated with the prepayment penalty period final end date. Where the prepayment penalty period final end date is the end date from loan first disbursement date basis the prepayment penalty period-based slabs, last slab’s end date.

This new prepayment threshold amount should be checked when the prepayment transaction is done before the Penalty Period Final End Date, the transaction is validated against this threshold amount. If the transaction amount is under the threshold, the transaction continues, otherwise, its further checked against a prepayment retention period being covered in section 2.2 above.

These new thresholds validate with the prepayment amount, the accumulated repayment amount for the defined accumulation period is not breaching the threshold of maximum accumulated repayment amount and the amount of next installment amount times the number of installments defined. If the transaction amount’s accumulated value is under the thresholds the transaction continues, otherwise, its further checked against a prepayment retention period being covered in section 2.2 above.
Note that in case of the prepayment penalty period-based rate slab are not set but the threshold conditions are set then these threshold conditions of ‘After Penalty Period Final End Date’ should be performed on prepayment.

The processing of RestAPI should follow the below steps,
Step-1
The RestAPI should first check the ‘Prepayment Allowed’ and ‘Prepayment Retention Applicable’ flag at loan product level, if allowed proceeds with the next step else gives error ‘Prepayment Retention Period not applicable for the product’. 
Step-2
As the next step, the account level ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ is to be checked if its already stamped if set as ‘1’-Yes, then error ‘Prepayment request already present’ should be returned else the next step to be done. For the value ‘3’-Indefinite Period it should allow to continue with next step for its modification. 
Step-3
As the next step, basis the user input the account level ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ field should be set as one of the below values,
‘1’-Yes and the ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ should be set as the new RestAPI transaction date + ‘Prepayment Retention Applicable Period’ as per loan accounts product
‘2’-No and ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ should be reset as blank if there is any value present.
‘3’-Indefinite Period and the ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ should be set as high value date to indicate that the retention period is set forever. 
With the flags ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ and ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ set for the loan. 
When a prepayment transaction is performed on the loan, it should first check the existing conditions and then the new threshold validations as detailed in above section 2.1 and section 3.1.2 point 1 (B2-026-1) above. During the validations if it’s over the threshold, system should do the retain process, which is to check the account level ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ and ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’.
If ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ = 1-Yes or 3-Indefinite Period, then system should check account level’s ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ if its greater than the prepayment date of prepayment enquiry or prepayment transaction date, then prepayment transaction is allowed to be performed else error should be returned as ‘Prepayment Retention period expired’.
If ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ = 2-No, then error should be returned as ‘Perform prepayment request with retention first’.
Both ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ and ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ should be a onetime setting for a prepayment retention period request. These fields should be reset every time the prepayment transaction is successful during the prepayment retention period or after the Retain Allowed Prepayment End Date is passed. So if the ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set’ flag is set as  ‘3-Indefinite Period’ then the flag should not be reset on prepayment transaction and in batch it will not be reset as the end date is a high value date. The user if needs to change the flag value then has to invoke the RestAPI again with the new flag values.
The existing prepayment transaction should be enhanced to perform the resetting of the fields  ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ and ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ as mentioned above.
The two new loan fields ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ and ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ should be added to the current loan enquiry API (Get Basic Loan Details - GET /consumer-loan/{account-number}/account-basic-details) for the user to verify the value stamped by the system in the two fields.
Consider the example below.
In loan instrument level, 
“Prepayment Retention Applicable” = 1-Yes
“Prepayment Retention Applicable Period” (in working days) = 10
When user executes the new RestAPI ‘Prepayment Request with Retention’, say on Aug.25th, user will input ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ = 1-Yes, and ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ is calculated and stamped as 2023/9/7 (2023/8/25 + 10 working days).
If prepayment is performed after than Sep. 7th with threshold breach, then the transaction should fail with the error ‘Perform prepayment request with retention first’.
If prepayment is performed before Sep.7th, the transaction is continued, and if the transaction is successful, both ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set‘ and ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ should be reset.

For the new prepayment penalty method, the below penalty calculation should be used,
6: Penalty based on Period End Date with Interest Practice days: 
For this new penalty method, the Method 1 using below formula as detailed in section 2.3 above should be followed.
Exclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = prepayment amount * rate% * (prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment date)/Interest Practice
Inclusive:
Principal credit/prepayment penalty = [prepayment amount / (1 + {rate% * ((prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment date)/Interest Practice)})] * rate% * ((prepayment penalty period final end date – prepayment date) / Interest Practice)
Here,
Prepayment amount: Prepayment transaction amount
Prepayment penalty period final end date: It’s the end date of prepayment penalty period slab for the account. Also detailed in section 2.1 above, as the same is used for threshold checks also.
Prepayment date: Prepayment date as given in prepayment transaction or prepayment enquiry transaction.
Rate: Prepayment penalty rate is the rate as defined in the prepayment penalty period-based slab.
Interest Practice: Interest Practice refers to the number of days in a year set for the product for normal interest accruals calculation basis which could be 360 or 365 or actual.
If for an account this method is set, then on prepayment enquiry or prepayment transaction the prepayment penalty is computed as per the above formula and shown in enquiry and applied with the prepayment transaction. Sample computation is given in section 2.3 above.

Business Requirement 
Threshold Period and Amount check in Pre-closure/Early Settlement with Retention Period Processing <B2-028-1><B2-028-8><B2-028-12>
CTBC requires to set certain pre-closure threshold amounts and threshold periods validations for pre-closure processing of loans. 
Threshold Period:
On Pre-closure request or on enquiry with an effective date, CTBC requires to validate the remaining loan term from the effective date to the loan maturity date against a threshold which can be one of the below thresholds as set at the product level.
Pre-closure Allowed Terms: 
It’s the number of terms as installments which is validated against the remaining number of installments of loan term from the pre-closure request’s effective date. 
If set to be 3, then it means only when the account has three or less instalments left, the pre-closure can be done.
Pre-closure Allowed Tenure Ratio (%): 
Here the number of threshold term/installments left is arrived basis the percentage of total loan tenor in installments.
The validation required is like “Remaining loan terms <= Loan tenor * Pre-closure Allowed Tenure Ratio (always rounded up)
For example: 
Assuming a loan has total 72 terms (72 installments).
Pre-closure Allowed Tenure Ratio (%) = 10
The allowed remaining loan term to be computed as, 
 Loan tenor * Pre-closure Allowed Tenure Ratio = 72 *10% = 7.2 rounded up to 8
So remaining installments threshold is 8 and from the 64th installment term the pre-closure is allowed, as also depicted in the below table.
Loan current terms
Remaining loan terms
Allow Pre-closure or not
62
10
N
63
9
N
64
8
Y
65
7
Y
66
6
Y
Once the threshold period validation is successfully cleared then the threshold amount validation is to be done as given in the below point. If the threshold period validation fails, then retention period processing should be performed. The retention period processing is detailed in point after threshold amount validation point.
Threshold Amount:
After the threshold period checking is successfully cleared, the outstanding principal amount should be validated against defined threshold amounts. The below 2 threshold amounts are required to be set at the product level.
Maximum Threshold Pre-closure Amount
Minimum Threshold Pre-closure Amount
If the outstanding principal balance is greater than the ‘Maximum Threshold’ then retention period processing should be performed.
If the outstanding principal balance is less than or equal to ‘Minimum Threshold’ then pre-closure transaction should continue the closure processing.
If the outstanding principal balance is less than or equal to the ‘Maximum Threshold’ and greater than the ‘Minimum Threshold’ then the transaction should be sent for supervisor override for checker approval. If approved, then pre-closure transaction should continue the closure processing else the processing should be stopped returning an error.
Retention Period Processing:
CTBC requires as part of the retention period processing to set a pre-closure retention applicable period at loan product. The customer requests for the pre-closure and after the pre-closure request is accepted, the customer is allowed to do the pre-closure within the pre-closure retention applicable period and thereafter it should be disallowed, and a new request should be raised.
The pre-closure retention applicable period in working days needs to be defined at loan product. When the customer requests for a pre-closure via call centre or branch the request is to be taken and basis the period defined at the product the pre-closure allowed retention end date should be set at the loan account and validated.
Once the end date is set, and then, when the pre-closure request or enquiry is done on the loan, then first the threshold period and threshold amount is checked as detailed in above paragraphs and where it’s said to check the retention period processing the accounts pre-closure allowed retention end date is checked if the transaction date has crossed the pre-closure allowed retention end date, if so then error is returned and pre-closure request or enquiry is failed else the pre-closure request or enquiry is processed.
The overall high-level flow is given below for reference.
New Pre-closure/Early Settlement Penalty Computation method <B2-028-2><B2-028-3>
CTBC requires to have new pre-closure/early settlement penalty computation methods in addition to the localized pre-closure/early settlement penalty methods.
The new methods should use the below formulas,
Pre-closure penalty = Outstanding Principal Balance * penalty% * ((Penalty Period Final End Date – Pre-closure effective date) / Interest Practice 
Pre-closure penalty based on accounts saved schedule balance.
The rate here is the localized pre-closure penalty rate set basis period tier. 
Interest Practice refers to the number of days in a year set for the product for normal interest accruals which could be 360 or 365 or actual.
Penalty Period Final End Date is the end date of the last pre-closure penalty slab for the account. 
That is, with localization the new method to compute pre-closure penalty in amount or percentage rate, basis period-based slab was developed as per below sample. 
Period From
Period To
%
Amount
0 months
3 Months
5
3 months
6 Months
3
6 months
9 Months
2
Here the pre-closure Penalty Period Final End Date is the date of 9months post first disbursement date for the above sample case.
For example,
Say the outstanding principal amount is 50000 NTD,
Loan disbursement date is 1Jan2023,
Loan Penalty Period Final End Date is 30Sep2023,
Pre-closure effective date is 10Jan2023,
Pre-closure rate tier is set as below for the new methods.
Penalty period from
Penalty period from
Pre-closure penalty rate
0 months

Then for the first 2 methods the penalty will be computed as below,
Method-1,
Pre-closure penalty = Outstanding Principal Balance * penalty% * ((Penalty Period Final End Date – Pre-closure effective date) / Interest Practice) 
When Interest Practice follows 365 days in a year
Pre-closure penalty = Outstanding Principal Balance * penalty% * ((Penalty Period Final End Date – Pre-closure effective date) / 365) 
= 50000 * 0.05 * ((30Sep2023 – 10Jan2023) / 365)
= 50000 * 0.05 * (263/ 365) 
= 50000 * 0.05 * 0.720548
= 1801(Rounded)
When Interest Practice follows 360 days in a year
Pre-closure penalty = Outstanding Principal Balance * penalty% * ((Penalty Period Final End Date – Pre-closure effective date) / 360) 
= 50000 * 0.05 * ((30Sep2023 – 10Jan2023) / 360)
= 50000 * 0.05 * (263/ 360) 
= 50000 * 0.05 * 0.730556
= 1826(Rounded)
Method-2,
As per this method the base of computing pre-closure penalty should be scheduled balance as per current date where the repayment schedule should be as of the latest disbursement date or latest pre-closure penalty rate update date when the Penalty Period Final End Date was changed, whichever is latest.
As we know, the repayment schedule is generated at disbursement, and it will change due to various reasons. For CTBC, for some accounts, they calculate the pre-closure penalty based on the saved repayment schedule generated at the time of 1st or latest disbursement or latest pre-closure penalty rate period slab’s update date whichever is latest instead of based on the most current repayment schedule.
A copy of the repayment schedule should be stored separately, so that the system can calculate the penalty amount based on the schedule that was saved.
Assume the table below is the copy that was stored, let’s call it Table A. If during the instalment of 16 period, the borrower comes to the bank to do pre-closure, then instead of using the loan accounts current repayment schedule, Table A’s principal balance will be used for penalty calculation. If today’s date is in the period of instalment 16, the principal amount to be used for calculation is 18,851,855 (from Table A) instead of current outstanding principal balance for this new pre-closure penalty method.
For CTBC business, with this new option system needs to support pre-closure enquiry to get the pre-closure penalty amount even after the loan account is discharged. 
The pre-closure penalty amount should be shown when doing the pre-closure enquiry, but the pre-closure penalty amount should not be included in the pre-closure amount. This pre-closure penalty amount will be collected later when loan borrower comes for the release certificate. So, the system should allow for enquiry for the penalty amount even after the loan account is discharged.
After the loan account is discharged, the pre-closure enquiry should show the penalty amount calculated with input dates and “the saved schedule”.
The formula used for calculating the penalty is “Saved schedule Amt” * penalty% where the “Saved schedule Amt” is the outstanding principal balance amount from “the saved schedule” as of the enquiry input date.
Once the user does the enquiry and gets the penalty amount, the penalty from the user will be collected manually through recollect transaction and issue the release certificate outside of GBP.

For the new prepayment penalty methods, the below penalty calculation should be used,
9: Penalty based on Period End Date with Interest Practice days: 
For this penalty method, the Method 1 formula as detailed in section 2.2 above should be followed.
Pre-closure penalty = Outstanding Principal Balance * penalty% * ((Penalty Period Final End Date – Pre-closure effective date) / Interest Practice)
Here,
Outstanding Principal Balance: It’s the outstanding principal of loan as of the pre-closure date
Pre-closure penalty period final end date: It’s the end date of pre-closure penalty period slab for the account. Also detailed in section 2.2 above. If this is computed beyond the loan maturity date, then maturity date should be considered.
Pre-closure effective date: Pre-closure date as given in pre-closure/early settlement transaction or pre-closure/early settlement enquiry transaction.
Rate: Pre-closure penalty rate is the rate as defined in the pre-closure penalty period-based slab.
Interest Practice: Interest Practice refers to the number of days in a year set for the product for normal interest accruals calculation basis which could be 360 or 365 or actual.
If for an account, this method is set, then on pre-closure enquiry or pre-closure transaction the pre-closure penalty is computed as per the above formula and shown in enquiry and applied with the pre-closure/early settlement transaction. Sample computation is given in section 2.2 above.
10: Penalty based on Saved Schedule Principal Outstanding:
For this penalty method the penalty is computed basis the outstanding schedule principal as of the pre-closure effective date derived from a saved repayment schedule. This is detailed in section 2.2 above.

Business Requirement 
Loan Account BSPL definition with Segment Code <B2-029-2>
CTBC requires to have the segment code stamped at the loan account, to be part of the loan accounts GL code/BSPL.
Segment code is added at loan account level as part of the FS – ‘NVBK_B2-019_放款帳戶建檔_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99’ with valid values as

This segment needs to be part of the account GL code (Account GLCC).
The earlier option in the RestAPI ‘Modify Loan Account Details’ to amend the segment code should not be allowed.
CTBC requires a separate option to change the loan segment code of a disbursed loan. 
The loan with unpaid dues, Interest Accrued, Penal Interest Accrued should be allowed to perform the segment code change. With segment code change the balance transfer entries should be generated for all the loan buckets including the interest accruals. This is required for loans in all currencies.

Prepayment without Installment and Term Change <B2-029-16>
CTBC requires to have the option for loan prepayment function, not to recalculate installment amount or change the loan remaining term. With no change to installment and remaining term only the last installment should be adjusted.
Further when the customer requests the bank, the loan needs to be rescheduled with a new installment effective from the immediate next installment after current application date. 
This is required only for loans with installment type “EI-Equated Monthly Installment” and “Equal-Equated Principal Installment”.
The loan reschedule option in such cases should have the option to simulate and show the old and new repayment schedule with the respective installments. Further on user confirmation the new schedule should be rebuilt and made effective for the loan. The new installment should be stamped from the immediate next installment after the reschedule transactions application date.

Proposed Solution
For the new requirements as detailed in section 2 above following enhancements are required to be done.
Loan Account BSPL definition with Segment Code <B2-029-2>
The current BSPL definition should be enhanced to include the loan accounts segment code which can be,
1: Consumer Banking 
2: Corporate Banking 
3: SBG
The field is added as part of the FS – ‘NVBK_B2-019_放款帳戶建檔_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99’.
The current RestAPI ‘Create Bspl Code’ should be enhanced to have its current attribute ‘noga_grp' to have a new value to define the loan accounts segment code.

The existing business domain

2: Corporate Banking

Thus, for a loan the BSPL should be formed with the new attribute of loan segment code. On definition of BSPL for a loan instrument thus 3 BSPL’s should be defined with each of the segment codes (1-Consumer,2-Corporate and 3-SBG).
In loan creation RestAPI’s, it should be checked that for the loan segment code given in creation there is the BSPL with the given loan segment code created, else error should be returned as ‘BSPL yet to be defined’. 
Say, for a loan with segment code 1 (Consumer Banking), the balance components should be defined with this loan segment in addition to its existing BSPL attributes.  
Consider the loan with outstanding principal balance of 1000 TWD, and its attributes as,
Principal CGL - 100001
Branch Code- 101
Segment Code- 1
Currency- TWD
Then the BSPL or CGL/GL code for the principal bucket of the loan account should be,
Principal – 101-TWD-100001-1
Similarly, each of the loan buckets BSPL should have this loan accounts segment code, if it’s defined with the new Noga Group.
A new RestAPI should be developed for changing the loan/LOC accounts segment code. 
The earlier option in the RestAPI ‘Modify Loan Account Details’ to amend the segment code should not be allowed (Part of FS-B2-019). A new error ‘Segment code change to be done via segment code switch option’ should be returned if segment code change is tried using the loan modify RestAPI.
The new POST RestAPI ‘Create Loan Segment Switch Request’ should be developed with the below input. This should be applicable for LOC accounts also for segment change.

The processing of RestAPI should follow the below steps,
Step-1:
Validate that the ‘Old Segment Code’ entered and the existing segment at the loan account is same, else error to be returned as ‘Incorrect Old Segment Code entered’.
Validate that the ‘New Segment Code’ given has the loan BSPL created for the loan account’s product with the new segment code value, else error to be returned as ‘BSPL yet to be defined’.
Validate that the ‘New Segment Code’ given and the existing segment at the loan account are not same, else error to be returned as ‘New Segment Code given is already stamped at the loan account’.
Validate if the account in which the segment code change transaction is performed is not written off either partial or full else return the error as ‘Segment code change not allowed in written off accounts’.
Step-2:
Stamp the new segment code value to the loan account and check the bucket wise balance of the loan account to generate balance transfer entries.
With the loan segment code as 1 and if the loan principal bucket was stamped as 101-TWD-100001-1 then if its changed as 3 then the new GL should be 101-TWD-100001-3.
Step-3: Generate Accounting entries.

Also, the balance transfer in case of NPA loan should transfer the balance of all components including the interest suspense component.
The above changes are applicable for loans of all currencies and hence this should be developed considering any currency and not just TWD only.
Prepayment without Installment and Term Change <B2-029-16>
CTBC for its loans with installment type as “EI-Equated Monthly Installment” and “Equal-Equated Principal Installment” wants to keep the installment amount and remaining term same after performing prepayment. 
The change to be made, if term and installment is to be constant is at the last installment. 
Further if there is a reduction of term due to higher amount of prepayment then the original maturity date should be stamped so that when the customer comes to reschedule then the original maturity date can be referred to set the new installment basis original loan term.
The current loan parameter ‘Regeneration Option’ should be enhanced to have a new domain value as ‘Last Installment Change’.
Sl.No.
Attribute Name
Description
O/M

1
Regeneration Option
(LOAN_FI_DETAIL - EI_REGEN_OPTN)
This is a current loan parameter to define how the repayment schedule should be regenerated on rate change or prepayment or repay day change etc.
In addition to the existing values to change tenure and installment a new value is added to change only the last installment and keep the installment same.
The existing business domain d_EIRegenOption needs to be extended with below value
5: Last Installment Change (New Value)
M
Varchar2 (3)
This same option should be added in the current ‘Reschedule Loan’ RestAPI in its field ‘regeneration-option’ having the same domain ‘d_EIRegenOption’. So, with this new option the current reschedule RestAPI should be enhanced to change only the last installment and keep the installment and tenure the same.
With the change in last installment only if the prepayment amount is high then the last installment may not be required as the principal will end before the original maturity date.
Hence its required to store in such cases the previous maturity date at account level so that when the customer comes to change the installment then the tenure as per previous maturity date can be used to arrive at the new installment amount and rebuild the repayment schedule.
So, consider the below case,
On loan creation with the new regeneration option parameter value of ‘5 – Last Installment Change’.
After prepayment of 10000 and normal installment payment on 1-Mar-2023 the repayment schedule should be regenerated as below.
Please note that here only the last installment has changed, the installment amount and the total tenure has remained the same.
Now say instead of 10000 the prepayment amount was done on 17000 then the repayment schedule should be regenerated as below as marked in blue below,
Here the last installment has moved before by one month (1-Jun-23) from the original last installment date or maturity date of 1-Jul-2023.
Hence the previous maturity date should be stamped at the loan account as a separate field. For this a new field should be added at the loan account level called as the ‘Original Maturity date’.
A new task needs to be developed to support the update of the field “Original Maturity Date”:
At the time of creation of the loan account 
At the time of reschedule action on the loan account
At the time of modification of the loan tenure
At the time of roll over of the loan
No other task can update this field value.

1

This new field should be stamped on first disbursement of loan basis the original term and last installment date arrived or the maturity date given by user in certain cases of loans.
Further this should be updated only when the loan is rescheduled or on modify tenure with increase/decrease in tenure or on rollover.
M

To be defined using existing domain 
d_date 
With the original maturity date stamped at the loan account level, on prepayment even if the last installment is before the original maturity date, the original maturity date should not be changed. The same should be followed in case of interest rate change and repay day change. This specific processing should be done when the loan product’s ‘Regeneration Option’ is set with the new option of ‘5 – Last Installment Change’.
Further for such accounts when the customer comes back after the prepayment to change his installment then the current reschedule transaction should be used to arrive at the new installment basis the remaining term till the original maturity date stamped at the loan.

Business Requirement 
Backdated Rate change during Subsidy Period <B2-030-1>
CTBC requires to have the option for backdated interest rate change for its loan under a subsidy program during the subsidy effective period.
The bank user should have the option to amend interest details for the loan account and the effective from date can be earlier than system date. And based on the input, system is required to recalculate the interest amount (both capitalized interest and accrued interest) based on the modified interest details and also record the new interest break downs and generate relevant accounting entries.
The backdated interest rate change is allowed till the last financial transaction date only. 
With the backdated interest rate change the running months subsidy interest accrual is also to be recomputed. 
For example, if today is Dec. 19th, and the backdate rate change effective date is Nov. 20th, then in this case, the account rate is updated with new rate from Nov. 20th to current date. But since subsidy for November is already calculated in November EOM, it is not to be impacted. For December subsidy amount, it is calculated at EOM of December. At the December EOM, the batch job that calculates the subsidy amount should calculate from Dec. 1st to Dec. 31st basis the actual rates.
Subsidy Interest Calculator <B2-030-5>
CTBC requires to have the option to compute the Subsidy interest for a loan account for a given period and rate, basis the loan account balance.
This is for the cases where an account is disqualified for the subsidy project or there may be some changes to the subsidy project; however, due to government procedures, it is possible that the bank receives such information late. 
For example, an account is disqualified on July 20th 2023, but the bank may receive this information on Aug. 5th 2023. And the bank would have already calculated the loan account’s subsidy amount and accrued normal interest at a lower rate for the month of July by 5th Aug. In such cases the bank wants to collect back the interest, which was given as part of subsidy, from July 20th 2023 to Aug 5th 2023 as the borrower was not eligible for subsidy and he was disqualified. For this the bank wants a new enquiry transaction to know what the subsidy amount for the period elapsed basis the new rate.
The inputs for the new enquiry should be the loan account number, from date and to date, and an intended rate (Index Rate & margin). With these inputs, the system is required to calculate the amount based on account’s principal history balance and the index rate references as per the input given. The output of the enquiry should show the old and new interest computation results for the user to check and collect.

From Date: 2023/7/20
To Date: 2023/7/31
Intended Rate Index: LIBOR – 1M
Margin: +0.2%

Assuming account level interest rate for the month of July is 2%.
Assuming the Index rates of LIBOR-1M is,
2% from July 15th

Proposed Solution
For the 2 requirements detailed in section 2 above, following enhancements are required to be done.
Backdated Rate change during Subsidy Period <B2-030-1>
For the backdated change of account level interest rate during the subsidy period the two accruals of debit interest and subsidy should be recalculated.
On change of interest rate at account level current processing of localized backdated account level interest rate change should be enhanced to recompute interest even with the subsidy record tagged with the account. For a loan account which is under an active subsidy project, with a backdated ‘valid from date’ request in ‘Modify Interest Conditions‘ RestAPI the debit interest is to be recalculated from the valid from date to current date and the accrual should be updated as per the localization. Further basis the subsidy project code tagged to the loan account the subsidy accrual for the current running month should also be updated. The localized subsidy accrual job should read for any backdated rate change done in the loan and for those in the subsidy accrual the changed account rate should be considered for computing the running months subsidy accrual. The new subsidy rate should be arrived as the Bank rate minus the new loan account rate. 
The backdated account level interest rate change should be allowed till the last financial transaction in the account as per the localization. If the effective backdating is beyond the last financial transaction, then the error should be returned as “Backdating allowed till last financial transaction only”. The localized subsidy accrual job should be enhanced to read for any backdated account level interest rate change and process with the new subsidy rate (Bank Rate – new account rate) in the enhanced localized subsidy accrual job.

Business Requirement 
Stop Repayment for certain Debt Negotiation Type plus Stage <B2-032-6>
CTBC for its loan under debt negotiation plan stamped with certain type and stage does not want to allow any repayment through any channel or interface.
For example, the condition could be like below,
Negotiation Type 
Negotiation Stage 
Repayment allowed 
NG
Apply
Yes
NG
Start of negotiation
No
NG 
Under regular repayment 
No
NG

Yes
Till the type and stage is not changed the repayment to the loan should not be allowed and after the type and stage is changed the repayment can continue.
This is in addition to the actions tagged with the debt negotiation type and stage. 
Enhanced Auto Debit Processing for Debt Negotiated Loan <B2-032-7>
For a borrower under debt negotiation plan who has multiple loans across multiple banks in Taiwan, the bank which has the maximum outstanding balance becomes the lead creditor for the borrower and all the payments are first collected by this bank.
Consider the case where the borrower has unpaid dues from 3 banks as given below,
     Bank X: Total unpaid balance=  500,000 
     Bank Y: Total unpaid balance=   200,000
     Bank Z: Total unpaid balance=1,000,000
The Borrower would first apply to the creditor (the creditor with the maximum total unpaid balance) for debt negotiation, in this case, that will be Bank Z.
Bank Z will then inform all creditors via JCIC on the settlement amount and their share of unpaid balance to be collected.
If CTBC is the creditor that borrowers are applying to, the borrower must start to repay his/her installment to CTBC’s specific account from negotiated start date, currently CTBC provides a virtual account to the borrower, a combination of 3-digit integer + identification no, the borrower need to deposit negotiated installment to this virtual account.
Thereafter the debt negotiation platform which is an external system transfers the negotiated installment received to internal CASA and external bank’s accounts. From the internal CASA its paid to the CTBC’s loans.
At CTBC to collect the negotiated installment to virtual account auto debits/standing instructions are set from internal CASA and via ACH mandate to collect from other banks.

The current localized debt negotiation type and stage record having the debt negotiation type and stage along with the actions should be enhanced to have a new attribute to define whether to stop any repayment in the loan marked under debt negotiation with the said type and stage. The definition of debit negotiation type and stage and the actions applicable for them is covered in the 1.2 gaps localization.

Thus, for the loan account under the negotiation type ‘NG’ and stage ‘AA’ the parameter could be set with the new attribute ‘Allow Repayment’ as 2-No then no online or batch repayment should be allowed in the loan. 
All the loan repayment RestAPI’s should be enhanced to validate that if the loan is under debt negotiation plan if their negotiation type and stage is set with ‘Allow Repayment’ as 2-No then the execution should fail with the error ‘Loan under Negotiation Plan does not allow repayment’. 
Enhanced Auto Debit Processing for Debt Negotiated Loan <B2-032-7>
For collection of the consolidated debt negotiated loans total repayment for a customer, a designated virtual account should be created. The virtual account creation using borrower’s customer ID will be covered under the SSR B32-061.
The ACH repayment option customized as part of the SSR B2-025 for 1.2 and 1.3 gaps should be further enhanced to collect the capture and collect the ACH repayment for the virtual account instead of loans. The virtual account number should be used for recording and processing of the ACH repayment. The batch jobs should be enhanced to process for virtual account also in addition to loan accounts. The amount for payment should be user input as per the debt negotiation external platform. The capture and processing of settlement instruction for this enhanced ACH collection for virtual accounts can be done under Loans or CCP microservices which will be taken up during development.   
When the repayment is to be collected from the bank’s internal CASA and credited to the Virtual account, it should be recorded as a collection record from internal CASA to virtual account as a standing order. The below RestAPI’s should be enhanced to have virtual accounts as its credit account.

Business Requirement 
Exclude Term Validation on Rollover for Corporate Loans <B2-033-6>
CTBC requires to have an exception for the validation of loan tenor against loan instrument’s Maximum Loan Period and Minimum Loan Period on rollover for its corporate loan’s basis certain conditions.
For corporate loan’s having their segment code as ‘2: Corporate Banking’ or ‘3: SBG’ and attached to a facility limit, the validation of loan instrument’s Maximum Loan Period and Minimum Loan Period should be skipped and validated against the limit level “Rollover Loan Tenure” value on capturing and executing the loan rollover instruction.
The limit attribute “Rollover Loan Tenure” is being added as part of limits. Even on exceeding the limit level “Rollover Loan Tenure” value the rollover should be recorded with a supervisor overridable warning.
Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-033 Rollover
Existing Functionality

Proposed Solution
For the requirement given in section 2 above, the below enhancements are required to be made.
Exclude Term Validation on Rollover for Corporate Loans <B2-033-6>
The current rollover request (RestAPI-Loan Rollover Request) should be enhanced to perform 2 checks of product term validation for its corporate loans and also validate against a maximum loan rollover term set on their limits.
The maximum period ‘Rollover Loan Tenure‘ for loan rollover is defined as part of limits under the SSR B2-002.
The RestAPI-Loan Rollover Request and its approval should first check if the loan accounts segment code is 2 or 3 (Corporate Banking or SBG) and check if it has a limit. 
If it’s not, then continue with the current processing of loan’s product level minimum and maximum term check.
If it is, then first check the total loan term for product level minimum and maximum and then whether passed or failed check with the ‘Rollover Loan Tenure’ defined at the loans linked primary limit, if any of these 2 conditions fail then an overridable warning should be returned as ‘Exceeds maximum term for rollover’.

Business Requirement 
Overdraft Closure Enhancements <B2-035-4><B2-036-10><B2-035-10><B2-035-11>
With overdraft loan account linked to a CASA, and approved amount at Overdraft loan account added to CASA’s available balance. CTBC wants an Overdraft Closure Indicator flag at the overdraft loan account. This field is already added as part of the FS- NVBK_B2-019_放款帳戶建檔_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99.
Overdraft closure using Overdraft Closure Indicator flag <B2-035-4><B2-036-10>:
Borrower informs CTBC that he/she wants to close the Overdraft loan Account and will get the closure amount using the closure enquiry.
Then the teller will modify the Overdraft Closure Indicator at the overdraft loan Account level as Yes.
Once the above field is modified as Yes, the system must subtract approved amount of overdraft loan Account from Overdraft Limit at CASA basis overdraft loan product flag. Based on this overdraft loan product flag the OD CASA limit should be reduced. At CTBC for interest compounding overdraft loans the limit should be reduced and for simple interest overdraft loan the limit should not be reduced.
In BOD batch on the subsequent day:
If the Overdraft Closure Indicator @Overdraft Account level = Yes, and system should close the overdraft loan account using the funds deposited in the OD CASA in next day BOD. 
If funds are unavailable in the OD CASA, then the closure should be tried the next day if the Overdraft Closure Indicator is still Yes, if user updates it to be “No” then Overdraft Limit at CASA should be reverted using the loans approved amount and then no more closure should be tried.
For example:
If the CASA is linked with two overdraft loan accounts, with approved amount of 200,000 and 300,000

Additional Validation for Overdraft closure <B2-035-10>:
CTBC wants additional validation for its overdraft loan accounts on performing closure transaction.
To proceed with closure transaction of an overdraft loan account, the below fields at account level must be “Yes”, if not then error message should be returned.

Overdraft Closure Indicator 
This is referred in FS- NVBK_B2-019_放款帳戶建檔_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99 as per below extract and in this FS its processing is detailed as given in the above point and in section 3.1.2. 
Correction of Overdraft loan account closure <B2-035-11>:
CTBC wants the overdraft loan account’s closure status to be reverted after the closure date on any subsequent day after EOD within a specified period set for the loan product.
In effect a Closed Overdraft loan Account can be reopened.
A new function is required to revert the account status from closed to active or expired with its previous approved amount.
If this account status is modified as “Expired”, then this account should allow to perform an additional Extension/Rollover.
Then tellers should be allowed to perform the linkage “Overdraft loan account + OD CASA” manually.
E.g.
If predefined period for closure correction is set as 3 months.
If closure date is on 2024-05-20, then this account is allowed to be reopened till 2024-08-20, otherwise the system must return error (from 2024-08-21).

The current localized OD minimum repayment due computation should be enhanced with additional processing and validations. The enhancements of interest compounding OD loan and those not compounding are different so should be first OD minimum repayment due should be computed as per the localization process thereafter the below additional processing should be done. 
Interest Compounding OD loans:
For interest compounding OD loans (product interest calculation basis = Principal and Interest), 
the OD loans principal plus debit interest outstanding as on the minimum repay due date (capitalization date) should be compared with the ‘OD Minimum Repay Threshold’ defined at the product level, 
If the threshold is higher, then no minimum repayment due should be applied.
Else the computed OD minimum repayment due should be compared with the OD excess amount (overdrawn amount over the OD limit)
If OD excess amount is higher, then it should be taken as OD minimum repayment due
Else the computed OD minimum repayment due should be taken as OD minimum repayment due.
The OD minimum repayment due thus computed should be round down to nearest parameter value basis the new parameter ‘OD Minimum Repay due Round down Value’ set.
The final minimum repayment due should be above OD Minimum Repay due plus other loan dues (like Charges or excess amount) for the OD loan. This should be applied on the interest repay date.
Simple Interest OD loans without interest compounding:
For simple interest OD loans without interest compounding (product interest calculation basis = Principal), the computed OD minimum repay due amount as per localization as of the due date (capitalization date) should be compared with the ‘OD Minimum Repay Floor’ value defined at the product level, 
If the ‘OD Minimum Repay Floor’ is lower, computed OD minimum repayment due should be taken as OD minimum repayment due.
If the ‘OD Minimum Repay Floor’ is higher, then OD loans principal outstanding is compared with the ‘OD Minimum Repay Floor’, 
if ‘OD Minimum Repay Floor’ is higher, then principal outstanding is first checked if it’s 0 and accrued interest is greater than 0, then accrued interest should be taken as OD minimum repayment due,
else principal outstanding should be taken as the OD minimum repayment due.
The OD minimum repayment due thus arrived should be round down to nearest parameter value basis the new parameter ‘OD Minimum Repay due Round down Value’ set.
The final minimum repayment due should be above OD Minimum Repay due plus other loan dues (like Charges or excess amount) for the OD loan. This should be applied on the interest repay date.
Detailed examples are given in section 2.2 for reference.
The localized batch job for stamping and raising the OD minimum repayment due should be enhanced to do the above processing.

Simple Interest Overdraft Processing with Online Reshuffle <B2-036-1><B2-036-6><B2-036-7>
CTBC requires online reshuffle for its Overdraft accounts in addition to the batch reshuffle. The batch reshuffle of simple interest overdrafts is only required for OD closure.
The online reshuffle is applicable only for overdrafts without interest compounding (Simple Interest) and having a one-to-one relationship between OD CASA and OD loan. Simple interest overdrafts will be always a one-to-one OD CASA and OD loan linked overdrafts.
Following processing are required for Simple Interest Overdraft,
Online Reshuffle(B2-036-1):
With the online transaction in the OD CASA, system should invoke the corresponding transaction in linked OD loan.
For example:

Payment due date = 5/16

The ‘Auto Debit’ in this gap is expected to fire existing transaction of CASA to CASA transfer, then in online reshuffle the OD loan is repaid.

Repay Day Change in OD Loan <B2-036-11>
The localized function to change OD repay day using the OD CASA account should be further enhanced for simple interest OD accounts to get the linked OD loan and then use the current reschedule RestAPI ‘Reschedule Loan by changing repayment details’ to change repay day of OD loan. Additional validations should be done on performing change of repay day in the linked simple interest OD loans having one to one linkage with its OD CASA.
It should not be allowed if there are any outstanding dues in OD loan or DPD > 0.
If the validation fails, then error should be returned as ‘Repay Day change not allowed with OD loan in arrears’.
If the validation is passed, then OD loan’s next capitalization date and the payment due dates should be updated as per the new repay day.
Sample case is given in section 2.4 above for reference. 
Auto Debit and Chasing in OD Loan <B2-036-15>
The current auto debit job ‘CR9009-Auto Repay’ should be enhanced for minimum repayment due recovery for OD loans with below additional features,
This ‘Auto debit’ enhanced processing should be done for simple interest OD loans with one-to-one linkage to OD CASA as covered in the point B2-036-3 of section 2.2 above.
To be done only if the settlement account belong to primary borrower of OD loan and the settlement account is not linked to the OD CASA for any sweeps.
Auto debit should start from the payment due date.
Auto chasing is also required if an account is in arrears, chase days at OD loan product level should be allowed to be defined in the existing field of loan product.
The unpaid minimum due amount should be used for ‘Auto debit’ recovery and chasing in full.
The ‘Auto Debit’ should fire the existing transaction of CASA (Settlement Account) to OD CASA transfer, then in online reshuffle the OD loan should be repaid.
The ‘Auto debit’ should only happen when the settlement account has funds to repay the full unpaid minimum due amount.
When the overdraft loan accounts turn NPL or written-off, the ‘Auto debit’ should be continued on daily basis. On NPA the overdraft loan accounts are delinked from OD CASA, and subsequent ‘Auto debit’ should follow the customization processing as per the gap reference B2-046-8 (FS - NVBK_B2-046_轉呆_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99).

FSD-B2-038.text:
Business Requirement 
Discounted Loan Term basis days in transit <B2-038-2>
CTBC requires to have a new field at loan account level for discounted loans to define a negotiation period for its export bills (transit period for bill to reach importers bank) within the total discounted loan term. 
Say with the new field as “Transit Interest Period” the upfront interest and term should be computed as below,
Disbursed amount = 10,000,000
Interest rate = 1.2%
Loan tenure = 42 days (2023/12/1 ~ 2024/1/12)
Case 1:
Transit Interest Period is not entered.
Discount Interest Period = loan tenure 
Interest amount of Transit Interest Period = 0
Interest amount of Discount Interest Period = round (10,000,000 * 1.2% * 42 / 365,0) = 13,808
Total upfront interest = 0 + 13808 = 13808
Case 2:
Transit Interest Period = 10
Discount Interest Period = 42 – 10 = 32 
Interest amount of Transit Interest Period = round (10,000,000 * 1.2% * 10 / 365,0) = 3,288
Interest amount of Discount Interest Period = round (10,000,000 * 1.2% * 32 / 365,0) = 10,521
Total upfront interest = 3288 + 10521 = 13809
Considering the above case new fields should be added in the loan enquiry to show the below values,
Transit Interest Period
Interest amount of Transit Interest Period
Discount Interest Period
Interest amount of Discount Interest Period
Refund and Recollect Interest Enquiry in Discounted loan <B2-038-3>
CTBC requires to have the option for additional interest collection and interest rebate for its discounted loans owing to discounted loans term change. 
A new loan enquiry is required to compute interest amount basis the new term details entered for an active discounted loan. Basis the new term the interest should be computed and shown, the excess or short interest to be collected or refunded will be done via the Interest recollect and refund option (B2-027 SSR). The interest recollect and refund transaction is required to be done for discounted loans also.
Example:
For a loan say,
Approved/Disbursed amount = 100,000
Interest rate = 3%
Credit start date ~ Maturity date = 2024/4/1 ~ 2024/7/1
Upfront interest = 100,000 * 3% / 365 * 91 = 748 (rounded)
For the new enquiry:
Case 1: (Case for interest refund)
Input: 2024/6/20~2024/7/1 
Output: 100,000 * 3% / 365 * 11 = 90 (rounded)
Then CTBC will manually perform the Refund transaction, return 90 dollars to the borrower.
Case 2: (Case for interest recollect)
Input: 2024/7/1~2024/7/12 
Output: 100,000 * 3% / 365 * 11 = 90 (rounded)
Then CTBC will manually perform the Recollect transaction, collect 90 dollars from the borrower.
Solution Analysis

The above list is as per the current API catalogue which will get further enhanced basis the updated catalogues.
Proposed Solution
For the new requirements as detailed in section 2 above following enhancements are required to be made.
Discounted Loan Term basis days in transit <B2-038-2>
The current loan creation RestAPI ‘Create Loan Account’ should be enhanced to add a new attribute ‘Transit Interest Period’ to capture the transit period.

Description
O/M

The field will take the input in days for the discounted loan for trade to specify the transit period days.
O

This attribute should be applicable for only discounted loan products having the localized interest due method of ‘Discount with gross disbursement’.
If loan creation is tried for any other product with value in this new field ‘Transit Interest Period’ then error should be returned as ‘Applicable only for discounted loans with gross disbursement’.
For the discounted loan with gross disbursement with term specified for ‘Transit Interest Period’:
Current loan tenor should be total loan period inclusive of days given in ‘Transit Interest Period’. 
The loan tenor should be always in days, else error should be returned as ‘Tenor should be in days for discounted loan with gross disbursement’.
The upfront interest should be computed in two parts first the upfront interest for ‘Transit Interest Period’ should be computed and rounded and then the upfront interest for the remaining period should be computed and rounded separately and then both the upfront interest should be added to arrive at the total upfront interest for the discounted loan. During interest calculation, decimal places should be kept at least for 7 decimal places and then rounded as per the currency. Sample computation given in section 2.1 case 2 above.
This way the total upfront interest will be more due to split in tenure and computing upfront interest for the two periods separately with rounding each time. This is shown in section 2.1 - Case 1 and Case 2 above. The total upfront interest thus will be higher and so any residual upfront unearned interest should be amortized on maturity.
The current loan enquiry RestAPI ‘Loan Account details’ should be enhanced to have the below new attributes to display additional details for discounted loan.

Number (21,7)
These fields should be added at loan account level and stamped with creation and disbursement. 
These fields should be in addition to the Total Upfront Interest field and the Unearned Interest field. The total upfront interest should be the sum of Transit Period Interest and Discount Period Interest. The unearned interest should be the remaining interest to be amortized.

The processing of recollect and refund transaction in discounted loan should same as in the normal loans as per localization(B2-027_04).

Business Requirement 
Adhoc Fee with Amortization for Limits <B2-039-1><B2-039-5><B2-039-6>
In addition to the current process of charging adhoc charges on Loans, CTBC wants to charge adhoc charges with limit reference. The fee is debited to the CASA/Internal account, system should allow to specify the limit ID on behalf of which the fee is getting charged.
The fee charged should be recorded with the limit and a new inquiry must be made available where all the Adhoc Charge transactions on a limit ID must be listed. That is, it must include all charge transactions fired on CASA accounts / Internal accounts or collected as Cash, with the limit ID linkage given.
When this Adhoc charge transaction with limit ID is performed, the accounting entry of debit side should record on limit branch for Internal Account and for the credit side of amortizable income account. The limit branch is covered as part of the localization (B2-002-3).
If the limit branch ID is modified to another branch, the unamortized fee income should be transferred to the new branch using balance transfer entries. The accounting of the unamortized amount should thereafter happen in the new branch in EOD batch. 
If the limit is closed, the unamortized amount under the Limit ID must be recognized as income on the given day as below:
  If Charge item is defined as “Monthly amortization” => on EOM 
  If Charge item is defined as “Daily amortization” => on the same day EOD (closure day)
Adhoc Fee with Daily Amortization and Additional Validations <B2-039-2><B2-039-3><B2-039-4>
CTBC wants daily amortization for its loans adhoc fee and additional validation for its amortization start and end dates. 
Daily Amortization of Adhoc Fee <B2-039-3> 
As part of localization, the amortization for the loan adhoc fee is done on EOM.
CTBC wanted to have an option to amortize the loan adhoc fee as a daily process for some charges and rest to have monthly amortization.
It will be like:
Loan charge item 5001: Monthly amortization
Loan charge item 5002: Daily amortization
For example:

Amortization End Date= 2024/7/25

Amortization Start Date is allowed to be entered as a back date or a future date.
Back date:
The past days amortization must be included on the first amortization day.
Future date:
The first amortization is required to happen on when,
system date = user input future start date (Daily amortization) 
or

Additional Validation on Amortization Start and End Date<B2-039-2> 
CTBC requires to capture amortization start and end date with some additional validations for amortizable and non-amortizable fees.
If the selected fee is a non-amortizable fee
Amortization Start Date and Amortization End Date are allowed to be entered, and Amortization End Date must be higher than the start date.
Also, below scenario is allowed for backdated start and end date:
Amortization Start Date < system date and 
Amortization End Date <= system date
If the selected fee is an amortizable fee
Below scenario is not allowed:
Amortization Start Date < system date and 
Amortization End Date <= system date
Syndication Contract Creation and Maintenance <B2-039-7>
CTBC’s requires to capture details of its syndication loans contract details by using limits. Facility limits are created for the portion of leading bank and participating bank. The syndication contract master data is captured along with limit numbers of the leading bank and participating bank with their participation percentage in the syndication. 
The data is captured and maintained manually. The information captured is used by the downstream/report system and then reported to JCIC.

Backdated and Future dated fee amortization <B2-039-4>:
The localized adhoc charging transaction RestAPI ‘Create Adhoc Charges’ should be enhanced to accept backdated and future date in the field ‘Amrtz Start Date’.
When ‘Amrtz Start Date’ is backdated the amortization job should amortize the fee for past period on the first amortization day as per the frequency set.
When ‘Amrtz Start Date’ is future dated the amortization job should start amortization when system date reaches the amortization start date for daily amortization fee and on end of month after the start date for monthly amortization fees.
The detailed examples of amortization are given in section 2.2 above.
The backdated amortization start date should be accepted only when Amrtz Income Accounting is set to ‘Straight Line’ else error should be returned as ‘Backdated fee amortization is only applicable for straight line amortization’.

Disbursement Before Interest Repayment via Auto debit < B2-041-3>

should be enhanced to have the capitalized interest on the reverse mortgage loan to be repaid from the CASA account to which it was disbursed via auto debit.
If the disbursement day is the same as interest repay day, CTBC wants the system to do the disbursement prior to the loan repayment (auto debit), to make sure the settlement account has available balance for auto debit. Currently Interest capitalization happens in EOD and auto disbursement happens in BOD, thereafter the recovery for the interest due should be done for the reverse mortgage loans.

Minimum Net Payment and Enhanced Multi-Tranche Schedule for Reverse Mortgage <B2-041-5>
Minimum Net Payment:
CTBC wants to ensure that its borrowers of reverse mortgage should get a minimum percentage of the reverse mortgage disbursed amount after collecting the interest repayment.
To make sure the borrower will at least get a certain percentage of the disbursed amount for each month, the interest repayment amount for each installment must be under a threshold. (currently, disbursement amount / 3)
The common practice in Taiwan is one third (0.3333333), the percentage is required to be parameterized.
It means the borrowers need to pay the interest up to the maximum of one-third of the disbursed amount. The excess interest for any installment (Capitalized interest) is expected to be collected on loan account closure.
For example: 
With the threshold interest payment percentage at loan product level set to be 0.3333333 (One third)
In case the disbursed amount of the month is 30,000 then the interest payment thresholdis computed as 30,000 * 0.3333333 = 10,000 Rounded to an integer without decimals.
With the disbursement and interest repayment date being on the same day, if the capitalized interest amount is 12,000 more than the threshold of 10,000, then
Interest capitalization is expected to be as per the current processing 
DR: Interest receivable 12,000

The excess amount of 2,000 is not to be made due in the months installment in repayment schedule, it should be moved as new delayed interest payment due. Similar to the penal interest delay payment processing done in the localization (B2-025_08).
Interest Capitalized= 12,000

Delay payment due= 2,000
Delayed Interest Payment Due:
If the loan account is marked as NPA, this new bucket must be included as part of the NPL-I(Non Performing Interest bucket value).
For the loans which are not NPA the amount should be part of the another delayed debit interest bucket.
This new bucket must be included in Closure Enquiry / Closure Transaction.
Adjustment for this new bucket is also required.

Enhanced Multi-Tranche Disbursement Schedule:
CTBC requires the reverse mortgage disbursements to have multiple frequencies and needs the option to amend the disbursement schedule as described below,
Following frequencies of Monthly, Quarterly, Semiannually and Annually are required for reverse mortgage at CTBC.
While generating the disbursement schedule, each disbursement amount must be rounded up as integer and last disbursement amount should capture the remaining amount.
For example:

Log must be maintained for the disbursement schedule’s execution for success of if the auto-disbursement is failed, report system will capture this information to generate the necessary error report.
Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-041 Reverse Mortgage
Existing Functionality 
GBP supports the function of having disbursement schedule and auto debit for loan dues in its term loans.
