Proposed Solution
The disbursement schedule processing in GBP should be enhanced as below for the new requirements of reverse mortgage as detailed in section 2 above.
Disbursement Before Interest Repayment via Auto debit < B2-041-3>
CTBC requires to have the loan disbursement schedule to be created with loan creation and allowed to be modified subsequently for its reverse mortgage loan.
The loan disbursement schedule can be created with the disbursement types of Single Tranche or Multiple Tranche or Free Format.
The reverse mortgage loans will use the loan disbursement schedule with disbursement type as ‘Multiple Tranche’. With ‘Multiple Tranche’ the disbursement will be scheduled using the below frequency fields as in the RestAPI ‘Create Loan Account’(CLM-6)
disbursement-freq-unit- Disbursement frequency unit
disbursement-freq-prd- Disbursement frequency unit in number
number-of-tranches- Number of tranches as 1,2,3 etc.
disbursement-date- Date of 1st Disbursement
For automatic disbursement as per the disbursement schedule, a new attribute should be added to flag if auto disbursement is required for the loan accounts disbursement schedule.
Sl.No.
Attribute Name
Description
O/M
Data Type
1
Auto Disburse - Disbursement Schedule
The flag should define whether disbursement as per disbursement schedule should be done.
The existing domain d_YesNoFlg should be used with valid values of 
1:Yes
2:No(Default)
O
VarChar2(3)
This new flag should be added in the RestAPI’s,
Create Loan Account (in the node ‘disbursement-details’)
Basic Loan Details Modification (in the node ‘account-basic-details’)
With this flag set as ‘2:No’ the current processing of disbursement schedule should continue. When set as ‘1:Yes’, the auto disbursement should be done by the system using the current job of ‘1752’.
Job / Job Step
Job Name
EOD/ BOD/ Intraday
Module
 Details
1752
Execution of Future dated disbursement
BOD
CR
This batch is used for future dated disbursement. While creating disbursement from screen for future date this batch will pick that record and do the disbursement process and mark it as executed.
This current job 1752 should be enhanced to check the disbursement schedule if this new flag is set as ‘1:Yes’ and then schedule the disbursements as per the disbursement schedule. The disbursement schedule could be of free format or multi tranche or single tranche. During these auto disbursements all the validations of disbursement should be applied, and any failure should be reported in the disbursement status. A log must be maintained for the disbursement schedule’s execution for success or if the auto-disbursement is failed, report system will capture this information to generate the necessary error report.
The current RestAPI ‘GET Disbursement Schedule’ (CLM-89) should return the total disbursed and the amount to be disbursed and the status of each of the processed disbursement schedule records. The RestAPI ‘Loan Account Servicing Details’ (CLM-184) should also return the total disbursed and the amount to be disbursed.
With the reverse mortgage defined with disbursement schedule and automatic disbursement, the regular interest capitalized is required to be collected on the next day after capitalization as per the interest repay date. 
The job 10657 does the interest due raising in BOD for the interest capitalized on previous days EOD. 
Then, the enhanced job 1752 for auto disbursement should be done to credit the settlement accounts.
Thereafter in BOD the auto debit job CR9009 should be done to collect the interest dues from the settlement account as per the settlement instruction setup.
Thus, the disbursement of reverse mortgage will be done before the interest due collections in BOD, by sequencing these jobs one after other.
Minimum Net Payment and Enhanced Multi-Tranche Schedule for Reverse Mortgage <B2-041-5>
Minimum Net Payment:
In order to ensure that borrowers of reverse mortgage should get a minimum percentage of the disbursed amount after collecting the interest payment, a new loan product parameter attribute should be added as below to define the same.
Sl.No.
Attribute Name
Description
O/M
Data Type
1
Reverse Mortgage take home Percentage
The field defines the threshold percentage of the disbursement amount that can be made due for interest recoveries.
O
Numeric (3,5)
The percentage defined here should define the maximum interest due that can be raised for interest due. 
As like the example in given in section 2.2 for,
Scheduled disbursed amount: 30,000
Reverse Mortgage take home Percentage: 33.33333
Maximum Interest Due that can be raised: 30000 * (33.33333/100) = 10000 (Rounded to integer without decimals)
Now if the interest capitalized is 12000 then the interest due should be raised only for the max amount of 10000 and the remaining 2000 should be moved to the delayed interest bucket.
Validation should be added to check if this new parameter ‘Reverse Mortgage take home Percentage’ is less than 100%, else error should be returned as ‘Max take home percentage cannot be more than 100%’.
For this the current interest due raising job 10657 should be enhanced to check on this parameter if its set for a value greater than 0 and if the ‘Auto Disburse - Disbursement Schedule’ is set to ’Yes’ for the account with active disbursement schedule for the running repayment period for the loan. Then the job should check the interest capitalized that is to be made due is not more than the maximum interest due that can be raised. If it breaches the maximum amount, then the excess amount should be moved to the delayed interest bucket marked to be paid at the end of loan term. 
Similar to the localized function for delayed penal interest payment to be moved to loan maturity for payment, here the excess debit interest should be moved to a new delayed debit interest bucket and marked to be paid at loan maturity. The job 10657 should be enhanced to perform this. The excess interest due thus made due on maturity should be collected on loan closure similar to the delayed penal interest collection on closure.
The unpaid interest amount in delay dues must get included in the total account balance and total balance payable fields in settlement quote generation (RestAPI- Get Quote for Settlement Amount Payable by Closure Date - CLM-83). 
The amount must also be included to be paid as part of Settlement / Early Settlement processing (RestAPI- Create Early Settlement Request - CLM-77). 
If the loan account is marked as NPA, this new bucket must be included as part of the NPL-I(Non Performing Interest bucket value).
For the loans which are not NPA the amount should be part of the new delayed debit interest bucket.
Adjustment for this new bucket is also required for which the localized delayed bucket adjustment (RestAPI-Create Loan account adjustment - CLM-127) should be enhanced to adjust this excess debit interest part also.
Enhanced Multi-Tranche Disbursement Schedule:
For ‘Multiple Tranche’ disbursement schedule with the below disbursement frequency fields in the RestAPI ‘Create Loan Account’(CLM-6) the disbursement frequencies of Monthly, Quarterly, Semiannually and Annually should be supported.
disbursement-freq-unit- Disbursement frequency unit
disbursement-freq-prd- Disbursement frequency unit in number
number-of-tranches- Number of tranches as 1,2,3 etc.
disbursement-date- Date of 1st Disbursement
The disbursement schedule thus created should be with amounts for each disbursement to be rounded to integer without decimals and the last disbursement amount to be the remaining amount as detailed in section 2.2 in 2nd point.
The disbursement schedule created with loan creation for reverse mortgage would be till the end of loan term. When the loan term is extended via loan rescheduling, the disbursement schedule should also be amended. For this a new RestAPI ‘Modify Multi-Tranche Disbursement Details’ should be developed to amend the disbursement schedule with disbursement type as ‘Multiple Tranche’. 
Input:
The new PUT RestAPI with loan account number as path variable should have below input fields.

Attribute Name
Description
O/M
Data Type
1
Next Disbursement Date
The field should be user input to specify the Next disbursement date from when the new disbursement schedule should be generated. The date should be validated that it’s not back dated or of current date.
M
Date
2
Disbursement Frequency
The field is to specify the disbursement frequency to be followed for multi tranche.
The valid values as below can be used as per the existing domain ‘d_DisbFreq’
1 - Monthly
2 - Bimonthly
3 - Quarterly
4 - Semi annually
5 - Annually
M

The valid values can be 1 to 31. Where 31 should mean its end of month day.

The field is to specify the number of tranches/disbursements that are required for the multiple tranche disbursement.

Validation:
The following validations should be done in the new RestAPI,
System should validate that the ‘Next disbursement date’ given in input is in future and not on or after maturity date, else error should be returned as ‘Incorrect Next disbursement date’.
The system should validate the number of tranches and frequency with next disbursement date to ensure that the last disbursement on building the disbursement schedule is not going beyond or on the maturity date of the loan. Else error should be returned as ‘Disbursements cannot be on or after maturity date’.
Loan should have its disbursement schedule with disbursement type of multiple tranche or should be without any disbursement schedule else error should be returned as ‘Only Multiple Tranche Disbursements can be modified’.
For a loan with disbursement schedule, on modifying maturity date or loan tenure change via the loan reschedule option, system should validate the next disbursement date in the disbursement schedule is earlier than the new maturity date.
Processing:
The RestAPI processing should consider the history to be completed and should not be touched, then from the ‘Next Disbursement Date’ new disbursement schedule should be rebuilt as per the ‘Disbursement Frequency’ and ‘Number of Tranches’ given. From the ‘Next Disbursement Date’ it should be ensured that the next first disbursement date in the disbursement schedule should be after the current date.
E.g.
Loan tenure= 12 Months
Disbursement date= 10-May-2024
Approved amount= 1,000,000
Frequency=Monthly      
Number of Tranches= 12
Disbursement schedule is expected to be generated as below
Disbursement date
Disbursement Amount

83,334

83,334

83,334
…
10-Apr-2025
83,326
1,000,000 – 83334*11 = 83326

Reversal of Partial and Full Write-off <B2-044-4><B2-046-10>
CTBC requires the option to correct and perform reversal of a write off transaction performed on a loan account.
The reversal is required for the below scenarios with backdated effect,
Reversal of partial write-off done on a NPA account
Reversal of complete write-off done on a NPA account
Reversal of partial write-off done on an already partially written off loan account
Reversal of complete write-off done on a partially written off loan account
With the reversal, the account should return to its previous status of NPA or partial write off along with the generation of accounting entries to reverse the written off balances and restore the old bucket balances with up-to-date interest components. 
The backdated reversal should be allowed only till the last financial transaction date of the loan account.
That is for a loan, say, the complete write-off was done on 10-Sep-2023 and then a repayment was done on 15-Sep-2023. If a reversal of write-off is tried on 20-Sep-2023 then it should fail, and error should be returned.
The user will need to reverse the repayment done on 15-Sep-2023 and then perform the reversal of the full write-off.

Penal Interest Reserve/Suspense in Non-Performing Loan <B2-044-11>
CTBC needs the penal interest computed after marking the loan as NPA to be bucketed and shown in the penal interest reserve bucket. Till the date of NPA marking the penal interest should be shown in penal interest bucket. 
The penal interest for the period before marking the loan as NPA is computed on the fly and accounted on repayment.
The computation of daily penal interest post marking the account as NPA should be accrued daily and follow the below formula,
“Principal outstanding * debit interest rate * 1 / interest practice * Percentage”
At CTBC the debit interest rate itself is used as penal interest rate, so the same rate is used for debit interest and penal interest.
For example:
NPA marked date: 01-Feb-2024
Outstanding Principal: 1000000
Penal Rate/Debit Interest Rate: 3%
Interest Practice: Actual by 365
Period weights in percentage is as below,
Period
Percentage
Upto 6 months (or 180 days)
10
Above 6 months (or 180 days)
20
That is, first 6 months (or 180 days) from NPA marked date, penalty percentage = 10%
After 6 months (or 180 days), penalty percentage = 20%
So, after EOD of 1-Feb-2024, the Penalty Interest Reserve accrual for the day will be,
PI reserve = (1,000,000 * 3% * 1 / 365) * 10% = 8.21917
The PI reserve bucket should be accrued with the computed penalty interest amount.
Loan Debit Interest Reserve and Penal Interest Reserve Adjustment <B2-044-13><B2-046-7>
With the new Debit or Normal Interest Reserve and Penal Interest Reserve being accrued daily in a separate bucket, an option is required for CTBC to perform adjustments of these buckets in addition to the existing option to adjust the other buckets.
No accounting is required to be generated for the adjustments, as in EOD the next days accrual would compensate the same.
The adjustment transaction for the reserve balance should be allowed only for loan account which are in below condition as these only will have reserve balance.
Non-performing loan 
Partial write-off 
Complete write-off

If there is any change of loan status to like ‘Pending Closure’ from the original write-off transaction date till current date, then also the request should fail with the error ‘Reversal not allowed due to interim loan status change’.

In order to manually upgrade a NPL loan, the localized loan restructure RestAPI should be enhanced to have the following changes for its attributes,

The user should be able to do restructuring by giving the new term, rate, or installment.
Validation should be added that no interest due is outstanding for the loan. All the interest outstanding be it debit interest, penal interest, debit interest reserve or penal interest reserve should be either paid off or waived. The manual upgrade should be allowed only with outstanding in principal and fee buckets.
This restructuring with the new domain values should be allowed only for NPA loans else error should be returned as ‘Restructure with NPA upgrade allowed only for NPA loan’.
The loan outstanding excluding the charges should be crystallized as the new loan principal and for this basis the new term and rate the new installment should be arrived and the loan repayment schedule should be built basis the regeneration option given as per the current processing.

CTBC after marking a loan as NPA system moves the normal principal and normal debit interest GL balances from Standard asset to Substandard asset GL, further on write-off the Substandard asset GL’s and Charges (Legal and Insurance) are written off using the provisions. The penal interest, Debit Interest Reserve and Penal Interest Reserve GL balances are not changed.

Here only the balances of Non-performing Principal (NPL-P), Non-performing Interest (NPL-I), Legal fee (L bucket), Insurance (X bucket) are written-off. The penal interest, debit interest reserve and penal interest reserve accruals are not reversed, as no accounting are done for these buckets and these are not reflected in any GL’s, its only computed and kept and on cash basis its realized.

After the loan account is marked as NPA, interest reserve and penal interest reserve is accrued and increased on daily basis, this should continue even when the accounts are fully or partially written-off.
That is, the daily increment for debit interest reserve should be computed using the formula, “principal outstanding * debit interest rate * 1 / 365” and penal interest reserve using the formula “principal outstanding * debit interest rate * 1 / interest practice * Percentage”.
At CTBC the debit interest rate itself is used as penal interest rate, so the same rate is used for debit interest and penal interest. When the debit interest rate is set as 0 then a separate penal rate is set and used for penal interest computation.
The repayment in a written off account is required to appropriate the balances with a different appropriation sequence as set at the loan instrument/product level. This appropriation sequence can be different from the appropriation sequence of NPA and non-NPA standard loan.
This new repayment appropriation will be applicable to fully written off and partially written off loans. 
The written off loans repayment appropriation sequence should include the buckets of PI Reserve and Interest Reserve.
To comply with the regulation of Business Tax (Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax), if the written-off amount includes NPL-I along with the other buckets. Once there’s a recovery in the written-off accounts, the original “NPL-Interest” must be recorded individually, and accounting entry has to be generated accordingly. Thus, on write-off the NPL interest is moved as written off interest and similarly the principal and fee buckets. Including the new buckets there should be a separate appropriation sequence for written off loans.

Auto Debit for NPL/Partial Write Off/Full Write Off Loans <B2-046-8>
CTBC needs the auto debit processing to continue even after the loan is marked as non-performing or partially or fully written off. 
The collection is basis the loan product, where for retail the collection is done when loan is NPL or written off and for corporate its only when its NPL.
The auto debit should collect the amount which is lower of loan account’s discharge amount and CASA’s available balance amount. The auto debit when account is in write-off status should not do chasing, it should only collect the full due on the repay days only.
For example:
Case 1:
Loan account’s discharge amount= 1000
CASA’s available amount= 1500
Then auto debit amount will be 1000.
Case 2:
Loan account’s discharge amount= 1000
CASA’s available amount= 300
Then auto debit amount will be 300.
Case 3:
Loan account was written-off on May-01
Repay day = 20
The first auto debit processing will be performed on May-20
Next auto debit processing will be performed on Jun-20
Succeeding date will be July-20, Aug-20.
The auto debit amount will be the discharge amount.
Account Currency Change for NPL Loan on Full Write-off <B2-046-12>
CTBC wants to have the option to change the loan account currency to base currency only on full write-off of loan. 
A new flag should be added in write-off transaction which should be enabled only with full write-off option. If the flag is selected as “Yes”, then all loans dues must be converted to base currency with negotiated exchange rate. The negotiated exchange rate should be entered in the write-off transaction which should be used for converting the loan dues and buckets. If no rate is specified, the prevailing Mid-Rate should be used for exchange.
All loan dues and accrued interest/penal interest are required to be recomputed with exchange rate.
Loan accounts in DBU will be converted to TWD as base currency.
Loan accounts in OBU will be converted to USD as base currency.

The enhanced RestAPI ‘Manual Write-off of NPA Account‘ for write off should perform the currency switch to base currency before performing the write-off. The following steps should be done.
Step-1:
Validate, that if the ‘Switch to Base Currency’ is given as ‘Yes’ then 
Loan account currency should not be of base currency. (Else error – ‘Account already in base currency’)
Write-off request is for full write-off (partial-writeoff  = N) (Else error – ‘Allowed with full write-off only’)
Step-2:
After the enhanced validations are done, the following processing should be done,
Like the loan account currency change processing defined in ‘FS- TCS-BaNCS-User Story – B2-020 撥款_Loan Disbursement’ for the point ‘B2-020-14’, here also the loan account currency should be changed, but here the loan account will have balances in all buckets even the accruals with which the currency switching is to be done.
The loan account’s currency should be changed to the OU base currency as specified.
The account’s GL should be remapped to reflect the new currency.
All the bucket balances in the loan account should be updated basis the new currency after converting the balance using the prevailing mid-rate to base currency.
If the exchange rate is input by the user, then that rate should be used to arrive at the converted amount in the new currency.
Balance transfer GL entries should be generated for the change of account’s old currency balance to the new currency balance in the similar lines as done in ‘FS- TCS-BaNCS-User Story – B2-020 撥款_Loan Disbursement’ for the point ‘B2-020-14’. Here it is required for all the bucket balances transfer and there it was given only for the principal.
For the buckets where there is no GL balance tagged, like the ‘penal interest’, ‘debit interest reserve’ and ‘penal interest reserve’, only the bucket fields should be updated with the converted balances and no balance transfer accounting entries are to be fired.
With the new currency balance at the account, it’s linked facilities utilization should be revalued using mid-rate between old currency to new currency using triangulation method.
The currency change for the loan should be listed in the new enquiry (covered as per of FS- ‘TCS-BaNCS-User Story – B2-020 撥款_Loan Disbursement’ point ‘B2-020-14’) with the additional details of,
Loan Account Number
Date of transaction
From currency (Old currency code of the loan)
To currency (New currency code of the loan)
Principal (NPL-P) (Old currency balance and new currency balance)
Interest (NPL-I) (Old currency balance and new currency balance if present)
Penal interest (Old currency balance and new currency balance if present)
Legal fee  (Old currency balance and new currency balance if present)
Insurance fee (Old currency balance and new currency balance if present)
Interest Reserve (Old currency balance and new currency balance if present)
Penal Interest Reserve (Old currency balance and new currency balance if present)
Step-3:
After the account currency is changed, the enhanced full write-off processing should be done. Failure in write-off processing should revert the loan accounts base currency conversion also.

Business Requirement 
Loan Account Repay Day Change Impact <B2-047-1>
CTBC requires to have the loan term unchanged and change the installment when the loan accounts repayment day is changed. 
Also, it wants the last installment to fall on the original maturity date irrespective of when the new installment dates are generated basis the new repay day.
Sample cases are given in the embedded excel spreadsheet for reference.
Here with the change in repay day the count of total installments may become more than or less than the original number of installments, but the last installment date will be always the original maturity date.
Also, the last installment derived can be more than or less than the regular equated installments being stamped, as the last installment should have the remaining amount for the loan to be settled.
Samples for these are in the embedded excel sheet given as individual cases.
Solution Analysis
Solution Analysis for B2-047 Others
Existing Functionality 
GBP supports the repay day change and rebuilding of repayment schedule.
The current RestAPIs to change repay day are as given below,

The above list is as per the current API catalogue which will get further enhanced basis the updated catalogues.
Proposed Solution
Below changes are to be developed whenever there is a change in repay day for a loan as detailed in section 2.1 above.
Loan Account Repay Day Change Impact <B2-047-1>
CTBC for its loans with installment type as “EI-Equated Monthly Installment” and “Equal-Equated Principal Installment” wants to have special treatment when the repay day is changed for rebuilding the repayment schedule. It wants the loan duration to be unchanged, that is the loan maturity date should remain the same and change the installment amount. 
Thus, the last installment should fall on the original maturity date irrespective of when the new installment dates are generated basis the new repay day. 
The change of repay day is done via the ‘Reschedule Loan’ RestAPI. The field ‘regeneration-option’ having the domain ‘d_EIRegenOption’ in the ‘Reschedule Loan’ RestAPI has the new domain value ‘06: Installment Change Basis Original Maturity Date’ added as part of the FS- NVBK_B2-029_貸後作業管理_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分). The domain value of 06 should be further enhanced to process the repay day change request in rescheduling to have the loan total period unchanged and change the EMI amount and have the last installment to fall on the original maturity date irrespective of when the new installment dates are generated basis the new repay day. 
With the change of repay day using this new ‘06’ domain value the number of remaining repayments can increase or decrease from the original agreed number of installment payments.
The last installment should cover the remaining loan amount which need not be equal to the new installment amount as generated.
Detailed samples of repayment schedule changes in different scenarios are given in section 2.1 above in an embedded excel worksheet.

Business Requirement 
Enhanced Validation for Pre-closure/Prepayment
Enhancement is required to add new validations in the following transactions
Pre-closure
Pre-closure enquiry
Prepayment
Prepayment enquiry
New validation for Pre-closure/Pre-closure enquiry
For CTBC, for some of their loan products its accounts cannot be discharged until its Debt Management Department completes all their internal processes.
For this, CTBC wants a new flag, say ‘Authorized closure flag’ at loan account level, which is to be set as Yes to close the loan else closure should not be allowed.
The Initial value will be space on loan creation which can be set as No by user or through a file interface via SI. 
For the loan eligible for closure after its required internal processes are completed it will be set as Yes by the CTBC users.
The field is allowed to be set as Yes only by the users of Debt Management Department at CTBC, so for GBP this should be allowed to be modified only when the modification is done via channel = ‘CTCPFORM’ or via SI. The channel ‘CTCPFORM’ stands for an external system which is used by Debt Management Department
If this field = No, then pre-closure or pre-closure enquiry must return error until this field is modified as Yes.
Any modification to this field is required to be recorded in the audit log for future reference.
Enhancement of retention process for Prepayment/Prepayment enquiry/Pre-closure/Pre-closure enquiry
CTBC wants to enhance the customized retention validations and processes of the 1.3 FS’s for B2-026 and B2-028 (NVBK_B2-026_提前還本_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99 and NVBK_B2-028_結清_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99).
New conditions are required to be added in the retention process. An additional processing is to be added to check 2 fields (Rating Agency, Rating) at CIF level. These two fields for CIF are covered in 1.3 FS of B31-016.
If ‘Rating Agency’ = ”CRRB” and ‘Rating’ = 17 or 18 or 19 or 20 or 95 for the loan accounts primary borrower, then the retention processing and validation is to be skipped and the transactions of Prepayment, Prepayment enquiry, Pre-closure and Pre-closure enquiry should continue unconditionally and proceed with the transaction processing.
Simulation Enquiry for Retention Processing Validation for Prepayment and Pre-closure
CTBC requires simulate enquiry to see the result of the validations done during stamping of retention for the below customized functions covered in the 1.3 FS’s of B2-026 and B2-028.
‘Pre-closure Request with Retention’ covered in 1.3 FS’s NVBK_B2-028_結清_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99.
‘Prepayment Request with Retention’ covered in 1.3 FS’s NVBK_B2-026_提前還本_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99.
The simulate function required for CTBC for the above transaction is to evaluate and show if the loan account is eligible for pre-closure and prepayment. The step-by-step process for evaluation is given below. 
Output field
Expected step-by-step process
Pre-closure allowed flag
Step-1:
If ‘Authorized closure flag’ = “N” then return “No” and no next step
Step-2:
If one of the below conditions is met, then return “Yes” and no next step
<1> If the loan is under debt negotiation plan
   Note: This one should be added as part of the retention process.
<2> ‘Rating agency’ = CRRB and ‘Rating’ = 17/18/19/20/95
<3> NPA or written-off 
<4> Outstanding principal <= ‘Minimum Pre-closure Amount’
<5> Remaining instalments <= ‘Pre-closure Allowed Term’
Step-3:
 If ‘Prepayment/Pre-Closure Retention Applicable’ is not captured or equal to “1-Prepayment” then return “Yes” and no next step
Step-4: 
If ‘Prepayment/ Pre-Closure Retention Applicable’ is equal to “2-Pre-Closure” or ”3-Prepayment and Pre-Closure”
  If one of the below conditions is met, then return “No” and no next step
<1> If ‘Pre-closure Retention Period Set’ = “2-No”
<2> If ‘Pre-closure Retention Period Set’ = “1-Yes” and system date is greater than ‘Pre-closure Retention Period End Date’ 
<3> Remaining instalments > Loan tenor * Pre-closure Allowed Term Percentage (always rounded up)
Step-5: 
Return “Yes”
Prepayment allowed flag
Step-1: 
If one of the below conditions is met, then return “Yes” and no next step
<1> If the loan is under debt negotiation plan
<2> ‘Rating agency’ = CRRB and ‘Rating’ = 17/18/19/20/95
<3> NPA or written-off 
<4> Above calculated ‘Pre-closure allowed flag’ = “Yes”
    Note: This one should be added as part of the retention process.
Step-2:
 If ‘Prepayment/Pre-Closure Retention Applicable’ is not captured or equal to “2-Pre-Closure” then return “Yes” and no next step
Step-3: 
If ‘Prepayment/ Pre-Closure Retention Applicable’ is equal to “1-Prepayment” or ”3-Prepayment and Pre-Closure”
  If one of the below conditions is met, then return “Yes” and no next step
<1> If ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set’ = “3-Indefinite Period”
<2> If ‘Prepayment Retention Period Set’ = “1-Yes” and system date is not greater than ‘Prepayment Retention Period End Date’ 
Step-4: 
Return “No”
The enhanced loan preclosure RestAPI ‘CLM-77 - Create Early Settlement Request’ covered in 1.3 FS’s NVBK_B2-028 with threshold validations should be further enhanced to skip the threshold validations and continue the transaction, if the account is under debt negotiation plan.
The ‘Prepayment Request with Retention’ stamping covered in 1.3 FS’s NVBK_B2-026 should be enhanced to also validate if the above new ‘Pre-closure allowed flag’ is Yes then skip the threshold validations. 
Enhancement in Product Switch for Retention Processing.
CTBC requires to skip the retention processing for its certain corporate loans/employee loans for prepayment and preclosure. 
The current loan parameter “Prepayment/Pre-Closure Retention Applicable” added as part of 1.3 FS’s of B2-026 and B2-028 is to be enhanced to have a new parameter value to skip the retention processing and directly allow the prepayment or pre-closure transactions.

Pre-closure Retention Validation Processing for Overdraft
As part of 1.3 FS-NVBK_B2-035_透支型融資_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分)_v0.99 for closure of an overdraft loan account, the below retention and closure flags should be “Yes” if retention processing is set for the OD loan accounts product.
Pre-closure Retention Period Set
Overdraft Closure Indicator
This same validation to check the flags of "Pre-closure Retention Period Set" and "Overdraft Closure Indicator" to be ‘Yes’ is required in the OD Full Closure batch (introduced in the 1.3 FS of B2-035) to change the overdraft loan account status from ‘In Provisional Closure’ to ‘Closed’.
In addition to this CTBC wants to have the check if for the OD loan product, 
If Prepayment/Pre-Closure Retention Applicable at product level = “3-Prepayment and Pre-closure” or "2-Pre-closure" 
then when user sets the ‘Overdraft closure indicator’ at account level as “Yes”, system should validate that the ‘Pre-closure Retention Period Set’ is set as “Yes” and ‘Pre-closure Retention Period End Date’ is stamped.
For example, say,
At the Overdraft loan product level, the,
“Prepayment/Pre-Closure Retention Applicable” at product level = “3-Prepayment and Pre-closure”
On 10th December 2024,
When teller tries to modify the ‘Overdraft closure indicator’ as Yes for an OD loan account with ‘Pre-closure Retention Period Set’ not set then error should be returned.
Thereafter after agreement with the customer the ‘Pre-Closure Retention Period Set’ is set as “Yes” and ‘Pre-Closure Retention Period End Date’ as 20th December 2024.
Now the teller should be able to set the ‘Overdraft closure indicator’ as Yes. 
Once set the OD Closure BOD batch will keep trying to close/discharge the OD loan account and on 20th December 2024 EOD the ‘Pre-closure Retention Period Set’ will be reset as ‘2-No’.
From 21st December 2024 in BOD the OD loan account closure should be skipped as ‘Pre-closure Retention Period Set’ is ‘2-No’.
Enhancement in ACH Processing <CR-B2-025-15>
CTBC requires to have additional customizations on the localized and customized ACH processing.
Audit log for ACH Mandate Records
CTBC wants to have an audit log for the ACH mandate modification, the ACH status change (online/batch) must be included.
Enhancement in Termination of eDDA-ACH Mandate and its Extraction
CTBC wants the option to terminate its ACH Mandates with its payment method as eDDA and its ACH Status in “Approved Success” status. 
In CTBC, it is done for eDDA-ACH and the “ACH Mandate Termination“ request comes from external system.
It also happens that on the same day of terminating an existing mandate record, the new mandate record is applied with same ‘Bank Code of External Bank‘ and ‘Settlement account number’ as in the ACH master.
In such cases when there are two records for same loan account for same application date then the record with status ‘Apply’ should be extracted into the ACHP02 file.
For example,
Consider the scenario as on 2024-12-23 if there are two mandate records in the ACH master for same loan account as below for ACH Batch Job 1 to process:

Enhancement in Deletion of eDDA-ACH Mandate
CTBC wants the option to delete its ACH Mandates via SI for the mandates with its payment method as eDDA and in “Document Confirmed” status.
Enhancement in Retry based on Failure Counter
CTBC requires the retry of ACH mandate only for the RCODE=01. With the current samples as listed below,
ACH Return Code    Threshold Count

When RCODE = ‘01’,
For the same installment period, system to request another “auto debit” on the next day if first attempt is failed with return code “01”. If that also fails, then the next “auto debit” will be extracted in next installment period provided the threshold count of 4 is not reached.
When RCODE <> ‘01’,
For the same installment period, system should not request another “auto debit” on the next day. Thereafter the next “auto debit” will be extracted in next installment period provided the threshold count for the RCODE is not reached.
In the case of “99”, its threshold count = 2
For example:
Current installment due date = 2025-May-10
If the first attempt for 2025-May-10 is failed, then the next extraction for “auto debit” will be on 2025-Jun-10 provided the failure count for the account is <2.
Enhancement in Batch Job 4 processing the ACHR01 file and updating ACH Repayment Records
Basis the localization and customization, the batch job 4 processes the input file ACHR01 and each record is written in a new table (ACH repayment records) irrespective of success/failure (R-RCODE). 
CTBC wants this to be enhanced to do the additional processing to compare the ‘R-RBANK’/’R-RCLNO’ in ACHR01 with ‘Bank Code of External Bank‘/‘Settlement account number’ in up-to-date mandate record(ACH repayment records), if it’s the same then stamp as “Yes” otherwise “No” in a new field in the ACH repayment records and this new filed should be available to be enquired as part of ‘ACH Repayment Records Inquiry’.
Enhancement in Batch Job 4 processing of the ACHR01 file in updating the customized failure counter
With the enhancement of the new field as per the point 3 above the batch job 4 should be further enhanced to update the failure counter introduced as part of 1.3 FS of B2- NVBK_B2-025_還款銷帳順序_客製化業務功能規格書(針對差異部分) in gap reference B2-025-15.
If the new field is marked as “No” then
Failure counter must be reset to 0
“Terminated by CTBC” must not be triggered on failure
Retry on failure should not be done for the RCODE with threshold greater than 1(e.g. RCODE=1)
Enhancement of Closure Enquiry
CTBC requires to have an additional field in the closure enquiries (CLM-83 and CLM-199) to show the total of all the debit interest’s values as listed below in a loan account.
Unpaid Debit Interest including
Debit Interest adjustments to be paid
Deferred Interest
Delayed Debit Interest (Due to delayed due adjustments for reverse mortgage interest thresholds)
Up to date Debit Interest Accrued including Debit Interest Reserve
Up to date Penal Interest on Principal arrears
Up to date Penal Interest on Interest arrears
Up to date Penal Interest Reserve
Up to date Deferred Interest

Enhancement in ACH Processing<CR-B2-025-15>
The following enhancements are required in the ACH processing.
Audit log for ACH Mandate Records
CTBC wants to have an audit log for the ACH mandate modification of the ACH status change in online or batch. 
With every ACH status change of the mandate record in ACH master the ACH master record should be copied and rewritten using a new sequence number. 
As per current processing only when the existing ACH mandate record becomes 'deleted' or 'terminated' or 'approve failed', a row is recorded with new sequence number. This should be enhanced to record even if the change is from 'Apply' to 'Awaiting approval', or 'Awaiting approval' to 'approve success'. Enhancement in Retry based on Failure Counter
The current retry function basis RCODE value should follow as below on return of ACH repay record,
When RCODE = ‘01’,
For the same installment period, system should request another “auto debit” on the next day if first attempt is failed with return code “01”. If that also fails, then the next “auto debit” should be extracted in next installment period provided the threshold count of 4(value set in parameter as per 1.3-FS-B2-025) is not reached.
When RCODE <> ‘01’,
For the same installment period, system should not request another “auto debit” on the next day. Thereafter the next “auto debit” should be extracted in next installment period provided the threshold count for the RCODE is not reached.
